title: Cert red: QEMU desktop smoke session outgrew its fixed 90 s wall deadline (8fab6e40)
description:
End-of-day make cert on 9dd62fe6 failed image-smoke at the QEMU desktop session: '--quit-after marker FLAIR-LIVE-READY not seen before requested wall deadline (expired)'. It is not a guest fault. The serial (1,030,334 bytes) runs the whole journey to FLAIR-EXIT-TO-DOS, types 'flair' at A:\>, and prints the second FLAIR-LIVE-READY, all just after the 90 s ceiling. keys_sent=0 and mouse_events_sent=0 appear because the counts are not reported once the session has failed.

Mechanism: factory/smoke-desktop.sh:57 passes --timeout-ms ${DESKTOP_SMOKE_TIMEOUT_MS:-90000} to a single QEMU boot that replays every journey. 8fab6e40 (Finder commands and Word modal-key omissions) adds 66 lines to apps/initechword/tests/smoke/journey.sh, which takes the QEMU trace from 55 to 96 W markers. Session wall time, measured as the qemu.stdout to qemu.serial mtime with a 300 s ceiling at load 3.2-4.2 (12 cores):
  aba1918d 67.2 s | e6a64b1c 68.0 | 16e1a446 71.5 (in-order W waits, +3.5 s) | 7d31fe34 67.3 | 8fab6e40 89.9 (green), and an earlier run of it stalled 20 s at the W marker 'FINDER-INFO Name: WORD.EXE' (once in two runs) | 23a76e97 92.9 | e7f0a018 92.9 | 9dd62fe6 93.8 | origin/main da8f453e 94.2.
With the default ceiling, da8f453e is red with the same error (session 94.2 s). With DESKTOP_SMOKE_TIMEOUT_MS=180000 it is green at load 6.35 (session 92.8 s, 11 checks, 0 failures).

Not reverted. git revert 8fab6e40 applies textually, but it would remove an approved GM4/GM6 feature (the Finder command split and Word modal keys) to satisfy a wall ceiling, and the journey growth is legitimate. Proposed fix-forward for the factory holder: raise the QEMU desktop session default in factory/smoke-desktop.sh:57 to 180000 (or derive it per journey), keeping the idle budget as the hang detector. Separately, check the 'FINDER-INFO Name: WORD.EXE' W stall seen once at 8fab6e40. Report: phase2/bisect-cert-desktop.md.
close_reason: QEMU desktop deadline sized from measurement (180000 ms, README), 09230b74

title: QEMU harness truncates oversized input specs instead of failing; desktop session exceeds buffer
description:
factory/emu/qemu.c:1391-1398 at d7773ea3 (qmp_inject_mouse): char buf[4096] silently limits the event stream to 4095 bytes after a stderr warning, then injects that prefix. qmp_inject_keys has the same truncation policy. This must reject oversize input before launching/injecting (or use an input-sized allocation and fail on allocation error), never grade a prefix as the requested scenario. Add independent boundary tests at 4095/4096 and a deliberately wrong/failing suffix that cannot disappear into a false pass.

Observed regression: sentinel full smoke GREEN da31e926, RED 37a03086. Desktop composes all journeys and absolute capture filenames into one --mouse spec. d7773ea3 changes the default output from relative build/smoke-desktop to $PWD/build/smoke-desktop/run.XXXXXX, repeated in every capture token. With the sentinel worktree output path, the trace is 6043 bytes already at d7773ea3, rising to 6725 at 37a03086. With the relative pre-d777 output those revisions are 3883 and 4565 respectively (coordinates from installed APPS listing). Exact emulator bisect is in progress.

Sentinel report: [harness] --mouse spec too long (max 4095); truncating; --quit-after marker FLAIR-LIVE-READY not seen before requested wall deadline (expired); keys_sent=0 mouse_events_sent=0. The zero counts are misleading on injector error: serial shows 123, Word, Calculator and Note Pad actually launched.

Reproduce: checkout d7773ea3, nice make -j2 image, DESKTOP_SMOKE_TIMEOUT_MS=150000 sh factory/smoke-desktop.sh from a long absolute worktree path. A temporary DESKTOP_SMOKE_OUT=build/smoke-desktop may avoid the path contribution at this revision; later journeys alone exceed even the relative-path limit. Fix must both preserve all input or fail immediately, and allow the complete registered session to run. Small-app shortening cannot remove the path overhead contributed by other components.

Evidence: /tmp/bisect-desktop-smoke/trace-lengths-relative.txt, trace-lengths-worktree.txt, trace-lengths.txt. title: InitechBase APPEND FROM reports success after an index fault and imports a blank row
description:
Post-landing review at origin/main 222e144ca748cdbf38044cc82ff557cfc007b1e5. No product edit.

apps/initechbase/cmd/mutate.c:1371 converts m_append's negative return to rc=*ec. Incremental index insertion failures in m_append at :724 set *ec=0. APPEND FROM therefore breaks its input loop with rc=0 and reports success after committing only a blank row, never importing any source field. This is error propagation in addition to the publication hole tracked as initech-9sued.

Reproducer: sh /tmp/review-landed-word-base/link-appendfrom.sh (exit 1 for independent failures). It links unchanged landed objects, opens a copy of genuine 49-record CLIENTS.DBF with CNAMES.NDX attached, and independently sets a source copy's DBF count to one. Source record 1 is Claire Buckman. Inject -PAL_EIO at PAL write 12 of APPEND FROM SOURCE.DBF, the first incremental index stage write after the blank append. Product returns rc=0 (success) and ROW.DBF now has 50 records with record 50 entirely blank, instead of Claire Buckman. Final no-fault controls return success with the complete source record.

Evidence: /tmp/review-landed-word-base/base-appendfrom.c, link-appendfrom.sh, base-appendfrom.log and base-work/AFROM-{FAIL,OK}.DBF. Independent dbf_ref.py --records confirms the failed-success file's last record is blank while the positive file has Claire/Buckman; the raw expected last record is copied directly from the genuine source bytes, not produced by a codec. ndx_ref.py independently reads AFROM-FAIL.NDX. The same false-success path occurs at other single write and metadata boundaries.

Propagate a nonzero error when m_append fails even without a populated catalog code; retain/recover the incomplete record and indexes as required by initech-9sued. Add a one-source-record command test requiring both successful content and an actual failure diagnostic, not just rc==0 or a DBF count increment. Earlier completed source records may remain committed; this reproduction fails within the first record and makes no batch rollback demand.

title: Bochs final verdict ignores abnormal emulator exit and termination signals
description:
factory/emu/bochs.c:617-625 bochs_verdict() checks markers, timeout and a narrow triple-fault scan but never checks exit_code, term_signal, or successful reaping. :999-1006 records exit status, then :1065 ignores it. If Bochs aborts/segfaults/exits nonzero after writing required markers with keys consumed, the harness can return OK=1. A partial completed session plus an emulator failure is accepted. This is distinct from fixed initech-5e3wu timeout handling.

Deterministic reproduction: sh /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2/review-factory-evidence/bochs-exit.sh <repo-root> <fresh-scratch>. C probe includes the actual driver and calls its final predicate using complete markers/input: exit_code=3 => OK=1; term_signal=SIGSEGV => OK=1. Timely harness SIGTERM => OK=1; timed_out=true => OK=0. Audited a49afccd7555dca0bdc4db980486fa528ef4aefd. No live emulator crash injected, so evidence is at the actual verdict boundary rather than an end-to-end crash.

Fix: track whether the harness intentionally requested shutdown after completed work, require successful reap and an allowed exit/signal for that path, reject spontaneous nonzero exits/signals. Do not break intentional SIGTERM. Extend bochs-verdict test with abnormal exit, SIGSEGV, SIGKILL/reap failure and valid intentional-shutdown controls.

title: Even strict certificate returns success while mutation coverage is pending
description:

title: Shared mutation runner counts timeout and startup errors as semantic kills
description:
factory/testlib/run-mutants.sh:40-46 discards test-run exit status and reduces every '  FAIL  <test>' line to its name. factory/testlib/run-test.sh:22 emits the same prefix for assertion failures, GNU timeout exit 124, and command/setup exit 127. Two identical infrastructure failures therefore kill a correct mutant. The outer factory/mutants.sh checks counts, not the underlying cause, so a full cert can accept fabricated kill coverage.

Reproducer: sh /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2/review-factory-evidence/shared-kill.sh <repo-root> <fresh-scratch>. Uses actual mk/host-test.mk and run-test.sh with a C program returning 0 and a comment-only patch. A PATH timeout substitute delegates the real baseline then injects exits 124 and 127. Both runs exit 0 and report 'fixture: 1 mutants, 1 killed, 0 survived, 0 errors'; mutation-summary.awk accepts 1 1 0 0. With no injection the same patch survives and runner exits 1. Observed at a49afccd7555dca0bdc4db980486fa528ef4aefd; no factory files edited.

Fix: preserve per-test outcome classification, distinguish completed assertions from timeout/startup/setup/build errors, require matching semantic failures twice, and count infrastructure failures as errors. DOS's tests/runtime/{verdict,classify}.sh now demonstrates that protocol. The shared runner feeds mk/mutants.mk, FLAIR and InitechBase grouped runners. Acceptance: comment-only patch never killed by exits 124/126/127, signal, missing runner, or emulator startup error; real assertion mutant still killed.

title: InitechWord failed replacement move discards the preceding destination
description:
Post-landing review at origin/main 222e144ca748cdbf38044cc82ff557cfc007b1e5. No product edit. Main document Save is sound in the reviewed matrix; this is a separate existing List Files write path.

title: InitechBase torn DBT high-water write makes existing memos unreadable
description:
Independent pre-landing review of t3/initechbase-write-safety-checks at 9d214ebd. fs/dbt.c is unchanged by the branch; no branch edit was made.

apps/initechbase/fs/dbt.c:226 writes next_free in place. dbt_append advances it at :442 and writes the new four-byte value at :447 without restoring a short write. A failed memo replacement (fs/dbf.c:1712) can therefore invalidate all existing memos even though the original DBF pointer is preserved.

Reproduced with a valid 255-block DBT, next_free=255, and an existing terminated 'old memo' in block 1. It reads successfully before the failure. Append 'new', permitting text, terminator and padding, but writing only one byte of the final next_free update (255=>256). dbt_append returns -1; after close/reopen next_free is zero and dbt_read(block 1) returns -5. Old memo bytes still exist but are no longer readable through the file's high-water mark. Byte 0 changes from ff to 00 with the higher bytes still zero. This violates the operator's preservation ruling; no real dBASE failure behavior is inferred.

Reproducer: /tmp/review-initechbase-evidence/codecs.c with link-codecs.sh, compiled against unchanged branch objects. Evidence: codecs.log, BEFORE.DBT, AFTER.DBT. Both geometry and expected old value are independently authored from the DBT format, not calculated by the product.

Preserve the previous header on reported append/flush failure without relying on a second media write succeeding. Add a 255=>256 boundary and persistent-error control. dbt_create is also destructive for existing files on the DOS PAL, but has no current product caller; qualify it if it becomes reachable.

title: InitechBase cannot REINDEX after an external writer removes an indexed record
description:
InitechBase cannot REINDEX after an external writer removes an indexed record

P0. apps/initechbase/cmd/nav.c:192 allocates an index sequence only as large as the current DBF record count; collect_visit (:142) rejects the stale third index entry when the DBF has two rows. apps/initechbase/ibase_main.c:389 consequently returns error 114 on USE. REINDEX at cmd/mutate.c:1072 calls d_key (:1056), which calls wa_nav_goto; cmd/nav.c:339 insists on rebuilding the same invalid old index sequence while trying to read physical records, so the repair fails too.

C21: syntactically valid OLD.NDX indexes AAAAAAAA->1, BBBBBBBB->2, CCCCCCCC->3. BASE.DBF was externally shortened to two records, with correct count/length/EOF; its two records are intact. USE BASE INDEX OLD; LIST OFF; GO BOTTOM; SEEK 'AAAAAAAA'; REINDEX; GO BOTTOM; REPLACE VALUE WITH 9; close/copy.

Real III+ lists the two available rows, GO BOTTOM raises EOF error 4 for stale recno 3, SEEK finds recno 1, REINDEX succeeds, AFTER 2 BBBBBBBB; saved row 2 VALUE=9 and independent NDX readback has only records 1,2.
InitechBase errors 114 during USE and REINDEX, reports SEEK .F. recno3, AFTER 1 AAAAAAAA; OLD.NDX remains stale and row 1 is updated instead. The user can work around it by closing the index; the normal repair command should work. P0: after the reported repair/navigation errors the ON ERROR handler resumes, and the final REPLACE overwrites the unrelated intact row 1 value (1 becomes 9) instead of the last actual row 2. This is a concrete wrong-record write, not a claim of table-structure loss or silent error-free execution.

Fixtures/reference/host observations under tests/conformance/{cases,reference,observed}/C21 on branch t3/initechbase-file-format-conformance. Run conformance/build.sh, run-host.sh, check.sh. Capture recipe CASES=C21 sh apps/initechbase/tests/conformance/capture.sh /absolute/empty/output (real DOS 3.30 + dBASE III PLUS 1.1, QEMU 486/8MiB).

title: CREATE_NEW truncates an existing file after a transient lookup read error
description:
Reviewed main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. P0 data loss, real shipped INT21/FAT stack.

kernel/int21.c:2688-2691 treats every nonzero existence-probe result as absence. kernel/fileio_fat.c:129-132 maps directory read errors to FILE_NOT_FOUND. A one-shot read error during AH=5Bh's probe of an EXISTING writable TARGET.BIN is followed by a healthy truncating create. AH=5Bh returns CF=0/AX=5 and the old 19-byte document is now zero bytes, clusters freed. No directory write error is involved. This is distinct from initech-rg6d5: the exclusive operation reports success and should NEVER attempt a truncate.

Reference: IBM DOS 3.30 Technical Reference printed p.6-215: 5Bh fails if the filename already exists. mtools independently confirms file bytes/size before and after.

Reproducer retained in reports/phase2/kernel-repro/ under /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/. Build dos_probe.c with the real kernel int21/devices/fileio_fat/fat12/sft/psp/mcb/irq sources and tests/disk/blockdev_file.c (build.sh records the command). run-dos.sh creates good TARGET.BIN with mtools. Run dos-probe new-1.img new 1 on a fresh copy: call 5b00 -> CF=0 AX=5; read_fault=1. mdir shows 0 bytes. Control new 0 -> CF=1 AX=80 and 19 bytes preserved.

Required property: only proven absence authorizes exclusive creation; a failed existence check must preserve the existing name and bytes. Distinguish lookup I/O errors from absence throughout the backend.

title: InitechDOS failed delete or create can free the original file's clusters
description:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: kernel/
Source findings: review-dataloss.md #1
Reports: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports
Evidence checked by reading the current tree. No make, emulator, mutation or test run was performed during this triage. Reported earlier experiments are attributed, not repeated.

## Evidence
kernel/fat12.c:2497-2506 frees and flushes the old chain before the fallible directory write at :2549-2552; unlink repeats this at :3130-3145. sdk/include/tbx_save.h:131-134 deletes the completed save temporary when target deletion reports an error.

## Failing scenario
A one-shot directory-sector write failure after successful FAT writes leaves OLD.TXT naming a now-free cluster. Later allocation overwrites it. A replacing Toolbox save can also discard the complete replacement. Static ordering confirmed; the report's external fsck probe is supporting evidence, not a fresh run.

## Source of truth
FAT allocation invariant: every cluster referenced by a live nonempty file must remain allocated to that file. CLAUDE.md, The constitution / The oracle is the truth. Exact failed-operation parity with DOS needs ground truth captured first.

## Proposed fix
Preserve a valid old/new allocation and discoverable file across recoverable create/unlink errors; coordinate save cleanup with sdk/.

## Red-first test and acceptance
Inject failure at each FAT-copy and directory write in create/unlink; independently inspect names, bytes, FAT copies and allocation ownership with mtools/fsck. Repeat through tbx_file_save, exit/reopen, and require a complete discoverable version.

## Ground truth or decision needed
What guarantee applies after persistent I/O failure or interruption, and how is a surviving replacement exposed?

## Coordination
sdk/ is shared; coordinate with initech-vtl9.

title: Execute complete batch files or reject an oversized script before execution
description: Root cause: os/milton/command.c:4212 caps the shared batch buffer at 4096 bytes; batch_load_file at :4375 silently stops at the cap and returns a normal length at :4396. run_batch at :4614 interprets the prefix as a complete file, so the final commands disappear without an error. Ground truth: pubs/manuals/initechdos-reference/ch4-batch.tex:19-25 promises sequential execution; CLAUDE.md Rule 2 forbids silently incomplete success. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend a C execution/PAL oracle at lengths 4095/4096/4097 and the BIG.BAT length, with split lines, labels and CALL reloads crossing the boundary. QEMU B063 must execute BIG-END then BIG-RETURNED, or reject the whole oversized file visibly before BIG-BEGIN. Mutant: restore silent 4096-byte truncation; the final sentinel or reject-before-side-effects assertion must fail. Scope: A streaming/re-reading interpreter is preferable for full compatibility; an explicit all-or-nothing size refusal is the bounded safety fix. Merely raising the constant leaves the defect at the next boundary. Audit evidence: docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/shots/suite4-B063-batch-long.png; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite4-B063.txt; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/BIG.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/cases/B063.BAT; docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/evidence/suite.py. (Audit docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/REPORT.md L005; triage docs/audits/2026-10-23-dos/TRIAGE.md)

Same path, case alias and qualified alias must refuse without changing bytes; inject read/write/full-disk/cancel/final-commit failures and independently read old/new files. Include stage retention after uncertainty.

Capture the DOS output/name/byte contract, then implement the observed cleanup and message behavior.

title: Scrollbar column of a Finder disk window is inDrag: clicking arrows/track drags the whole window; scrollbars are chrome-only, no scroll state
description:
AUDIT F02 (docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/REPORT.md, section F02). Reviewer steps: in the root create 18 folders (File>New Folder + Ctrl-N, 22 entries total); click vertical down arrow (367,251) x3, up arrow (367,89), press Page Down; drag the track from (367,160) to (367,240).
SEEN: lower rows clipped; arrows and Page Down changed nothing; arrow clicks logged zero-distance FLAIR-DRAG; track drag moved the root window (20,60)->(20,140) (serial FLAIR-DRAG win 0 (20,60)->(20,140)). No thumb or position indication.
EXPECTED: arrows step, track pages, thumb drags, window never moves. Screenshots: docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/shots/50-overflow-folder.png, 51-scroll-down.png, 53-page-down.png, 55-scrollbar-drags-window.png.
ROOT CAUSE (triage, read from source): the scrollbar column lies in strucRgn but outside contRgn (CalcDocContentRect, os/flair/window.c:176-190 subtracts FLAIR_CHROME_SCROLLBAR_W), so FindWindow (window.c:956-1022) falls through to its last line 'any other chrome pixel is the drag region' and returns inDrag; kmain.c:4442 then runs flair_live_do_drag. There is NO scroll state and no ControlRecord for Finder windows: the bar is drawn by chrome.c:554-596/834-845 (thumb explicitly deferred, chrome.c:551), and finder_windows.h:183 states scrolling is DEFERRED; grid layout stacks overflow on the last row. Fix: (a) FindWindow/pump must route scrollbar hits to a control/scroll tracker, never inDrag; (b) Finder view needs a scroll offset applied in finder_win_paint, hit-test, drag clamp and grid origin. Shares work with initech-tdnl.4 (live scrollbars) - this bug is the P0 stop-the-bleeding slice: minimum acceptable interim is that a scrollbar click never moves the window and, until tdnl.4 lands, the bar draws as inactive/empty when nothing overflows. Files: os/flair/window.c (FindWindow part code), chrome.c, control.c, finder_windows.c/.h, finder_desktop.c (paint/hit offset), kmain.c pump arms ~4442. OVERLAPS 34dh area (finder_desktop.c hit/clamp, kmain flair_live_do_surface).

DONE MEANS: (1) a host oracle for the logic plus a named mutant proven RED (Rule 6); (2) an emulator gate driven by a locked injected input trace on the booted image, asserting the serial markers and a pixel probe; (3) a recorded clip via record-flair (build/clips/<script>.{gif,mp4}, repro-proven) that the operator eyeballs (CLAUDE.md Rule 14 - a window feature with no clip is not done); (4) test-flair-* tri-emulator legs stay green (QEMU + Bochs). title: region_op: per-band xmerge scratch[RGN_ROW_X_MAX=256] too small — silent stack buffer overflow when na+nb > 256
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R3 2026-06-28, wf_a2a0042d, adversarially verified] subsystem=FLAIR/region (os/flair/atkinson/region.c).
EVIDENCE: region.c:425 `int16_t scratch[RGN_ROW_X_MAX]` (256) is passed to xmerge at region.c:451; xmerge writes `out[no++]=x` (region.c:391-395) with no bound on `no`. region_normalize caps each input row to 256 entries, so an XOR/merge of two maximally-dense rows yields no<=na+nb<=512, overrunning the 256-slot stack buffer. The scratch needs 2*RGN_ROW_X_MAX, not RGN_ROW_X_MAX.

EXPECTED: scratch sized for na+nb (>=512), or xmerge checks `if (no >= cap) fail-loud` before each write.

ACTUAL: xmerge writes entries 256..511 into the next stack frame when two normalized rows together exceed 256 inversion points; stack corruption.

REPRO: Two regions each a single scanline of 128+ disjoint spans (256 inversion points each); region_op(&out,&A,&B,RGN_OP_XOR) overruns scratch[256..511].
close_reason: Fixed in 1ff449f: xmerge output-bounded + fail-loud at RGN_ROW_X_MAX; over-cap merges fail loud instead of overrunning scratch. Oracle: over-cap fail-loud probe + ASAN NO_XMERGE_CAP mutant (RED). Locked spec unchanged; cap decision is initech-44ab.

title: Latent: one baked-program output 'build' is dropped deterministically (reproduces on KVM)
description: While building the test-datetime baked program (beads initech-yv9), found that exactly ONE field-build in a multi-field output sequence is dropped/garbled deterministically per build (the dropped field shifts with code layout: MIN, HOUR, DOW observed). NOT a TCG artifact -- it reproduces under -accel kvm (real hardware) AND -accel tcg,one-insn-per-tb=on. The INT 21h handlers return CORRECT values (host oracle test-int21 + the values that DO appear confirm this); the corruption is in the GUEST program's instruction/data stream during execution. Symptoms: a cat-string loop appends nothing (string's first byte reads as NUL) or a store writes to a shifted address, at a position-dependent code site. Hypothesis: a kernel/loader memory-layout interaction corrupts the running program's code/data page during INT 21h processing (the PSP/DTA/env or staging copy region near 0x20000-0x20300). Worked around in os/milton/datetime_program.asm by emitting every field TWICE (one clean copy always survives the single per-run drop). Repro: build the datetime image, boot with -rtc base=...,clock=vm; observe one DT-* field missing without the duplicate-emit. Needs root-cause: instrument the program's code/data page for writes during a multi-INT-21h-write run; check loader staging/PSP/DTA overlap with PROGRAM_IMAGE (0x20100).
notes: ROOT-CAUSED by orchestrator (was mis-hypothesized as guest-exec corruption). The LOADER corrupts the program: load_program (os/milton/loader.c ~L224-232) does loader_memcpy(PROGRAM_IMAGE=0x20100, image, image_len) to copy the whole .COM, THEN writes the 2-byte empty env block at ENV_BLOCK=0x20200 = PROGRAM_IMAGE + 0x100. So for ANY program > 256 bytes, the env-zero OVERWRITES the program's own bytes at file offset 0x100-0x101 -> deterministic 2-byte corruption (reads as NUL). Matches every symptom (position-dependent, reproduces on KVM, 'first byte NUL'). Small programs (<256B, e.g. GREET/type/dir) are unaffected (env-zero lands past them); the resident shell is unaffected (not loader-loaded). CRITICAL: blocks InitechBase + Turbo Initech (both >256B). FIX: relocate ENV_BLOCK out of the program-image arena (memory_map.h is LOCKED spec -- deliberate change per Rule 8 + this issue) and remove the datetime_program.asm emit-twice WORKAROUND so the gate honestly verifies the fix. Mutation-prove: a program with a string at offset 0x100 must round-trip clean.
close_reason: ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED (was masked by an emit-twice workaround). Cause: load_program wrote the 2-byte env block at ENV_BLOCK=0x20200=PROGRAM_IMAGE+0x100 after the image copy, zeroing 2 bytes of any .COM >256B. Fix: relocated ENV_BLOCK to 0x5F000 (dedicated region below the stack, outside the image arena; PROGRAM_IMAGE_MAX capped to ENV_BLOCK). Workaround removed; test-datetime now emits each field once and is green -- proving the fix. Verified full vector green under load.

title: Screendump QEMU keystones flake on fixed wall-clock timeout (non-deterministic gate)
description: test-tracer-boot, test-boot, test-fs (and rarely test-shell) grab a framebuffer at a fixed --timeout-ms (~6s) and assert painted pixels via ppm_text_check. Under back-to-back QEMU boots (e.g. inside 'make test'/'make test-emu') the guest often has not rendered the banner/desktop within the wall clock, so the screendump is blank (fg=0) and the gate goes RED -- a wall-clock race, not a logic failure (they pass when the box is idle, confirmed: 3/3 tracer-boot, 2/2 boot, 2/2 fs standalone; RED inside the aggregate). A non-deterministic gate is worse than none -- it trains us to ignore red and makes 'make test' (initech-4mc) unusable as the rock-solid signal. FIX: replace the fixed-wall-clock screendump with poll-until-rendered (screendump-on-marker, or retry/grow the deadline until a serial 'rendered' marker appears, or screenshot when the guest signals paint-complete over serial). Must stay deterministic (Rule 11) and not weaken what ppm_text_check asserts (Law 2).
acceptance_criteria: 'make test' (host+emu, all 44 gates) passes deterministically 5x in a row on a loaded box; the screendump is captured only after the guest has actually painted (marker-driven, not fixed wall clock); ppm_text_check assertions unchanged; no sleeps that just paper over the race.
close_reason: Fixed: added --screendump-after MARKER; screendump now waits for the guest paint-complete serial marker (BANNER/DIR-OK) before grabbing, with the wall-clock as backstop and honest-RED fall-through. Verified: make test GREEN 2x under 6-core load (previously RED), negative control (NEVERPAINT) terminates at backstop and fails honestly, no hang.

title: Turbo IDE save staging name can alias the live work file and silently save only EOF
description:
Location: turbo/ide/editor.pas:483-495 (SaveAs), turbo/ide/buffer.pas:430-468 (BufSave), work names turbo/ide/editor.pas:1061-1062.

Scenario: user opens TURBOWK1.PAS in the IDE directory, edits, F2. SaveAs computes Temp=TURBOWK1.$$$ which is WorkName1. The Path-vs-work guard (editor.pas:495) does not cover Temp/Bak, and the stage-existence probe passes because side 1 is not created until BufSave's own PageFlush creates it; BufSave then Rewrites Temp, truncating the just-opened live work file, so the stage receives only the EOF byte. Renames publish it: TURBOWK1.PAS becomes a single 0x1A, dirty flag clears, success is reported. The edit survives nowhere (BAK holds only the pre-edit bytes); the work file is also renamed away.

Verified 2026-11-15 with the product's own save-identity host binary on origin/main 27f64482: 'FAIL save identity: TURBOWK1.PAS mode=0 err=0 dirty=FALSE bytes=<1A>'. TURBOWK0.PAS refuses with error 80 only because side 0 already exists. Re-review: reports/phase3/xreview-turbo-2.md finding 1.

Red-first regression: extend save-identity with TURBOWK0.PAS and TURBOWK1.PAS (both work sides, before and after a page flush): each save must either complete with XOLD+EOF at the name or be refused before any truncation with the dirty flag set; never success with wrong bytes. Distinctness must cover source, stage, backup AND both work names (the ge49u contract).

title: InitechBase failed READ retains a dirty GET and rewrites another record on untouched retry
description:
Independent read-only review at origin/main 1e0b1691b8b508e4eed9e5107ec9f3b00c69ac59, 2026-11-15.

apps/initechbase/cmd/query.c:1656,1663,1844,1862 return on q_get_write failure without clearing the pending GETs. q_get_rebind at :1273 copies the old GET, including changed=1, then replaces its buffer from the record current on the next READ. An untouched Enter can therefore write that newly loaded record through the lossy date parser despite receiving no edit.

Host reproduction (scratch C harness, product source unchanged): copy captured forms-f13a FORM.DBF/DBT, set record 2 FD to literal 20020115 in the independent fixture; declare GET FD on record 1 with CENTURY OFF; type 010194 and Enter while the stage-write PAL hook returns -PAL_ENOSPC. READ reports #56 and preserves record 1, but ngets remains 1. Recover the device, GO 2, READ with only Enter and no new GET: YEAR(FD) changes 2002 -> 1902; disk bytes at offset 250 are 19020115. This persists the old request's dirty state into another record.

Red receipt: build/xreview-forms2/repro.c, invoked with date from build/apps/initechbase/host/work/test_ibase_gets; review-read-failure fails the literal YEAR(FD)==2002 assertion. Log build/xreview-forms2/stale-date.log. Scratch paths are under reviewer worktree /home/tobias/.t3/worktrees/InitechOS/t3-0544d152-526fccacebf64dae. A first-write-failure control leaves FC unchanged and passes.

Fix/acceptance: define cleanup consistently for every failed READ, and never transfer a prior buffer's changed flag to a newly loaded buffer. Add a host fault test which fails once, recovers, navigates, and performs an untouched READ; compare the entire predecessor DBF, plus a semantic mutant restoring the stale dirty GET. Preserve captured normal READ/Esc behavior.

title: InitechCalc deferred cleanup deletes unrelated files that reuse a former stage name
description:
Read-only phase 3 re-review at 4b3b5634ea83c9334cbbab735dd2ed001ef48e52 (2026-11-15).

New regression in 2bc04cb8, apps/initechcalc/calc.c:549-552 and :561. A refused DELETE sets left_behind[i]; the next Save unconditionally deletes whatever is now at stage_names[i]. No check establishes that it is still the file CREATE_NEW originally reserved. CREATE_NEW later in :567 cannot protect this earlier DELETE.

Failing scenario: Save/cancel has a transient cleanup DELETE failure. Dismiss the notice. While Calc remains open, the user removes/moves that old temporary through the resident Finder, and an unrelated file is placed under the same name (e.g. copied or renamed to APPS\TABLES.TMP). Calc's next Save deletes that unrelated file, recreates the name as its stage, and deletes it on completion. No active-copy race or second disk app is required; these operations happen between completed requests.

Verified over sdk/host with unmodified product source: ordinary type 73 / Save / failed FILECOPY event, with TBX_FILE_DELETE=5 during its cleanup. Observe leftover=1 and left_behind[0]=1. Clear the fault, dismiss the notice, delete the old stage and put distinct literal user bytes at the same path (the host fixture models the intervening filesystem actions). Save/complete again. Result: foreign-present=0 and dirty=0; reproduction exits 1. Stock preexisting-stranger tests pass because they never establish and then invalidate an old ownership bit.

Red-first test: fault the cleanup; replace that leftover with a different file before retry; require that file's bytes remain and that Save chooses a different stage or safely refuses. Baseline currently fails this runtime assertion. Recovery needs to establish current ownership, or refuse/leave an ambiguous leftover, rather than treating a pathname remembered from an earlier transaction as continuing ownership.

Related but different old defects: initech-1tuwf used truncating CREATE after an OPEN fault; initech-40kpb forgot leftovers altogether. This new loss is caused by the newly added deferred DELETE of an ownership bit whose file has been replaced.

title: InitechCalc save guard compares a rounded display value and silently changes stored numbers
description:
Read-only phase 3 re-review at 4b3b5634ea83c9334cbbab735dd2ed001ef48e52 (2026-11-15), covering the five Calc/frame commits after 61e8f545.

apps/initechcalc/calc.c:344-349 obtains the cell value by formatting it with i123_cell_content and parsing that text. apps/initech123/core/fmt.c:600-643 explicitly formats that control-panel text to 15 significant digits. The new put_value check at calc.c:293-299 compares its output with the already rounded value; it never compares against the actual stored cell value. Its successful roundtrip therefore does not establish the new README promise that a number saves as itself.

Verified through ordinary typing, Save, successful FILE COPY provider completion, and reopening over sdk/host, using i123_cell_value to observe actual worksheet numbers independently of the display formatter:
- Type 1234567890123456: the stored value is exactly 1234567890123456. Save succeeds, clears g_dirty, and writes (G) 1234567890123460. Reopening raises no alert and stores 1234567890123460.
- Type 0.12345678901234567: stored double 0.12345678901234568 becomes 0.123456789012346 after successful Save/reopen.
- The 0.0000001 control saves/reopens unchanged.

This differs from closed initech-3yye3 (exponent syntax rejected the whole document): the document now opens normally but silently contains a different numeric value. The lossy extraction predates these five commits, and the new guard does not catch it.

Red-first test: type a 16-digit integer, capture its actual numeric value via i123_cell_value (not i123_cell_content), Save/reopen and require equality, or require clear save refusal with dirty work and the previous file preserved. Current reproduction exits 1. Use the public numeric-value accessor for serialization or refuse before publication when actual stored values cannot roundtrip.

title: XCOPY deletes a pre-existing destination when the source read fails after the first 2 KiB
description: Review 2026-11-15 (xreview-dos-4 F1), follow-up to closed initech-wz16r. dos/xcopy/xcopy_tree.c:246-257,275: transfer() reads only the first 2048-byte chunk (buf[2048]) before CREAT truncates the destination; any later AH=3Fh failure sets error and line 275 then unlinks dst unconditionally. So XCOPY SRC\BIG.BIN DST over an existing DST\BIG.BIN, with the source unreadable past byte 2048, destroys the old destination entirely (before 064fb460 it was left partial; now it is gone). The code's own cited premise is that genuine XCOPY buffers sources in memory before writing, which would leave the destination untouched for any file that fits in memory; the operator disk-full ruling covers write-side full disk, not source read failure, and no genuine XCOPY capture exists (compat33/dos33 ORIGIN: XCOPY absent from media). Reproduced on host: harness variant failing only the 2nd AH=3Fh, 5000-byte source, 28-byte pre-existing destination -> exit 5, 'Access denied', DST\BIG.BIN not found (mtools). The wz16r test only fails the FIRST read, so it cannot see this. Red-first: in xcopy_tree.sh fail the 2nd read on a >2 KiB source over a seeded destination and cmp the destination bytes with mtools. Fix options: buffer the whole file (or as much as memory allows, as genuine XCOPY does) before CREAT, or keep the pre-existing destination on read-side errors. title: InitechBase field GET writes into a different table after USE reopens its work area
description:
Independent cross-provider review, 2026-11-15, origin/main c4722e74.

A field GET records only (area, field index) at declaration (q_get_resolve in apps/initechbase/cmd/query.c, about :1194-1204). The write (q_get_write, about :1395-1402) checks only wa_is_open(area) before ibase_write_field(area, recno, field_index). The eval.h comment says the binding is "re-resolved at READ/write-back", but only the record is re-resolved. The table and field are not.

Verified on the host (scratch harness against the built objects), files read back:
- USE FORM; @ 5,10 GET FN; USE BASE (conformance C37 BASE.DBF: KEY C8, VALUE N6); READ; Ctrl-Y "99" Enter. BASE.DBF record 1 VALUE becomes 99. FORM.DBF is byte-identical to its input.
- Same with GET FC: BASE.DBF KEY becomes "ZZ".

The edit lands in a different file and field that the user never declared a GET on. Design C13 asked for exactly this case ("Repeat after RELEASE/USE closes a binding ... invalidation/error behavior, no stale pointer"). It was never captured: forms-f13a/b/c cover binding precedence and record moves only.

Red-first test: declare a field GET, reopen the area on another table, READ with an edit, and assert the second table's bytes are unchanged. Capture real III+ for USE/CLOSE/CLEAR ALL between declaration and READ to settle the error or no-op behaviour.
close_reason: Fixed in 2ba157fc following real III+ (F20d-F20n): real III+ does write into the table now open in the area, by field position and with that field's type; READ reloads from the current record, repaints only changed cells. Mutant mutate-get-keeps-binding.

title: InitechBase GET write-back at end of file overwrites the last record
description:
Independent cross-provider review, 2026-11-15, origin/main c4722e74.

ibase_write_field (apps/initechbase/cmd/mutate.c:617) writes wa_recno() of the GET's area with no EOF guard. REPLACE's default scope has that guard (mutate.c:684-687, captured C04: at EOF nothing is replaced). After GO BOTTOM / SKIP (EOF, RECNO()=3 on the 2-record forms-f13a FORM.DBF), `@ 5,10 GET FC`, READ, keys "AB" Enter writes "AB      " over record 2's FC ("WXYZ" before). Verified on the host with a scratch harness against the built objects. xxd of FORM.DBF after the run shows record 2 FC = "AB      ", and READKEY is 271.

The user typed into the phantom EOF record, and the last real record was silently overwritten.

Red-first test: test_ibase_gets field case at EOF asserting FORM.DBF bytes are unchanged (literal from the SETUP fixture). Capture the real III+ behaviour of GET/READ at EOF (and on an empty table) before deciding what READ shows and returns there.
close_reason: Fixed in 8b82f1f2 (F20c/F20g): READ at end of file is #4 at entry, nothing written. Mutant mutate-read-at-eof.

title: InitechBase READ rewrites untouched date and numeric GETs: 2001 becomes 1901, CENTURY ON 1992 becomes 1919
description:
Independent cross-provider review, 2026-11-15, origin/main c4722e74 (forms landed 1d64c36d..4217ee5c).

READ writes every GET it leaves back to its variable or field, edited or not (apps/initechbase/cmd/query.c q_read: Enter/Down at 1476-1481, Up 1483-1488, Home/End chains, final save-exit write ~1634-1639). The write re-parses the display buffer, so the round trip is lossy:

- Dates: q_get_parse (query.c:1367-1384) reads only the first six digits as MMDDYY and always sets year=1900+yy. It ignores SET CENTURY and SET DATE.
- Numbers: the stored value is the rounded display text, and a pictured numeric GET takes its decimals from the template (q_get_resolve, about :1250-1254).

Verified on the host by a scratch harness linked against the built host-core objects (keys fed through pal->conin_char, as test_ibase_gets does), one Enter and no edit in every case. READKEY returns 15, the "unchanged" exit:
- SET CENTURY ON, USE FORM (forms-f13a fixture), GO 2, @ 5,10 GET FD, READ, Enter: DTOC(FD) goes from 01/15/1992 to 01/15/1919. On disk, FORM.DBF record 2 FD changes from 19920115 to 19190115 (cmp -l: bytes 253-254).
- Default settings (CENTURY OFF, AMERICAN) on a 2001-01-01 date: YEAR() goes to 1901.
- SET DATE BRITISH with D=CTOD("05/01/92"): becomes 1 May (month and day swapped). With 31/01/92, Enter is refused (invalid date) and the form cannot be left with Enter. ANSI likewise.
- N=10/3: after Enter, N*3 = 9.99. N=12.345 with PICTURE "999.99" becomes 12.34.

Capture contradiction: forms-f11-func, N=-12.5, GET PICTURE "@( 999.99", Enter. Real III+ RESULT has "N=        -12.5" (RK2=15); the product prints -12.50. So real III+ does not re-store an untouched pictured numeric. The Y2K canon (typed 013100 -> 1900, F08/F17) is about entered dates. It does not license rewriting an untouched record.

Red-first test: a test_ibase_gets case asserting that F11's N=-12.5 is unchanged after Enter (literal from forms-f11-func/exports/RESULT.TXT), and a field case with SET CENTURY ON asserting the FD bytes on disk are unchanged after an untouched READ. Capture the CENTURY ON and BRITISH date GET pages and results on real III+ before implementing date editing in those modes.
close_reason: Fixed in 5650a0e7 (captures a9bbb4f1, F20a/b/l): only GETs a key changed are stored; edited dates follow SET DATE/CENTURY. Mutant mutate-get-writes-untouched.

title: Menu-bar title spacing is 5 px per title wider than the period Menu Manager
description:
Found while working initech-jeo8c (FLAIR expectations sharing renderer bugs). The menu-bar title layout is wider than the period Menu Manager, and every existing check derives its expectation from the product, so it passed.

## Evidence
- s7_desktop.png (System 7.5.3, Chicago 12; system7-decomp specs/desktop/menu-bar.md "Title layout"): title ink File 43..63, Edit 79..101, View 117..146, Label 162..194, Special 210..253; uniform 15 px white gap.

title: Turbo IDE discards loaded and saved directory paths so F2 writes the wrong file
description:
## 5. P1 — Load/Write to discard the path used by later saves

**Location:** [turbo/ide/editor.pas:438][editor438], also `WriteTo` at 590–591, `DoSave` at 523 and `LeafName` at 564–579.

**Scenario:** The user loads `SUB\DOC.PAS` (or a file on another drive), edits and saves it. The IDE saves to `DOC.PAS` in the current directory instead; the intended source stays unchanged and another file can be overwritten.

**Evidence and verification:** Load opens the complete supplied name, then keeps only `LeafName` as `FileName`. Write to does the same. There is no CWD/drive update or separate stored full path; `DoSave` passes this basename to `SaveAs`. The no-fault `path` reproduction loads literal host filename `SUB\DOC.PAS = OLD`, with `DOC.PAS = ROOT-SENTINEL` beside it. F2 leaves the loaded file `OLD`, replaces root `DOC.PAS` with `XOLD` plus EOF, moves the root sentinel to `DOC.BAK`, and clears the dirty flag.

**Red-first regression:** Load from a subdirectory and from another DOS drive with an unrelated same-basename sentinel in the current directory. After edit/F2, only the originally selected file may change. Repeat after Write to and subsequent F2; assert full identity, not just displayed leaf text.

title: Turbo IDE first F2 save overwrites existing files without confirmation or backup
description:
## 4. P1 — First F2 save overwrites an existing file without confirmation or backup

**Location:** [turbo/ide/editor.pas:618][editor618], also 623 and 626–629.

**Scenario:** In an unnamed buffer, the user presses F2 and enters an existing filename. The IDE immediately replaces that file, with no overwrite prompt and no BAK.

**Evidence and verification:** `SaveCommand` opens `NameRename` for the unnamed buffer. `NameAccept` tests `FileExists` only for `NameWrite`; `NameRename` falls through to `WriteTo(NameText, false)`. The false `Existing` flag bypasses the old-file copy. The no-fault `rename` reproduction starts with `DOC.PAS = OLD`, types `X` in a new buffer, presses F2 and accepts `DOC.PAS`. It returns `mode=0 dirty=FALSE`, replaces the old file with `58 1a` and creates no `DOC.BAK`.

**Red-first regression:** First-save to an existing name must enter the overwrite state before any write; Esc/N must leave all bytes unchanged. Y must preserve the previous version according to the chosen save policy. Include read-open errors in the existence probe so an inaccessible existing destination is never treated as absent.

title: Turbo IDE saving a .BAK source replaces the edit with its old bytes and reports success
description:
## 3. P1 — Saving a .BAK source silently restores its old contents

**Location:** [turbo/ide/editor.pas:477][editor477] and 494–495.

**Scenario:** The user opens `DOC.BAK`, edits it and presses F2. Save reports success and clears the dirty flag, but the file contains its pre-edit bytes.

**Evidence and verification:** The backup name is always the source stem plus `.BAK`, so `Path` and `Bak` alias for an accepted `.BAK` source. After writing the new document, `Erase(Bak)` deletes it and `Rename(Temp, Bak)` installs the old copy in its place. The no-fault `bak` reproduction edits `OLD` to `XOLD`; `DoSave` returns editor mode and `dirty=FALSE`, while `DOC.BAK` is exactly `OLD`, without even the newly saved EOF marker. No filename filter prohibits loading/saving `.BAK` files.

**Red-first regression:** Open/edit/save `DOC.BAK`; require `XOLD` plus EOF to remain at that name and the modified flag to clear only then. Also cover case-insensitive aliases, extensionless files and a source named `DOC.$$$`, since the temporary name is derived in the same way. Choose distinct names or explicitly refuse conflicting names before any truncation.

title: Turbo IDE deletes its recovery copy even when restoring a failed save also fails
description:
## 2. P1 — Failed save recovery deletes the only copy of the previous file

**Location:** [turbo/ide/editor.pas:488][editor488], also 497–499 and `FileCopy` in [buffer.pas:384][buffer384].

**Scenario:** A write to an existing source fails, and writing the previous bytes back also fails. The IDE leaves the named file truncated and erases the recovery copy even though restoration never succeeded.

**Evidence and verification:** `SaveAs` calls `FileCopy(Temp, Path)` on save error but never checks its `BufErr`. It then always erases `Temp` on the error branch. Both the initial save and recovery use `Rewrite`, truncating the destination first. The `rollback` reproduction starts with `DOC.PAS = OLD` and injects two zero-byte writes to `DOC.PAS`, after the complete `DOC.$$$` copy has been made. It reports error 101 and stays dirty, but `DOC.PAS` is zero bytes and both `DOC.$$$` and `DOC.BAK` are absent. The previous bytes survive nowhere in that directory.

**Red-first regression:** Inject failure in the main write, then independently in every recovery write and close. On every reported failure the original path must retain its original bytes, per the design's save contract. At minimum never destroy the recovery file on a failed restoration; a checked staged replacement is needed to meet the stronger original-name contract.

title: Turbo IDE commits a failed page flush and later saves the truncated document
description:
## 1. P1 — Failed page write is committed, losing the dirty page

**Location:** [turbo/ide/buffer.pas:155][buffer155], also `PageFlush` at 124–161, `PageLoad` at 171–177, and `BufSave` at 413–420.

**Scenario:** The disk fills while a dirty edit page is being flushed during navigation or Save. The IDE adopts the incomplete work file, discards the dirty page and can later save an empty/truncated document while reporting success.

**Evidence and verification:** `OutFlush` records short writes in `BufErr`, but `PageFlush` unconditionally advances `DocLen`, `PgOrig`, `WorkSide` and clears `PgDirty`. `PageLoad` then clears/reloads the in-memory page. `BufSave` clears `BufErr` *after* calling `PageFlush`, hiding that failure. The `paging` reproduction loads `OLD`, inserts `X`, and gives the alternate work file one zero-byte write. Output: `buferr=101 pgdirty=FALSE pglen=0 side=1`. Retrying Save returns code 0, clears the modified flag, and replaces `DOC.PAS` with the single byte `1a`. Its BAK contains only the original `OLD`; the edit is lost.

**Red-first regression:** Fail each prefix/page/suffix/flush/close operation during page replacement; assert no side/index/dirty-state commit, the edited page remains recoverable and the old named source stays byte-identical. After removing the fault, navigation and Save must produce independently authored edited bytes. Include failure on the direct Save-triggered page flush, so resetting `BufErr` cannot hide it.

title: InitechCalc successful saves with exponent-form numbers cannot be reopened
description:
Independent read-only frame review, 2026-11-15, origin/main a0f352df14d666f15af338f4e70b4bee4d7bf869. Introduced in ee66540c.

apps/initechcalc/calc.c:277-279,324-329 serializes numbers through i123_number_text, which emits exponent notation. The reader at :90-103 (especially :99) accepts only digits, decimal point and commas; it rejects E. One such cell makes parse refuse the whole document (:173,250-252).

Verified through the real Calc entry point and Save events over sdk/host: start with valid LEDGER.TXT and previous TABLES.TXT, type 0.0000001 into the first cell, File > Save, approve replacement, complete the FILE COPY provider contract, then relaunch on the saved bytes. The saved row is `1\t(G) 1E-7`; completion clears g_dirty, but relaunch says TABLES.TXT could not be read and opens the original ledger. Typing 1000000000000000000000 produces `(G) 1E21` and the same failure. Normal 73 saves/reopens green. The previous readable file has already been replaced; all user edits in the new document become unavailable through Calc.

Red-first regression already run: ordinary typed input -> Save/replace -> copy stage under the host provider's contract -> reopen must preserve the edited value without an unreadable-document alert. Both exponent cases return 1; 73 returns 0. Extend across negative and format variants; align serialized numeric syntax with the reader, or refuse before replacing a file.

title: Word piece-read cache survives borrowed-document restore: Undelete cancel or Look corrupts the document
description:
Cross-provider review 2026-11-14 (scope 123-word), head aba1918d. Introduced by 4dafaa7c "Speed sequential Word piece reads without reducing tests".

## Defect
apps/initechword/core/piece.c:34-36,208-224 caches the last piece read by iw_doc_byte, keyed on the document's ADDRESS (byte_doc). Only iw_doc_init/load/insert/delete reset it. Three face paths borrow g_ed.doc for a temporary document and then restore it by struct assignment, which does not reset the cache:
- face_a.c:1068-1080 (Undelete F1 preview paint, g_preview)
- face_a.c:1714-1723 (List Files Look, Up/Down)
- face_a.c:1809-1830 (List Files Look paint, g_look_w.body in the spare bank)
After the restore, iw_doc_byte(&g_ed.doc, pos) returns bytes of the borrowed buffer for every pos below its length. iw_doc_read (Save/flatten) uses locate() and is correct, but every unit walk, wrap, paint, search, code test and Delete/Backspace length uses iw_doc_byte.

## Failing scenarios (reproduced on host)
1. Type Q, Backspace; type a, F6, cd, F6 (body 61 c3 0c c3 63 64 c4 0c c4); cursor before the Bold code; F1 (Undelete preview), F1 (cancel); Del. The cached byte at 1 is 'Q', so Del deletes one byte of the 3-byte C3 0C C3 group; the body becomes 40 bytes of broken codes and iw_wp5_read of the flattened document returns IW_E_CODE (-4). A subsequent F10 writes that file; Retrieve then refuses it as "Incompatible File Format". With piece.c from 4dafaa7c~1 the same steps leave the document intact. Repro: build/xreview/repro_word_cache.c in the reviewer worktree (t3-a69b83d4).
2. Type abcdef; F5 Enter; select a WP file containing ZZZZZZZZZZ; 6 (Look); Esc; F7. The editing screen row 0 shows ZZZZZZ while the document is abcdef; iw_doc_byte(&g_ed.doc,0) == 'Z'. Any edit before the next insert/delete operates on the looked-at file's structure. Repro: build/xreview/repro_word_look.c.

## Red-first test
In test_iword_undo: after "Cancel removes preview without inserting", assert the screen row and that Del at a code boundary leaves a document iw_wp5_read accepts. In listfiles: Look a different file, return to the document, assert the screen shows the document's own text. Both are red today and green with 4dafaa7c reverted.

## Fix direction
Invalidate in the borrowing paths, or key the cache on (d, d->pc, d->npc, d->orig, d->add) so a restored struct cannot match a stale entry.

title: QEMU desktop marker waits accept stale and substring markers
description: factory/emu/qemu.c:1515 sends W<marker> to wait_for_serial_marker (qemu.c:1656-1673), which passes on the first strstr hit anywhere in the serial. Bochs counts the n-th occurrence (desktop-bochs.c:44-46); QEMU does not. smoke-desktop.sh runs every journey in one QEMU boot, so every TENANT-EXIT wait after 123's first exit, Paint's 2nd-4th FLAIR-DISPATCH app=PAINT, the second app=NOTEPAD and the second Control Panels repaint TENANT-GATE all pass immediately. launch_app CALC.EXE (FLAIR-DISPATCH app=CALC) is satisfied by the earlier app=CALCULAT line, and the end-of-run grep -Fc count also counts CALCULAT, so in QEMU the proof that CALC.EXE was dispatched is vacuous. TENANT-FILECOPY-DONE can be satisfied by InitechWord's earlier FILE COPY. Repro: /tmp/xr-factory/qw.c includes qemu.c and runs qmp_inject_mouse_trace with WTENANT-EXIT x3 and WFLAIR-DISPATCH app=CALC against a serial with one exit line and one CALCULAT line: all four pass in 166ms. Red-first: extend factory/tests/qemu-trace.c to require line-exact n-th occurrence for repeated W tokens; make the smoke-desktop marker totals line-exact. title: Warm image build can ship an old resident desktop after rebuilding its archive
description:
system/Makefile:19-23 forwards component archives through order-only `components`, then decides whether to relink system.elf. A warm `make image` can rebuild libdesktop.a without relinking the resident image. The exact causal edge is an inference from these rules; the stale shipped artifact and wrong runtime behavior are directly reproduced.

At factory HEAD b12ab5ba, fresh isolated source tree:
1. `nice make -j2 image` from empty build, then a real Bochs Finder-open baseline passes.
2. Apply factory/mutants/desktop-wait/stall.patch (an unconditional cli/hlt loop immediately after FLAIR-LIVE-READY).
3. Run `nice make -j2 image` once. Log shows start.c recompiles and libdesktop.a is rebuilt, but no system linker/objcopy command.
4. Bochs still opens Finder and exits0; the unconditional halt is absent from the shipped image.

Evidence retained under /tmp/factory-3-evidence/warm-image/ (build logs, exact patch/source, stat/hash receipt, healthy and erroneously healthy mutant serial/reports). Original source/build tree: /home/tobias/.t3/worktrees/InitechOS/t3-fbaa1340-c4a6b012d7f17dbc/build/factory/desktop-wait-mutants/run.DXm4lc/. libdesktop.a mtime11:09:08.892602035; system.elf11:08:59.192158756; INITDOS.SYS11:08:59.195096971. Healthy and mutant boot clones have IDENTICAL SHA-256 b1e41682abc93d987d7cf779ad92aecfd2fbe116feb3d1943f3e79f86ab2bae4.

The new factory stall grader correctly reports `1 errors`, never a kill, for this unexpected survival. It now cold-builds both pristine and mutated images from the same snapshot, so its own fault proof does not rely on warm component propagation. No system product Makefile was edited by factory owner.

Fix the component-forwarder/link prerequisite ordering or freshness propagation; do not simply build twice. Acceptance: a single warm image build after this external source fault ships the changed code (FLAIR-LIVE-READY then no Finder marker), and a single warm build after restoring source opens Finder again. Keep a genuinely independent runtime or equivalent source-specific negative control, plus normal cold image/repro checks.

title: Mutation source snapshots ignore tar producer failures
description:
factory/gate-mutants.sh:12, factory/red-desktop.sh:18 and factory/smoke-mutants.sh:11,17 pipe 'tar -cf - ... | tar -xf - ...' under POSIX set -eu. The pipeline returns only the extractor's status; a read failure reported by the source tar does not fail snapshot creation. An incomplete snapshot or a file changed while read is accepted as trusted input to the graders.

Observed at a49afccd7555dca0bdc4db980486fa528ef4aefd: PATH tar wrapper executes /usr/bin/tar then returns 2 for -cf (stderr 'injected tar source-read failure after stream'), while extraction delegates normally. nice env PATH=/tmp/review-factory-tar/bin:$PATH sh factory/gate-mutants.sh exits 0: 10 mutants, 10 killed, 0 survived, 0 errors, despite ten producer errors. Intact sweep also passes 10/10. Injected log /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2/review-factory-evidence/tar-injected.log, intact /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2/review-factory-evidence/gate-mutants.log.

Wrapper:
#!/bin/sh
/usr/bin/tar "$@" || exit $?
case $1 in -cf) echo 'injected tar source-read failure after stream' >&2; exit 2;; esac

Fix: create/check an intermediate archive before extraction, or use a POSIX producer-status receipt that the parent checks. Source copying errors must count as setup errors, not success. Add a producer-failure regression. P1: proven evidence-acquisition false pass, no claim that this complete-stream injection omitted product bytes.

title: INT 21h close of standard handles falsely succeeds without freeing the JFT slot
description:
kernel/int21.c:3302-3307 treats AH=3Eh CLOSE of process handles 0..4 as unconditional success without clearing the JFT entry. This contradicts real DOS 3.30 and blocks the final InitechBase conformance case C33 on the target. InitechBase's reviewed scope is apps/initechbase only; no kernel edit was made.

Independent real-DOS probe: close inherited AUX handle 3 (AH=3Eh), open existing MINT.PRG (AH=3Dh), require returned handle 3. Genuine DOS 3.30 prints CLOSE3-OK. Exact NASM source, COM bytes, boot/data disks, driver log and VGA text are in the disposable path listed below. Runtime is the hash-pinned DOS 3.30 media used by goldens/dataloss; no InitechOS code is an expected value.

The genuine III+ C33 PSP/JFT/SFT capture also shows that dBASE reuses AUX for its overlay, retaining four standard descriptors, DBASE.OVL, MINT.PRG, table/alternate output and twelve independent PROBE.PRG descriptors before its twenty-slot JFT is full. The InitechBase host now matches all 36 captured cases. Target C33 reaches only eleven because its request to free AUX reports success without freeing it. Both a reused smoke process and a fresh InitechBase process reproduce it; it is not leftover work-area state.

Fix request: AH=3Eh should clear any valid JFT slot, including predefined handles, while retaining/pinning the underlying resident device SFT as needed. A file duplicated into a standard-number slot must close its file reference normally. Invalid handles must retain DOS errors. This must be fixed by the kernel owner, with its red-first reference test. Do not work around it by a private kernel call from the app or by changing C33's expected output.

title: FILE COPY forgets handles after cancel cleanup and rate-file CLOSE failures
description:

A second tbx_fc_close is then a no-op. Also :1632-1634 returns the MICHAEL.CFG close error without retaining/retrying that handle. title: InitechBase REPORT and LABEL silently consume injected source I/O failures
description:
Independent review of t3/initechbase-write-safety-checks, 9d214ebd. These source-error handling paths predate the diff; no branch edits.

apps/initechbase/cmd/report.c:385-387 ignores expression failure while inferring report column types and explicitly clears its error. Source I/O failures can then be retried silently. LABEL also masks a source failure through the existing cursor/EOF behavior: cmd/report.c:528, wa_nav_skip/nav_raw_skip in cmd/nav.c (EOF transition ignores wa_goto return). The new output-preservation test deliberately skips seek/read injection for REPORT/LABEL/ALTERNATE at tests/test_ibase_dbsafe.c:228, leaving these failures invisible.

Reproduction: copy tests/test_ibase_dbsafe.c outside the branch, remove only `if(cmd>=3 && (kind==1 || kind==5))break;`, link against the unchanged branch objects, and run `writes`. Exact disposable source, link command and log: /tmp/review-initechbase-evidence/full-matrix.c, link-matrix.sh, full-matrix.log. Results: 5647 checks / 8 failures. REPORT TRAVELER NEXT 1 TO FILE OUTPUT.TXT returns success on seek boundary 1 or read boundary 3; LABEL ADDRESS TO FILE OUTPUT.TXT returns success on seek boundary 2 or read boundary 3. The existing PREVIOUS-FILE destination is replaced in all four cases. This is a silent source-error/false-success gap; the experiment does not establish that every recovered one-shot source failure produces wrong field values, so do not describe all four as demonstrated corrupt reports.

Propagate source faults or explicitly capture/qualify a retry policy and resulting complete output. Add both fail-once and persistent source-failure controls with independent output expectations. Current output-only write/close tests cannot certify the source-navigation seam.
close_reason: Review hypothesis disproved: returned-success outputs are complete and identical; reported failures preserve the destination.

comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text: Follow-up disproves this as a concrete defect: /tmp/review-initechbase-evidence/source-output.c compares all returned-success outputs with the corresponding no-fault run and checks old destination on returned errors. All six successful injected cases produce byte-identical complete output, including the redundant final LABEL reread under persistent source error. REPORT persistent failures return errors and retain the preceding destination. The expanded matrix incorrectly required every internal injected operation to become a command error even when the command recovered. Retracting this review finding; the recovered-output comparison is an investigation, not an independent conformance oracle.

title: Note Pad treats legal positive short reads as a damaged store
description:
Read-only finding during initech-gxb4z, baseline 09d52a32.

apps/notepad/notepad.c:118 makes a single tbx_file_read, then :119 treats any count other than DA_FILE_BYTES as a damaged store. A legal positive short read of 4 bytes on the valid 8224-byte N01.DAT fixture sets g_keep, exposes empty pages, and blocks later saves even though the store is complete and readable. The same compiled source is used for Scrapbook. This is a false refusal, not the destructive InitechText defect: g_keep makes save() at :143 leave the original bytes untouched.

Concrete host probe using the real app, FLAIR TextEdit, SDK host and the 4fb96275 N01.DAT fixture:
  read_limit=0: bytes=8224 keep=0 shown=1024 save=1 unchanged=1
  read_limit=4: bytes=8224 keep=1 shown=0 save=1 unchanged=1

Source and reproduction will be retained in phase2/initechtext-evidence/notepad-probe.c and the phase2/initechtext.md handoff. No Note Pad code was edited. Load should accumulate successful positive reads before judging the fixed-size store, retaining the existing no-overwrite behavior on real errors/EOF.
close_reason: Landed on main (48d1d141 range): loader gathers positive reads; red-first fixture test, mutant da_mut_single_read killed in both builds; smoke green both emulators.

title: Console-pair smoke times out while waiting for another Bochs run
description: kernel/tests/smoke/conpair.sh:30 wraps the emulator harness in timeout 40, but factory/emu/bochs.c:607-641 deliberately queues for the host-wide /tmp/initech-bochs.lock before starting the guest execution deadline. Under concurrent builders, conpair dies in the lock queue before launching Bochs, then line 36 fails because run.serial does not exist. Observed on t3/kernel-dataloss-import at 0735a6bf: both QEMU cases pass; report contains only another Bochs run holds /tmp/initech-bochs.lock; waiting, no run.serial, make smoke exits 2 before the aggregate smoke. Log retained at /tmp/kernel-phase2-logs/smoke-final.log and copied with P2/kernel.md. Queueing must not consume the execution deadline; retain bounded guest execution and exit/status/serial/independent byte checks. No product behavior failed in this attempt; rerun after serialization is in progress.

title: DOS batch percent-0 contains the resolved path instead of the invocation name
description:
Review 2026-11-14, t3/dos330-compatibility-study, base 09d52a32.
File: dos/command/command.c:4590-4600 run_batch_invoke stores the resolved
filesystem path as argv[0]. Case: invoke BATCH.BAT with ordinary arguments
and ECHO PARAMS=[%0][%1][%2][%9]. Independent pinned DOS 3.30 prints
[BATCH.BAT][one][two][nine]; product prints [A:\BATCH.BAT][one][two][nine].
The reference working volume is B: but %0 has no drive/path at all, so this
is not an A:/B: normalization difference. P1: batch programs inspecting
or reusing the invocation spelling observe a different value. Evidence:
dos/command/tests/compat33/{expected,observed}/BATCH input/TRACE readbacks.
Keep the opened path separate from the invocation token. SHIFT correctly
changes %0 on both; retaining later arguments is existing initech-tyvt.
No product code changed in review branch.
close_reason: Closed

title: DOS resolves device basenames through nonexistent directories and invalid drives
description:
Review 2026-11-14, t3/dos330-compatibility-study, base 09d52a32.
File: kernel/int21.c:2238-2290 device basename resolution before ordinary
path/drive validation in do_open at :2345.
Read-only DEVPROBE.COM opens each name, queries IOCTL's device bit, closes;
it never reads/writes a printer or serial port. Genuine pinned DOS 3.30 opens
CON, SUB\CON.TXT, SUB\PRN, SUB\NUL, SUB\AUX as devices, but refuses
MISSING\NUL and Z:\NUL when parent directory/drive is absent. InitechDOS
reports DEVICE for both invalid paths. CON: is refused by both (control).
P1: invalid paths silently succeed. Evidence: dos/command/tests/compat33/
{expected,observed}/DEVICES/files/TRACE.TXT; dual 16/32-bit devices.asm
reproducer; disk snapshots show SUB exists and MISSING does not. Product was
486/8 MiB and completed cleanly. No product edits. Search for 8.3 and device
path issues found no open duplicate; see report for other name differences.

comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text:
Research diagnosis at origin/main eeb680304bcf7e95f135eb18e5da632a953a18f5, branch t3/diagnose-bochs-desktop-smoke. No repository files edited.

This adds evidence to the existing desktop wait defect rather than duplicating it. The original "no timeout override" part of this issue is superseded: factory/desktop-bochs.c:37-41 now supports DESKTOP_WAIT_MS. The remaining failure is the fixed nominal per-marker budget, which is not reset by meaningful phase progress, plus a separate insufficient default full-session allowance.

Seventh tenant launch is TEXT.EXE (fifth registered journey directory): previous launches are 123, WORD, CALCULAT, NOTEPAD from Calculator's clipboard check, NOTEPAD, SCRAPBK. Sentinel 59a3ecda serial ends during Text Paste's repaint, before the following Undo/Select All/Clear/Undo and Save are consumed. keys_sent=235 means the driver sent through Ctrl-S, not that the guest acknowledged it. The indexed unchanged trace maps key230=Paste, 231/232=Undo, 233=Select All, 234=Undo, 235=Save; await Standard File follows immediately.

Five Bochs-only repetitions of the complete unchanged desktop trace, image and driver:
1. nice10, session90s/marker10s: RED at90.06s, 6/12 exits, timed_out=1. Text Save dialog, successful rename to UNTITLED, and Save As dialog all appear before termination.
2. nice0, session90s/marker10s: RED at94.29s, 6/12 exits, first TENANT-SF put up missing, timed_out=1; serial advances every second through Text edits. No concurrent work of mine; image/tools had been built with nice -n0 make -j1.
3. nice10, session240s/marker10s: RED at100.22s, EXACT sentinel failure: first TENANT-SF put up missing, keys_sent=235, 6/12 exits, timed_out=0, signal15, triple_fault=0. Serial continues typing alpha then Return up to termination. Enlarging the session allowance alone does not fix the failure.
4. nice10, session240s/marker60s: GREEN at169.81s, all12 counted exits plus Paint via=close, keys_sent=312, all8 verifier scripts green.
5. nice0, session240s/marker60s: GREEN at177.06s, same markers/input counts and all8 verifiers green. Text dispatch~79s, first Save dialog~122s, rename~124s, Save As~130s, Cancel~131s, exit~133s (one-second external serial-size sampling).

All runs have triple_fault=0 and no KBD-RING-DROP, FLAIR-EVT-DROP, TENANT-FAULT or PANIC marker. Source disks/driver and trace hashes match across all5. TEXT.EXE matches the sentinel binary byte-for-byte, SHA256 aa14b90f998bdc5c91a15313ad191c3bded440164e178122942a6262f25888af.

Verdict: a factory wait/replay failure, not a demonstrated app/Toolbox hang or lost event. Shared-host load varied7.5-12; nice0 also failed, and emulator CPU utilization was96-100%, so this is not proof that scheduler starvation alone causes it. It demonstrates that the nominal10s W wait aborts a live backlog. factory/desktop-bochs.c:35-55 polls500 times with20ms sleeps and no progress renewal; factory/emu/bochs.c:883-905 counts sent RFB keys without guest consumption acknowledgements. On parse failure the driver breaks and intentionally terminates Bochs. Its overall90s default in factory/smoke-desktop.sh:64 is also insufficient for these complete traces.

Factory owner request: implement bounded phase progress/input-consumption synchronization instead of a fixed short wall-time assumption; retain RFB pumping, repeated-marker counts, all journeys/readbacks, and hard monotonic overall expiry. Clock-only serial chatter must not keep a missing phase alive indefinitely. Add deterministic controls for slow meaningful progress past10s, a genuinely missing marker, unrelated heartbeat noise and late completion still being RED. Keep the initech-5e3wu timeout guard; this diagnosis does not justify accepting late completion. Coordinate the ordered phase-wait work with initech-b8vxr. The240s/60s invocations are diagnostic green controls, not a default make smoke fix.

title: InitechBase disk DO recursion reaches a different limit and error from real III+
description:
InitechBase disk DO recursion reaches a different limit and error from real III+

P1. apps/initechbase/cmd/proc.c:589 closes each disk program handle immediately after loading; p_do uses the20-level recursion cap (:138) rather than reproducing real disk-program file-handle exhaustion in this environment.

C33 opens BASE.DBF and RESULT.OUT, then recursively DOs the same PROBE.PRG while public D<23. CONFIG.SYS FILES=40, CONFIG.DB STATUS=OFF/BELL=OFF; full input/runtime hashes retained. Real dBASE III PLUS 1.1 reaches D=12 and raises6 Too many files are open; it unwinds and saves. InitechBase reaches D=19 and raises103 DOs nested too deep; it unwinds and saves. Do not infer that real III+ has a12-level general DO limit: the existing independent do-file-mint/depth/GOLD.OUT demonstrates procedure-library recursion reaches19 then error103. Disk nesting plus these open files is the concrete differing scenario.

Capture CASES=C33 sh apps/initechbase/tests/conformance/capture.sh /absolute/empty/output on real DOS3.30/III+1.1/QEMU486/8MiB. No hangs or damaged tables observed, only visible limit/error mismatch. title: Desktop smoke can lose selecting mouse events and relaunch the previous app under load
description:
factory/emu/qemu.c:1568-1574 and factory/desktop-trace.sh:49: the desktop smoke queues Finder l1,l0,kctrl-o after an app exits, relying on a 40 ms QMP drain for mouse delivery. During the phase-2 shared build load on the unchanged driver, selection of WORD.EXE was not delivered: qemu.serial shows 123 exiting, then cursor (146,258), then Ctrl-O, with no intervening mouseDown; the still-selected 123.EXE launches again. The wait for FLAIR-DISPATCH app=WORD then fails correctly. This makes the acceptance journey unreliable under contention, not a demonstrated Finder label fault.

Reproducer: at commit 3e6b4e8e9dbd82d91a85ed843af5870c12784526 run nice -n 10 sh factory/smoke-desktop.sh while the shared phase-2 builds are active (observed load 40+ on 12 CPUs). Original trace output retained in phase2/desktop-evidence/desktop-qemu.serial and desktop-qemu.report. Around serial lines 481-489, no selecting mouseDown arrives after the exit. Script exits 1 waiting for Word.

A diagnostic copy which only adds 250 ms holds around Finder single selections (l1,w250,l0,w250,kctrl-o), preserving the initial volume/folder double-click timing, successfully selects and launches WORD.EXE at the same icon position. Its full results and exact three-line script diff are retained in phase2/desktop-evidence/desktop-select-paced.*. Do not globally delay all mouse transitions: that breaks the initial double-click interval.

Factory owner should synchronize selecting mouse delivery with guest progress (or otherwise prove delivery under contention), preserving double-click semantics and all existing marker/readback checks. No factory source was edited by the desktop implementer. Final quiet-machine smoke is still required before landing.

title: InitechBase refuses a cut-off NDX page which dBASE III+ reads and repairs
description:
InitechBase refuses a cut-off NDX page which dBASE III+ reads and repairs

P1. apps/initechbase/fs/ndx.c:334 requires physical file size divisible by 512 and :388 requires total_pages==physical_size/512. It refuses an otherwise readable partial final page before examining its entries.

C22: OLD.NDX header says root=1, pages=2, C8 key KEY, group length16, capacity31. Its leaf contains 3 valid entries A/B/C->1/2/3 and trailing child0, but the physical file ends at byte600 rather than1024; all used node bytes are present. BASE.DBF contains the matching intact 3 records. USE BASE INDEX OLD; LIST OFF; GO BOTTOM; SEEK 'AAAAAAAA'; REINDEX; GO BOTTOM; REPLACE VALUE WITH 9; close/copy.

Real III+ opens it, lists all three records, seeks successfully, REINDEX succeeds and leaves a full index (independent NDX readback retained). InitechBase returns error15 Not a dBASE database and the guarded program skips access, leaving the stale short index. This is a recoverable disk-full index, not a demand to accept arbitrary corrupt nodes.

title: InitechBase truncates displayed memos at its 512-byte output buffer
description:
InitechBase truncates displayed memos at its 512-byte output buffer

P1. apps/initechbase/cmd/query.c:903 uses one Q_LINEBUF=512 buffer for the entire ? statement, including wrapped memo lines; q_render_val at :275 renders all lines into it and q_append at :200 silently drops bytes after the cap. apps/initechbase/cmd/workarea.c:903 independently truncates memo values to WA_MEMO_BUF_CAP=2048.

C16 is 511 bytes of text with its 1A1A terminator crossing a block boundary. C17 has 2300 text bytes with normal terminator, next-free 6. USE BASE; GO TOP; ? VALUE; REPLACE KEY WITH 'SAVED'; close/copy. Real dBASE III PLUS 1.1 displays the whole text (C16 has 550 padded content-column bytes; C17 has 2300). InitechBase emits only 492 content-column bytes in each case, then BOTTOM/SAVE/END as if successful. The accepted LEN(VALUE) probe additionally exposes C17's 2048-byte resolve cap (real rejects LEN(memo), tracked separately).

The DBT bytes are unchanged by these programs, so no overwritten memo is alleged: P1 visible missing content. title: Kernel replace primitive: commit a staged file over an existing name in one directory-sector write
description:
Needed for the safe-save ruling (phase 2, ruling 1): after any failure an app reports, the previous file still opens under its own name. With DOS calls alone (write temp, rename old to backup, rename temp to old, delete backup) a double failure (final rename fails and the restore rename fails) leaves the previous version only under its backup name. The Toolbox save path (initech-vtl9) lands with that residual case reported honestly; this primitive closes it.

Specification: a kernel file-layer operation replace(staged, dest) on one volume and directory whose single commit point is one directory-sector write: the destination entry is repointed to the staged file's cluster chain, size and time in one sector write; only after that write succeeds is the old chain freed and the staging entry removed. Any failure before the commit leaves dest byte-identical; failures after it leave dest = new bytes and at worst a leaked chain or stray staging entry, which CHKDSK reports and which never loses user data. Cross-directory and cross-volume are refused. Red-first tests: fault injection at every sector write, independent mtools/fsck readback, cluster-conservation invariant (initech-rg6d5's).

Then the Toolbox owner switches tbx_file_save and FILE COPY's commit to it (how the Toolbox reaches the kernel follows the existing file binding; do not widen the open two-interface question, initech-q9p80). Order: after initech-rg6d5 lands.
