title: Finder file operations write a FAT16 volume through the FAT12 writer with no type check
description:
Found by the phase-2 FAT16/interface analysis (P2/analysis-fat16-interfaces.md, B7) and checked by the orchestrator at 09d52a32.

The DOS file layer refuses every mutation on a non-FAT12 volume (kernel/fileio_fat.c:254 and siblings: fat_type != FAT_TYPE_FAT12 -> ACCESS_DENIED). The Finder bypasses that layer and calls the FAT12 writer directly: mkdir flair/desktop/finder_actions.c:20, move :47, unlink :87, rmdir :96, create :107, positioned write :150; Desktop DB create/write flair/desktop/desktop_db.c:117ff. Its only guard, finder_fat_geometry_ok() at flair/desktop/volumes.c:29, checks sectors-per-cluster, never fat_type. A FAT16 volume mounts with a two-sector window and fat_len 0 (kernel/fileio_fat.c:951).

Scenario: the Finder's current volume is FAT16 (a FAT16 working volume, today readable). New Folder, a drag/move, Put Away/Empty Trash or a Desktop DB save then runs fat12_* with 12-bit packing against a 16-bit FAT and a zero-length FAT buffer. Expected: refused like INT 21h (Access denied / write-protect), disk unchanged. Actual: untested; at best a misleading error, at worst 12-bit entries written into a FAT16 FAT.

Fix whatever GM2's FAT16 ruling turns out to be: enforce the volume write capability below the Finder (as the analysis recommends), with a red-first test that mounts an mtools-built FAT16 image, performs each Finder mutation, and checks the image is byte-identical. Interim owner: flair/desktop.

title: CREAT and CREATE_NEW report handle exhaustion when the fixed root directory is full
description:
Reviewed main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. P1 wrong DOS error on ordinary directory exhaustion.

kernel/fileio_fat.c:269-270 maps FAT12_ERR_DIR_FULL from CREAT to TOO_MANY_OPEN (4). Fill all 224 fixed-root entries on an otherwise empty 1.44M floppy. AH=3Ch or 5Bh for a new filename returns CF=1 AX=4, although JFT/SFT slots and all data clusters are free. Real MS-DOS 3.30 returns CF=1 AX=5 for both. Reproducer source, captured bytes, DOS boot/data disks and replay script retained beside review-kernel.md in kernel-repro/. No root-growth feature is requested; this corrects the error returned by an existing bounded refusal. Root-full refusal itself leaves the disk unchanged.

title: Turbo Initech div/mod of minimum Integer by -1 halts the OS
description:
Reviewed 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c. P1; no evidence that the present compiler source/self-host fixed point is affected.

Both compilers emit unguarded 32-bit CDQ/IDIV for div and mod: turbo/seed/codegen.c:1263-1270 and turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:3002-3011. Signed minimum / -1 overflows the x86 quotient even when Pascal only requests the exactly representable remainder zero. A legal accepted program halts the entire product with PANIC vec=00 err=00000000 / HALTED.

Smallest tested modulo program:
```pascal
{$mode delphi}{$B+}{$H-}
program ModMin;
var a,b: integer;
begin
 a:=-2147483647-1; b:=-1;
 writeln(a mod b); writeln('done')
end.
```
Independent FPC 3.2.2 (`fpc -Mtp -B -O-`, source corpus directives select Delphi/B+/H- and 32-bit Integer): `0`, then `done`. Direct seed EXE, FPC-hosted Turbo native EXE, and resident Turbo native EXE on QEMU: no Pascal output; `PANIC vec=00 err=00000000`, `HALTED`. The resident transcript includes TURBO-GEN-OK and TURBO-NATIVE-OK before executing the defective result. Also reproduced for `q:=a div b; writeln(q)` (q declared Integer); FPC prints -2147483648 then done; all three product paths halt. Neither divisor is zero. The documented arithmetic wrap rule is retained (operator ruling 7); this is not a request to use 16-bit Integer.

Reproducers are turbo/tests/review-phase2/mod_min.pas and div_min.pas on branch t3/review-turbo-defects. Existing differential harness accepts TURBO_EXEC_SOURCES=<path>, TURBO_EXEC_PATHS='seed hosted resident', TURBO_EXEC_EMULATORS=qemu, TURBO_EXEC_OUT=<separate output> sh turbo/tests/execution/run.sh. Run each path in isolation: panic prevents remaining batch cases from executing. Use an external timeout: the QEMU driver was observed not to retire promptly after HALTED and some fault runs were explicitly killed after serial capture. This driver behavior is not the basis of the defect: the serial CPU exception is.

Full report/evidence: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2/review-turbo.md and review-turbo-evidence/.

title: FAT backend reports existing-file media read errors as FILE_NOT_FOUND
description:
Reviewed main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. P1 media errors misreported as filename absence.

kernel/fileio_fat.c:129-132 and :169-171 collapse a directory read error or file data read error into DOS FILE_NOT_FOUND (2). Open a healthy 19-byte TARGET.BIN, then make its next disk read fail. AH=3Fh on the valid handle returns CF=1 AX=2; AH=59h then also records the wrong class of failure via the dispatch wrapper. The file still exists with identical bytes. OPEN/FINDFIRST/parent resolution have similar lossy mappings. A READ failure within write_at is separately hard-coded as WRITE_FAULT at :302; exact call/extended-error mapping should be established rather than treating all errors alike.

Reference: IBM DOS 3.30 Technical Reference printed pp.6-137/138 (READ error via AX and 59h), p.6-42 (2=file not found,30=read fault,31=general failure). Exact primary AX after INT24 Fail should be captured before fixing; the demonstrated defect is the invented absence, not an asserted universal primary AX=30.

Reproducer: reports/phase2/kernel-repro/dos_probe.c and run-dos.sh. dos-probe readerr-1.img readerr 1 with mtools-created existing file: OPEN CF=0 AX=5; READ CF=1 AX=2; read_fault=1. No-fault control reads AX=1, and independent mtools readback preserves all 19 original bytes.

title: WRITE acknowledges bytes after a failed SFT refresh, then the same handle reports false EOF
description:
Reviewed main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. P1 successful WRITE followed by false EOF on the same handle.

kernel/fileio_fat.c:316-322 ignores failure of the final directory refresh and returns success. The caller in kernel/int21.c:1136,1157 retains its old size/start snapshot. Start with an empty TARGET.BIN, OPEN read/write, WRITE 512 X bytes; fail exactly the read used to refresh the SFT after the data/FAT/directory writes have succeeded. AH=40h returns CF=0 AX=512. Seek to offset 0 and READ 512 on THAT SAME handle returns CF=0 AX=0, while mtools reads all 512 X bytes from disk. SEEK-from-end similarly consults stale size. No second-open sharing policy is involved. A caller copying that acknowledged file can accept/save an empty document.

Reference: IBM DOS 3.30 Technical Reference printed pp.6-137/138 (AX=0 denotes EOF), pp.6-139/140,6-143; known requested bytes independently read by mtools. The backend must either return an error or provide valid updated metadata for a successful write.

Reproducer: reports/phase2/kernel-repro/dos_probe.c, run-dos.sh; fresh mtools-created empty TARGET.BIN; dos-probe refresh-4.img refresh 4. Actual: OPEN success; WRITE CF=0 AX=512; SEEK CF=0 AX=0; READ CF=0 AX=0; read_fault=1. Control refresh 0 returns READ AX=512. int21_file_stamp is unbound in this harness, so the fourth read is exactly the final refresh (a bound clock changes only its ordinal).

title: MKDIR rollback leaves unequal FATs and an orphan when its parent did not grow
description:
Reviewed main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. P1 on-disk orphan and FAT divergence after a recoverable write fault.

kernel/fat12.c:3841-3858, fat12_mkdir: on own-cluster FAT-flush failure the new cluster is freed only in memory. A rollback flush happens only indirectly when parent_grew is true. On the fixed root, or any nonfull parent, parent_grew is false: failure writing FAT copy 2 leaves the first FAT with an allocated EOC cluster and the second FAT with FREE. No directory entry is ever published. The disk retains the leak after process exit/reboot even though the one-shot fault has cleared.

Reference: FAT-copy agreement and cluster ownership, independently checked by fsck.fat -n. This is a missing existing rollback leg, not a request for journaling.

Reproducer: reports/phase2/kernel-repro/fat_probe.c and run-fat.sh; mformat a blank 1.44M image, fat-probe mkdir-2.img mkdir 2. Actual rc=-10 fault=1 writes=2. fsck.fat -n: FATs differ but appear to be intact; Reclaimed 1 unused cluster (512 bytes). Control mkdir 0 creates a clean directory; mkdir 1 fails before any disk allocation and leaves a clean disk. Existing test_fat12_fault_rollback scenario C tests a full/grown parent and misses this branch.

title: FAT12 positioned extension leaks allocations after late FAT, data, or directory faults
description:
Reviewed main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. P1 persistent allocation loss / FAT-copy divergence.

kernel/fat12.c:2978-2980 commits a newly allocated extension and returns immediately on a FAT flush error; :3048-3049 and :3074-3081 also return on data/directory I/O failure without detaching/freeing that extension. Empty TARGET.BIN, 1024-byte WRITE: two clusters are allocated and zeroed, then either FAT copy, the payload writes, or the directory publication fails once. The call reports error while allocated clusters remain unowned by any directory entry. Repeated retries consume the disk; failing FAT copy 2 also leaves unequal FATs. With failure on copy 1, dirty in-memory allocation survives despite neither disk FAT reflecting it, and a later unrelated flush can publish the leak.

This is distinct from initech-rg6d5: no existing file is unlinked or truncated; allocation during ordinary AH=40h extension leaks.

Reference: Microsoft FAT ownership/chain invariants, independently graded by fsck.fat and mtools; not a claim of crash atomicity or unchanged old payload on failed in-place overwrite.

Reproducer: retained reports/phase2/kernel-repro/fat_probe.c and run-fat.sh. Run fat-probe partial-5.img partial 5 on a freshly mtools-created empty TARGET.BIN. Actual rc=-10 wrote=0 fault=1; fsck.fat -n: Reclaimed 2 unused clusters (1024 bytes), while TARGET.BIN still has size/start 0. Faults 4,6,7 also leak; 4 additionally reports FATs differ. Control fault 0 is clean, size 1024, two owned clusters. Directory-commit fault 7 reports out_written=1024 despite rc=-10; DOS backend resets it to zero.

Rollback should cover the complete allocation-to-publication interval and both FAT copies, with separately tested persistent rollback failure. Retained disk images preserve the evidence.

title: Region merge exhausts output before redundant bands are normalized
description:
Targeted Toolbox review of main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. No product changes.

flair/region/region.c:473 (also :488, normalization only at :491) emits every source y boundary into out before collapsing equal bands. region_push_row checks row and pool capacity at :95-96. This aborts a valid Boolean operation even when the final normal form fits the supplied output exactly. Source of truth: flair/region/include/region_algebra.h section 5 explicitly defines storage failure in terms of the region's normal form; union-of-sets identity is independent of implementation.

Concrete reproducer: A=[0,10)x[0,10), B=[0,10)x[5,15). Both are normalized two-row rectangles. Their union is the rectangle [0,10)x[0,15), exactly two rows/two pool entries. A larger output produces two rows/two entries, establishing this is not genuine result exhaustion. The same premature checks affect row capacity and x_pool capacity independently.

Reproducer retained at P2/toolbox-probes/region-window.c; run P2/toolbox-probes/run.sh <repo-root>. P2 is /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2. Output: CONTROL union normalized rows=2 pool=2; DEFECT exact-cap union signal=6. Larger constructions can exhaust the production 32-row/128-entry tenant region despite a much simpler final result; no emulator witness for that integration consequence is claimed.

Repair direction: collapse equal/leading empty bands before consuming destination capacity, as region_from_rects already does. Add independent exact-cap union/intersection/difference tests, separately limiting rows and pool; preserve genuine exhaustion fail-loud probes. Do not increase caps to conceal intermediate growth.

title: Turbo Initech seed compiler local record arrays overwrite preceding locals
description:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: turbo/
Source report: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/review-turbo.md
Current file:line evidence and retained reproduction inputs/stdout/exit records were read and checked. No builds, make targets, emulators or tests were rerun during this filing. Earlier executions below are attributed to the reviewer.

Source finding: review-turbo.md #3

## Evidence
turbo/seed/codegen.c:2307 places element zero/field zero at the highest allocated address. gen_elem_addr at :978-982 subtracts element strides. gen_designator_is_local_frame at :1101-1102 returns false for every indexed designator, so gen_field_addr at :1119 adds the field offset into preceding frame storage. The normalization claim at :1013-1017 is inconsistent with that allocation. The Pascal compiler correctly treats SkLocalArray as descending at turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:2858-2862.

## Failing scenario
Writing r[1].b changes sentinel from 777 to 12. P1: direct seed-generated writes corrupt unrelated caller-frame storage. An array declared first could reach the saved frame word; that consequence is inferred, not demonstrated. The Pascal compiler passes this particular probe.

## Failing program
```pascal
program probe;
type Pair = record a,b: integer; end;
procedure Run(dummy: integer);
var sentinel: integer; r: array[1..2] of Pair;
begin
  sentinel := 777;
  r[1].a := 11; r[1].b := 12;
  r[2].a := 21; r[2].b := 22;
  writeln(r[1].a, ' ', r[1].b, ' ', r[2].a, ' ', r[2].b, ' ', sentinel)
end;
begin Run(0) end.
```

## Expected versus actual
| Execution | Output |
|---|---|
| FPC TP | `11 12 21 22 777` |
| Seed | `11 12 21 22 12` |
| Turbo | `11 12 21 22 777` |

Retained evidence: /tmp/turbo-defect-review/local-record-array/input.pas, reference.stdout (reference-longint.stdout for #4), seed.stdout/turbo.stdout and seed-exit/turbo-exit where generated. For #2 seed-build.log records rejection.

## Source of truth
Independent execution of the reproduction with Free Pascal in TP mode, as retained under /tmp/turbo-defect-review. CLAUDE.md constitution: The oracle is the truth; show the differential red before the fix. GOLDEN-MASTER item 7.

## Proposed fix
Recognize indexed local arrays when choosing the seed field-offset direction, including whole-record copies using this helper. Recheck global arrays and local/global copies. Coordinate with the var-record layout defect rather than treating this direct-access fix as a complete ABI repair.

## Red-first differential test and acceptance
Before fixing, execute direct seed output and compare the exact program stdout to fpc -Mtp: red must show final sentinel 12 versus 777. Keep Pascal Turbo Initech as a passing control. Extend gen_local_record_array with a preceding live sentinel, negative lower bounds, direct fields and whole-record copies. The existing fixture can conceal the overwrite because its function-result slot precedes the array but is assigned later. A Pascal-only smoke cannot detect this seed-only path.

Track shared execution coverage in existing task initech-h5uk7. Keep tier 0 emulator-free; use a suitable host runtime or the product-image tier-1/2 runner.

## Evidence limits
The reviewer used FPC 3.2.2, fpc -Mtp -B -O- -v0 references and a scratch-built C seed / FPC-hosted Pascal Turbo Initech compiler. Seed/Turbo results are executions of their emitted x86 assembly, linked with unchanged Multiboot startup and run under QEMU at 8 MiB. They do not verify resident loading/file runtime or native instruction encoding. Debug-exit status 1 denotes successful completion here; 124 denotes timeout. No product-image or self-host/DDC run is claimed. K2 == K3 alone cannot establish correctness of shared translation semantics.

title: Turbo Initech var char writes overwrite following string characters
description:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: turbo/
Source report: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/review-turbo.md
Current file:line evidence and retained reproduction inputs/stdout/exit records were read and checked. No builds, make targets, emulators or tests were rerun during this filing. Earlier executions below are attributed to the reviewer.

Source finding: review-turbo.md #2

## Evidence
turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:3764-3770 accepts indexed string characters as char lvalues. ParseCall at :3401-3406 requests the address for a var formal. ParseAssignment at :4401-4404 emits a byte store only for an indexed string symbol; a char formal instead emits mov [edx], eax. Char reads at :3849-3854 use movzx byte only for directly indexed strings, otherwise a dword load. The C seed independently rejects this documented actual argument: turbo/seed/typecheck.c:1103-1110 requires a real array for an indexed var actual and :1115-1123 diagnoses it. Its generic var loads/stores are dword accesses at turbo/seed/codegen.c:1480-1483 and :1782-1785. The report cited typecheck.c:1111; the exact rejection condition is :1110, confirmed in the current tree.

## Failing scenario
The Pascal compiler accepts Change(s[1]) but changing one character clears three following characters. P1: generated code corrupts adjacent bytes. The seed rejects the program rather than exhibiting that write corruption. A read-only char formal reading adjacent bytes as high bits is inferred from the load emitter, not executed in this review.

## Failing program
```pascal
program probe;
var s: string;
procedure Change(var c: char);
begin c := 'Z' end;
begin s := 'ABCD'; Change(s[1]);
  writeln(ord(s[1]), ' ', ord(s[2]), ' ', ord(s[3]), ' ', ord(s[4]))
end.
```

## Expected versus actual
| Execution | Output |
|---|---|
| FPC TP | `90 66 67 68` |
| Seed | compile error: var argument requires variable, array element, or field |
| Turbo | `90 0 0 0` |

Retained evidence: /tmp/turbo-defect-review/string-var-char/input.pas, reference.stdout (reference-longint.stdout for #4), seed.stdout/turbo.stdout and seed-exit/turbo-exit where generated. For #2 seed-build.log records rejection.

## Source of truth
Independent execution of the reproduction with Free Pascal in TP mode, as retained under /tmp/turbo-defect-review. CLAUDE.md constitution: The oracle is the truth; show the differential red before the fix. GOLDEN-MASTER item 7. The archived programmer guide explicitly permits a string character as a var actual at attic/pubs/manuals/turbo-initech-programmers-guide/ch07-routines.tex:77-80.

## Proposed fix
Make var-char loads/stores byte-safe for every supported actual argument and preserve zero extension, forwarding and alias identity. A one-store change can leave high garbage bits in dword char slots read later. Align the seed acceptance path with the documented string-character var argument.

## Red-first differential test and acceptance
First execute this write probe through Pascal Turbo Initech and compare to fpc -Mtp: the comparison must be red (90 0 0 0 versus 90 66 67 68). Assert seed acceptance separately; it is currently red with a var-argument diagnostic. Add read-only ord(c), forwarding/aliasing, scalar/record/array chars, and the final character of string[4] with adjacent live storage. Extend gen_string_deep/gen_func_deep and execute generated programs, checking every neighboring byte.

Track shared execution coverage in existing task initech-h5uk7. Keep tier 0 emulator-free; use a suitable host runtime or the product-image tier-1/2 runner.

## Evidence limits
The reviewer used FPC 3.2.2, fpc -Mtp -B -O- -v0 references and a scratch-built C seed / FPC-hosted Pascal Turbo Initech compiler. Seed/Turbo results are executions of their emitted x86 assembly, linked with unchanged Multiboot startup and run under QEMU at 8 MiB. They do not verify resident loading/file runtime or native instruction encoding. Debug-exit status 1 denotes successful completion here; 124 denotes timeout. No product-image or self-host/DDC run is claimed. K2 == K3 alone cannot establish correctness of shared translation semantics.

title: Turbo Initech and seed compiler corrupt caller locals through var record parameters
description:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: turbo/
Source report: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/review-turbo.md
Current file:line evidence and retained reproduction inputs/stdout/exit records were read and checked. No builds, make targets, emulators or tests were rerun during this filing. Earlier executions below are attributed to the reviewer.

Source finding: review-turbo.md #1

## Evidence
turbo/seed/codegen.c:2312 allocates field zero of a local record at the highest address. gen_designator_is_local_frame at :1098-1104 excludes CG_VARPARAM; gen_field_addr at :1116-1119 subtracts field offsets for direct locals but adds for var parameters. gen_designator_base_addr at :1073-1084 and gen_addr_of/gen_call at :1876/:1987 forward the same address without layout information. turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:2257 allocates descending locals; GenDesignatorAddress at :2796-2800 forwards a var pointer; GenApplyField at :2858-2864 subtracts direct-local offsets but adds through var formals.

## Failing scenario
Both compilers accept Change(r), then r.b := 99 writes the caller sentinel rather than r.b. Neighboring-local corruption is demonstrated. If the record is first in the frame, the same positive offset can reach the saved-frame word; that risk is inferred from the allocator, not demonstrated by this probe. P1: accepted input generates memory-corrupting writes.

## Failing program
```pascal
program probe;
type Pair = record a,b: integer; end;
procedure Change(var r: Pair);
begin r.b := 99 end;
procedure Run(dummy: integer);
var sentinel: integer; r: Pair;
begin
  sentinel := 777; r.a := 11; r.b := 22;
  Change(r);
  writeln(r.a, ' ', r.b, ' ', sentinel)
end;
begin Run(0) end.
```

## Expected versus actual
| Execution | Output |
|---|---|
| FPC TP | `11 99 777` |
| Seed | `11 22 99` |
| Turbo | `11 22 99` |

Retained evidence: /tmp/turbo-defect-review/local-record/input.pas, reference.stdout (reference-longint.stdout for #4), seed.stdout/turbo.stdout and seed-exit/turbo-exit where generated. For #2 seed-build.log records rejection.

Use a consistent physical record field direction across globals, locals, local-array elements, whole-record copies and forwarded var parameters. Changing only var-parameter offsets breaks global arguments. Preserve alias identity; copy-in/copy-out is not equivalent.

The reviewer used FPC 3.2.2, fpc -Mtp -B -O- -v0 references and a scratch-built C seed / FPC-hosted Pascal Turbo Initech compiler. Seed/Turbo results are executions of their emitted x86 assembly, linked with unchanged Multiboot startup and run under QEMU at 8 MiB. They do not verify resident loading/file runtime or native instruction encoding. Debug-exit status 1 denotes successful completion here; 124 denotes timeout. No product-image or self-host/DDC run is claimed. K2 == K3 alone cannot establish correctness of shared translation semantics.

title: InitechDOS DUP returns the wrong AX and aliases invalid handles
description:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: kernel/
Source findings: review-interfaces.md #4
Reports: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports
Evidence checked by reading the current tree. No make, emulator, mutation or test run was performed during this triage. Reported earlier experiments are attributed, not repeated.

## Evidence
kernel/int21.c:1731 narrows EBX and :1739 replaces AL only; :1749-1751 narrows both DUP2 operands.

## Failing scenario
DUP(5) returns AX=4506h, so a normal caller cannot use AX as its next handle. BX=0105h or CX=0101h aliases valid handles and mutates tables instead of returning error 6.

## Source of truth
MS-DOS 3.3 Programmer's Reference AH=45h/46h: AX contains new handle; invalid operands return error 6. Existing flat ABI validates full EBX on other handle calls.

## Proposed fix
Validate full operands before byte conversion and use set_ax for DUP success.

## Red-first test and acceptance
Assert exact AX=6, CF clear for valid duplicate; EBX/ECX 0100h-0113h and large 32-bit operands must return CF/error6 with unchanged JFT/SFT.
close_reason: Fixed 3ee85331. DUP returns complete AX; DUP/DUP2 validate full operands before narrowing. Independent handle/table conservation tests red then green in /tmp/initechdos-fix-logs/handles-{red,green}.log. Kernel suite and DOS/program smoke green.

title: F11 Local sentinel: tools/sentinel.sh post-push detached worktree runs the diff-scoped set then tools/cert-sharded.sh at bounded -j; tools/culprit.sh re-runs a red gate across first-parent merges since the last green cert
description: sentinel.sh: on demand or after push (git hook post-push via a local alias, NOT GitHub CI), creates/reuses a detached worktree ../initech-os-sentinel at origin/main, runs make test-for DIFF=<last-green>..HEAD, then cert-sharded.sh -j <bounded, default 8> with a load guard (skip/defer when loadavg > N, log it); writes build/sentinel/<sha>/{summary,gates.log}; records last-green SHA. culprit.sh <gate>: re-runs the gate on each first-parent merge commit since the last green SHA (temp worktrees), prints the first red merge. title: Stop interrupted TYPE and DIR before consuming invalid syscall results
description: Root cause: os/milton/int21.c:5392 invokes INT 23h and returns before servicing the interrupted call; int21.c:5337 only sets the resident recovery latch. os/milton/command.c:2797 treats the unchanged AH=3Fh request register as a read count, and :2809 writes that count from a 128-byte stack buffer without testing the latch or bounding got. Thus an interrupted read can turn EAX=0x3F00 into 16128 output bytes. command.c:2741 ignores the same latch after the DIR /P key wait and :2766 continues enumeration. Ground truth: MS-DOS 3.3 User's Guide, Reference printed p.159 / PDF244 (evidence/manual-page-244.txt); ADR-0003 DEC-16 Fork A; PRD 6.1. Cancellation must not manufacture file bytes. Acceptance oracle and mutant: Extend harness/diff/fat_diff/test_dos_break.c and the INT21 host seam with Ctrl-C at read, write and DIR pause boundaries. Verify CLOSE and all stdin/stdout restoration paths. Replay controlshort and gaps2 on copied disks under QEMU, require an immediate usable prompt, no later HUGE/F299 lines and zero non-file bytes; also redirect TYPE and compare the committed prefix independently. Add a mutant that omits the interrupted check or permits got > sizeof(chunk); it must fail the byte-boundary and cancellation checks. Scope: Keep child-program INT 23h termination intact. This is a returning resident-call completion bug, not another request to add BREAK ON checkpoints (initech-bsy.4). title: Keep GUI command keys out of the DOS Control-Break input path
description: B01. Root cause: os/milton/kbd.c:351 queues each key in the DOS cooked ring before :364 also posts it to FLAIR; :254 translates Ctrl-C to 03h. os/milton/int21.c:5389 polls that stale byte for BREAK ON and :5392 invokes INT23, whose default terminates at :5341. The desktop itself polls DOS time at os/milton/kmain.c:7412. This is shared input ownership, not a failing Scrap put. Ground truth: CLAUDE.md Rule 2 does not authorize killing a GUI session for Copy; the local Macintosh System Software Users Guide V6.0, printed pp.125 and 152, describes accessory/document clipboard work. spec/toolbox_gate.h Sec 12 defines the Scrap seam; ADR-0003 Amendment DEC-16 governs the DOS break checkpoints. Scope: Give the active GUI and DOS console explicit input ownership across entry, exit and SAMIR suspension. Consume GUI chords once; preserve authentic DOS Ctrl-C and extended-key/typeahead behavior when DOS owns input. Do not fix this by globally disabling BREAK or removing INT23. Acceptance oracle: Extend keyboard/ring and INT21 host ownership tests, then lock copybreak in QEMU and a Bochs leg: Copy, idle through a clock poll, Paste, drag, close and relaunch must work with no INT23-BREAK/INT21-EXIT. A restored dual-ring leak mutant must terminate/fail this oracle; DOS prompt and child Ctrl-C controls must still pass. Record a record-flair clip. title: Initech SideKick: the Borland SideKick (1984-ish, v1.5x) Initech-version -- a DOS TSR desk-accessory set (notepad, calculator, calendar/appointments, ASCII table, phone dialer) popped by a hotkey over any InitechDOS program
description: Operator directive 2026-10-17: 'implement a version of borland sidekick. call it initech sidekick.' Period reference: Borland SideKick for the IBM PC (1984; the 1.5x releases ship on DOS 3.3 era machines) -- the first mass-market TSR: SIDEKICK (SK.COM) stays resident, Ctrl-Alt (or a configured hotkey) pops its menu bar over the running program, with the Notepad (WordStar-style keys, up to a 4000-byte file), Calculator (decimal/hex/binary, paper-tape), Calendar + Appointment book, ASCII table, Phone dialer/directory, and the main menu (F1..F8). This is the InitechDOS side of the house (MILTON, not FLAIR): it exercises the DOS TSR mechanics the kernel must grow -- INT 21h AH=31h Keep Process (TSR) with a resident size, INT 09h/16h keyboard hook for the hotkey, INT 28h idle and the InDOS flag for safe pop-up, INT 10h/direct text-mode screen save/restore (the 4000-byte 80x25 save-under), INT 8/1Ch tick for the clock; all on the DEC-08 flat .COM model (no v8086; the resident part is a flat-32 image kept by AH=31h, PRD Sec 6 / ADR-0003 Appendix A). Deliverables (each a sub-bead, RED first, Law 1 ground truth before code): (1) RESEARCH: docs/research/SIDEKICK-period-grounding.md -- the SideKick 1.5x manual/screens (acquire a period source locally: the manual scans or the SideKick reference card; the screen layouts of the menu bar, Notepad, Calculator with its paper tape, Calendar, ASCII table, Dialer; the keystrokes; the exact pop-up chord; the resident-size figure), with provenance; (2) KERNEL: TSR support in MILTON -- AH=31h keep with resident paragraph count, the InDOS flag + INT 28h idle hook, a keyboard-hook vector the resident can chain, screen save/restore primitives -- host oracle + emu gate + mutants; headroom budget respected; (3) SK.COM: the resident + pop-up with the six accessories mirroring the originals' screens (text mode, period box-drawing, the SideKick colour scheme as period-correct on CGA/mono/VGA), config file SK.CFG, the Notepad saving to a real file through INT 21h; (4) ORACLES: a host core suite for each accessory (calculator arithmetic vs an independent golden -- bc/the real SideKick under dosbox-x if a period binary can be sourced for differential, the Law-2 way; calendar maths vs cal(1); ASCII table vs the IBM code page 437 table), an emu gate that boots to DOS, runs a foreground program, pops SideKick by the hotkey, uses the Notepad and saves, pops down, and proves the foreground screen is byte-restored (screendump before == after) + mutants (hotkey ignored, screen not restored, TSR not kept); (5) MANUAL: the Initech SideKick Owner's Handbook under pubs/ mirroring the Borland manual's structure, gated like the other books (commands/keys inventory from the shipped binary, screens replayed), with the house slips; (6) FLAIR: no GUI work -- but SideKick must also pop over FLAIR's Exit-to-DOS shell and over TPSREP; (7) clips per Rule 14 for the pop-up over DOS. Sub-beads to be filed by the research lane after (1). Depends on nothing merged-pending; conflicts textually with the DPB and Finder lanes in kmain.c -- schedule after they merge.

title: I123 /Copy and /Move disagree with real 1-2-3 R2.2 on 5 of 8 minted pairs: ERR corners, 8-bit /Move column delta, wrap past column A / row 1, loaded 0xFFFF refs
description: Found 2026-10-16 by the cjot lane (merge 21cde96; goldens lotus123-decomp 51025ee: mint/COPY01.steps, MOVE01.steps, WRAP01.steps -> goldens/minted/COPY01A-D, MOVE01A-D, WRAP01A-C; ledger re/mint-results-002.md). test-i123-copy-move --corpus grades the artifact's i123_transfer against the real before/after .WK1 pairs through the independent readers (wk1_ref.py, wk1_formula_ref.py --bytes) and is RED on MOVE01B, MOVE01C, MOVE01D, WRAP01B, WRAP01C; green on COPY01B/C/D (relative, $A$1, $A1, A$1, ranges: /Copy never rewrites reference bytes). The manual-derived model (test-i123-copy-move-model) encodes the WRONG rules in four places; real R2.2 is the reference (Law 1), the model must follow it. Disagreements, with golden bytes: (1) /Move over a referenced cell: real keeps a VAR or RANGE corner with col and row words 0xFFFF (MOVE01B E1 = 01 ffff ffff 05 0100 09 03, shown +ERR+1 / +ERR / @SUM(ERR)); the artifact emits token 32 @ERR (06 00 20 05 01 00 09 03). (2) Relative column rewritten by /Move: real stores 0x8000|(delta&0xFF), e.g. fb80 for -5 (MOVE01C F5, MOVE01D, moved corner of G3); the artifact stores the 14-bit form fbbf. (3) /Copy past column A (WRAP01B, shown +IV1+1): real keeps ffbf; the artifact writes ff80. (4) /Copy past row 1 (WRAP01C, shown +A8192+1, value 1): real wraps the row and keeps ffbf ffbf; the artifact and the model turn it into @ERR (cached inf) -- the model's 'row < 0 is ERR' rule is wrong. (5) Loading: the artifact evaluates a real ERR reference VAR ffff ffff as relative -1,-1 (MOVE01C E2 cached 5.0, real is ERR) and a later /Move rewrites it to ffbf ffbf, losing the ERR marker; this affects ANY real .WK1 carrying 0xFFFF references, not just /Move. DONE MEANS: artifact (os/i123 transfer + codec + evaluator) matches all 8 pairs byte-for-byte on the meaningful bytes; the model in test_i123_copy_move.c is corrected to the real rules (and the lotus123-decomp spec distilled from the goldens is amended with the encodings, citing the golden bytes); test-i123-copy-move green and back in TEST_UNIT_GATES; a corpus-mode mutant (the existing test-i123-copy-move-mutant only runs model mode) proven RED; test-i123-copy-move-model/-mutant/-baseline, test-i123-* family and test-flair-i123-* emu gates green. title: L003: Give work-area tables independent allocation lifetimes
description: AUDIT L003 (docs/audits/2026-10-05-astra-full-drive/REPORT.md). SEEN: L003: No desktop return, prompt, or recovery followed. QMP still responded; the CPU snapshot had HLT=1 and interrupts disabled (EFL=0x93). The two-area mutation variant also hung. The single-area USE/LIST/QUIT control returned to FLAIR. EXPECTED: Independent work areas remain usable after another area closes; QUIT closes all handles and returns to the suspended desktop. Rejecting an unsupported duplicate open must happen before allocation/mutation and must not strand the process. ROOT CAUSE (triage): os/samir/samir_main.c:762 calls wa_close_all on QUIT. os/samir/cmd/workarea.c:675 closes areas in numeric order. dbf_close reaches os/samir/fs/dbf.c:249 teardown, which resets the SHARED PAL arena to the table mark at :257. After closing the first-opened area, the second table and its mark are beyond the new bump pointer. os/samir/pal/pal_milton.c:797 rejects that mark and :799 calls milton_panic; :126-131 executes cli; hlt. This explains the disabled-interrupt HLT snapshot; duplicate filenames are not required for this lifetime error. DONE MEANS: Separate persistent table/area storage from transient expression storage, using per-area arenas or a safe reclaim scheme. Close codec handles without rewinding across another live object; reclaim only when ownership proves it safe. Reversing numeric close order alone is not a fix: areas can open in any order and CLOSE can target an older area while a newer one remains live. Apply the ownership rule to DBF/DBT/NDX close and failure cleanup, not just QUIT. Add a strict PAL lifecycle oracle that poisons reclaimed bytes and enforces reset marks. Exercise opens 1->2 and 2->1, two distinct files and the same file, CLOSE/reopen of either area, indexes/memos and failed opens. Extend test_interp_use.c/test_samir_repl.c and PAL contract tests; target db_exit_probe.py must return to FLAIR after each case and then accept another app launch. Grounding: ../dbase3-decomp/specs/environment/work-areas-relations-and-limits.md:42 documents ten independent work areas. os/samir/include/samir/pal.h:185 explicitly says reset frees every allocation after the mark. ADR-0008/ADR-0009 define the shared engine/PAL, and PRD 6.6 grounds the hosted database. Clean process return is the OS lifetime expectation. See TRIAGE.md; source pinned to 50e084e.

title: L001: Make refused APPEND preserve a reopenable DBF
description: AUDIT L001 (docs/audits/2026-10-05-astra-full-drive/REPORT.md). SEEN: L001: The first nine appends worked. Later appends failed. RECCOUNT() still reported 12. After closing, USE could not reopen the table. Independent extraction found a 502-byte DBF with header count 21, header length 129 and record length 31: only 12 complete records exist, whereas the header requires 781 bytes including EOF. The original three rows remain in the bytes but the table is unusable through SAMIR. EXPECTED: A refused append leaves all prior records and the committed count consistent; close/reopen succeeds. In-memory table and work-area counts must describe committed records. ROOT CAUSE (triage): os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1517 increments tbl->nrec before persistence. os/samir/cmd/mutate.c:754 appends, then :760 flushes; :761 returns on failure without undoing the count. os/samir/fs/dbf.c:1319 serializes the new count and :1324 writes the header BEFORE :1361 writes the larger record region. A short or failed body write leaves the new header over the old short file; later attempts keep incrementing it. The work-area count is refreshed only after success at mutate.c:765, explaining RECCOUNT() staying 12 while the disk header reached 21. DONE MEANS: Add an append commit path that preserves the existing header geometry, reserves needed growth before publishing it, writes the new record/tail before the committed count, and restores in-memory nrec/cursor on refusal. A staged replacement is another option only if its failed allocation leaves the original untouched. Merely moving the header write in the whole-file rewrite is insufficient if an earlier write can damage old records or normalize +2 geometry. Stop subsequent mutations from flushing an uncommitted count. Keep the diagnostic repair in B02 separate. description:

SEEN: NOTES window has active chrome; the lower bar reads the Finder bar; a press at (196,28) drops Finder Special (Clean Up, Restart, Shut Down) over an apparently Notes-active desktop. Screenshots: docs/audits/2026-10-03-flair-gui-codex/shots/66-moved-volume-icon.png, 68-hidden-special-menu.png.

Screenshot 66 shows the bar is the FINDER bar 'File Edit View Special Help' and 196 lies ON its Special title. So the real defect is not an invisible hit zone; it is that the Finder bar stays up while a NOTES window is the active (hilited, front) window.
ROOT CAUSE (triage): by explicit design, no demotion when the last disk window closes (os/milton/kmain.c:3400-3402, flair_live_finder_foreground only ever PROMOTES). flair_live_do_finder_close and the FCMD_CLOSE_WINDOW arm (kmain.c:3282-3296, 3346-3354) call only finder_desk_repaint; process list head stays g_ten_finder, no FlairProcess_activate of the tenant owning the newly frontmost window, no DrawMenuBar. Band 2 hit-test resolves through flair_live_tenant_bar -> list->head->menubar (kmain.c:4478-4490), so it keeps answering as Finder. window.c DisposeWindow re-hilites NOTES (window.c:416-423) independently of the process list. Fix: after any Finder window close, activate the owner of the new frontmost visible window (reuse FlairProcess_activate + flair_live_finish_tenant_switch), or if no window remains keep Finder (period). Also ctrl-chords then route to NOTES correctly. Files: os/milton/kmain.c (finder close arms, flair_live_finder_foreground -> symmetric 'sync foreground to front window'), no change needed in finder_windows.c. comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text:
Independent desktop review, 2026-11-14; factory/emu/bochs.c:199-204 and :680. The fixed-port failure is still reachable when something outside the cooperative host lock occupies 5900. At desktop branch 3e6b4e8e9dbd82d91a85ed843af5870c12784526, run nice -n 10 make -j2 image, then DESKTOP_SMOKE_OUT=build/review-smoke-desktop nice -n 10 sh factory/smoke-desktop.sh while 5900 is occupied. The stock QEMU journey passes all nine exits/readbacks. After obtaining the host lock, this Bochs reports 'Trying port 5900 / Could not bind socket / Trying port 5901 / listening for connections on port 5901', followed by '[RFB] timeout! no client present'. The harness nevertheless says rfb_unblocked=1, rfb=720x530, serial_len=0, keys_sent=0, OK=0. Its child CPU never executes (EIP=0). The harness is connecting the listener on 5900 rather than its own emulator. A host-wide lock cannot exclude unrelated RFB/VNC users or uncooperative reference/mutation runs. Fail explicitly on a port collision, or bind/connect a verifiably owned endpoint. P1 acceptance-gate failure; outside the reviewed desktop diff.

Portable evidence: phase2/review-fix-desktop-evidence/bochs.bochs.log, bochs.bochsrc, bochs.report and review-desktop-smoke.log under the shared reports root. Original worktree logs: /home/tobias/.t3/worktrees/InitechOS/t3-84308dca-815ff318bf45a2b4/build/review-smoke-desktop/. This adds evidence to existing initech-d9tt rather than filing a duplicate.

comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text:
Reproduced the port-fallback failure in phase 2 on 2026-11-14, branch t3/123-worksheet-protection-saves HEAD 22b79bba, inherited factory/emu/bochs.c from 09d52a32. No factory changes in this branch.

Command: nice -n 15 make -j2 -C apps/initech123 smoke DESKTOP_JOURNEYS=<absolute file containing apps/initech123/tests/smoke>.

QEMU DOS smoke and independent mtools verification passed. The Bochs DOS prerequisite failed before any serial bytes or keys, after logging that another run held /tmp/initech-bochs.lock. Its Bochs log says: Trying port 5900; Could not bind socket; Trying port 5901; listening on port 5901; PANIC timeout! no client present. Meanwhile the harness report says launched=1 rfb_unblocked=1 timed_out=0 exit=1 serial_len=0 marker_found=0 keys_sent=0. This is a pre-boot RFB failure, not a guest/protection failure.

factory/emu/bochs.c:166 chooses the connect port, :202-204 ignores it when emitting the RFB config, :231 rfb_unblock connects the selected fixed port. Host flock remains present at :602 onward; evidence shows the port-fallback case can still occur on the current shared host. Other builders had Bochs runs active; no foreign process was interrupted or lock removed.

Evidence copied beside phase2/initech123.md in initech123-logs/: smoke.log, dos-bochs.report, dos-bochs.bochs.log, dos-bochs.bochsrc. An app-only desktop journey retry is being run independently to get the requested 123 QEMU/Bochs coverage without this earlier DOS prerequisite.

Factory owner: investigate this recurrence, ensure the harness detects/unblocks its own guest at the actual listening port, and preserve the pre-boot failure diagnostics. Reopen rather than duplicate the existing issue.

title: ref_tenant paints at its LAUNCH-time cached content rect forever: paint_content/accent_rect/marker_rect read p->content (open-time snapshot), so any moved tenant reconstructs content at the OLD position
description: Found 2026-07-31 landing Wave A (solid leg B went RED on the L-strip of the moved window). title: Makefile: SEVEN KERNEL_*_OBJ rules reference later-defined prereq vars (evaluate EMPTY at parse) -- region/heap/chrome/window/blitter/desktop/flair_shell .o not rebuilt on source edits (false-green incremental builds)
description: [Found during initech-jmc5] The rule for KERNEL_DESKTOP_OBJ (Makefile ~line 6976) lists prerequisites $(DESKTOP_C)/$(DESKTOP_H)/$(REGION_ENGINE_H), all defined LATER in the file (~10031/9050). GNU Make expands prerequisite lists immediately at parse time, so they evaluate EMPTY -> editing os/flair/desktop.c does NOT trigger a rebuild of build/desktop.o; make silently reports 'up to date' and the kernel links a STALE desktop.o. A real false-green hazard (kin to the clock-skew gotcha). Workaround used during jmc5: rm -f build/*desktop*.o before rebuilds. FIX: move the DESKTOP_C/DESKTOP_H/REGION_ENGINE_H definitions above the KERNEL_DESKTOP_OBJ rule (or use := late-bound correctly / literal paths). Audit other KERNEL_*_OBJ rules for the same late-var-reference pattern.
notes: SCOPE WIDENED by audit 2026-07-09 (was desktop.o only). Verified via make -rpn: build/region.o prereqs = 'spec/region_algebra.h | build' (MISSING region.c AND region.h -- the PRD-6.2 load-bearing math); build/heap.o has ZERO source prereqs; build/chrome.o missing chrome.c/chrome.h. Cause: GNU Make expands PREREQUISITE lists immediately at parse time; REGION_ENGINE_C etc. are defined ~2000 lines after use (Makefile ~7105-7145 vs ~9261+). The comment at Makefile:7100-7101 conflates deferred RECIPE expansion (true) with prereq expansion (false) -- delete it. Fix: move the var defs above first use, or use literal paths like the menu/control/dialog rules already do. Oracles unaffected (test_region compiles sources directly; test-kernel-repro force-rm's objects) -- this is a dev-loop/shipped-image integrity bug: editing region.c + incremental make relinks a STALE kernel.
close_reason: Fixed 8 object rules (the audited 7 + KERNEL_WINDOW_MUT_OVERLAY_OBJ found by full-file audit): late-defined prereq vars replaced with literal paths matching the menu/control/dialog idiom; misleading Makefile:7100 comment rewritten to distinguish recipe vs prereq expansion. Verified first-person: make -rpn shows full prereqs on all 8 objects; touch region.c/desktop.c triggers rebuild, second run up-to-date; test-region 37/37 green. flair-desktop-mutant-rules template checked -- NOT a bug (eval fires after defs, documented at :8976).

title: COPY same-file guard: cover relative-vs-absolute path forms (residual of initech-ojxn)
description: Follow-up to initech-ojxn. cmd_same_file (os/milton/command.c) proves src==dst from operand TEXT only: it covers identical/case/bare-name-8.3/'.\'-prefix/default-drive-prefix and identical subdir paths. It does NOT resolve relative-vs-absolute or '..' forms for files in a subdir, because the shell exposes no AH=60h TRUENAME / file-path canonicalizer (only AH=47h GET-CWD + a CHDIR-scoped directory canon in fileio_fat.c fat_canon_from_cluster). RESIDUAL DATA-LOSS VECTOR: for a MULTI-CLUSTER file named via an uncovered same-file spelling (e.g. 'COPY \FOO.TXT FOO.TXT' at root, 'COPY SUB\A.TXT .\SUB\A.TXT', or '..\' traversal), the guard does not fire and dos_creat truncates the source (fat12_create -> fat12_free_chain) so the copy loses the tail clusters -- the same class of loss initech-ojxn fixed for the direct forms. FIX OPTIONS: (a) expose an AH=60h TRUENAME (or a file-path canonicalizer) in the kernel and canonicalize both operands before comparison; or (b) DEEPER/root-cause: make dos_creat (AH=3Ch) refuse to truncate a file that is already open (DOS sharing semantics) so any src==dst is caught at the SFT layer regardless of path spelling. Option (b) also covers REN/other flows. Oracle: extend test-copy-selfcopy with the relative-vs-absolute key scripts once a canonicalizer/sharing check lands.

title: region: RGN_ROW_X_MAX=256 contradicts its own spec comment (640px scanline => 640 inversion pts); wide regions fail-loud
description: [Follow-up to initech-mswo P0 fix] spec/region_algebra.h:279-282 defines RGN_ROW_X_MAX=256 with a comment that says '640px wide => at most 320 disjoint spans => 640 inversion points; this cap covers that with headroom' -- but 640 > 256, so the constant CONTRADICTS its own stated worst case. Consequences after the mswo P0 hotfix (xmerge fail-louds at the per-row cap): a legitimately busy full-width scanline (up to 320 spans / 640 inversion points) or the XOR of two max-density (256-pt) rows now FAIL-LOUD (panic) instead of corrupting -- correct per Rule 2, but it means such regions are unrepresentable. RGN_X_POOL_CAP is already 1024, so the pool has room. DECISION NEEDED (Rule 8 locked-spec change, deliberate act): raise RGN_ROW_X_MAX to its spec-intended value (>=640 to cover a 640px raster) and re-size scratch/tmp/normalize consistently, OR ratify 256 as the true cap and correct the misleading spec comment. May warrant a committee review since it ripples through the load-bearing ATKINSON engine (region_op scratch, region_normalize tmp, region_push_row). NOT to be done silently inside the P0 hotfix.
design: COMMITTEE DECISION 2026-07-10 (3 independent lenses: spec/ground-truth, engine/memory, oracle-impact -- UNANIMOUS): RAISE RGN_ROW_X_MAX to exactly 640 (not 1024). Key argument (lens A): 640 is the coordinate-DOMAIN bound from locked ADR-0004 OD-3 640x480; since both merge inputs draw toggles from the same positions and xmerge collapses coincident edges (region.c:398-401), a single band's merged output is domain-bounded -- at cap=640 the Sec-5 'cannot overflow' claim becomes TRUE, at 256 it is false and mswo-realizable. RIDERS (binding): (1) RGN_X_POOL_CAP 1024->2048 in the same deliberate act (1 dense row=640 + ~100 typical rows*4pts~=400 exceeds 1024 already; at cap 1024 one dense row could starve the pool). (2) Implementer derives the EXACT per-band scratch bound from the code (collapse-on-emit => ~domain-size; else 2*cap) and documents it + boundary test. (3) Kernel-stack audit: region_from_rects/complement stack triples at new sizes vs the single 64KiB stack (kstart.asm esp=0x9FFFC, shared with IRQ handlers); numbers documented -- hosted test-region green does NOT prove freestanding stack safety (lens C). (4) New deterministic oracle legs: full-width 320-span pixel-exact homomorphism round-trip + at-cap boundary case on a wide grid; small/deterministic, not fuzzed. (5) mswo ASAN mutant auto-scales (NSPANS=cap/2) -- re-verify it bites; fix stale literal comments. (6) Prose: Sec-5 two-bounds rewrite (pool bound vs per-row bound), region.c:364-373 'do NOT bump' note rewritten, ADR-0005:158 formally amended citing 44ab. (7) Worklog note records the Rule-8 deliberate change. Steelman for RATIFY-256 (all three lenses): no shipped UI object exceeds ~14 pts/row today; recorded and rejected -- the engine claims Z^2-per-scanline with no density restriction, an unreachable-today panic is a landmine (Law 4), and the fix costs ~1.5-8KB per-op stack against 64KiB.
acceptance_criteria: RGN_ROW_X_MAX and its spec comment agree; scratch/tmp/normalize/push_row consistently sized; a full-width 320-span scanline round-trips through region_op+normalize without fail-loud; test-region green + a new wide-region case; worklog note records the deliberate Rule-8 change.
notes: COMMITTEE ROUND 3 2026-07-11 (guard-bust escalation resolved; verification PASS conditional): kernel_shell measured 8340B OVER _kernel_end<PROGRAM_BASE with the static WS (pre-change runway ~10KiB; structural runway filed as its own bead). FINAL MECHANISM: dual-mode working-set storage, engine stays heap-agnostic. HOSTED: g_rgn_ws stays a static value array (tests unchanged). FREESTANDING: g_rgn_ws becomes bound pointers; kmain.c allocates the backing from the FLAIR heap via the flair_desktop_alloc_region idiom (FLAIR_CLASS_REGION, flair_desktop_oom on failure = boot-time fail-loud) and calls a freestanding-only region_engine_bind_ws(...) BEFORE region_engine_reset(); region_engine_reset keeps its universal guard-clear-only signature in both modes. BINDING TWEAKS: (W1) rgn_ws_acquire in freestanding must RGN_FAIL_LOUD on unbound/NULL pointers -- naive swap crashes silently pre-init; (W2) shrink slot 'one' to the 2-row/2-slot shape (region_complement pattern) -- saves ~6.1KiB BSS hosted + heap footprint, zero cost (acc/tmp must stay full-size, they accumulate); (W3) bind strictly before reset/first Toolbox call; update the region.c WS banner to describe pointer-binding; (W4) after landing re-run test-flair-desktop QEMU+Bochs (Rule 5) and confirm kernel_end margin restored (~10KiB). Single-mode alternatives checked and rejected: one-shrink alone insufficient (6124B < 8340B), hosted-only helpers save .text not .bss (they share slot 0 with acc), second ext-mem ld section violates the ADR-0004 DEC-03 single-owner arena. Query helpers already share slot 0 -- keep that.
close_reason: LANDED 4835184. Cap raised to the OD-3 domain bound (640) + pool to 2048; Sec-5 two-bounds rewrite; ADR-0005 amended; dual-mode working set (hosted static / freestanding FLAIR-heap-bound) after the guard-bust escalation; all committee riders (T1-T4, W1-W4) executed. Verified on main: test-region 65/65 + 4 mutants, kernel_shell links margin 8644B, QEMU+Bochs boots PASS. Acceptance criteria met: constants agree with derivation, full-width 320-span scanline round-trips pixel-exact, worklog note in WL-0071.

title: scan_string pool-wrap fires only when out==0 — valid strings falsely rejected 'too long' when the pool tail is small
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R3 2026-06-28, wf_a2a0042d, adversarially verified] subsystem=seed/lexer (seed/lexer.c).
EVIDENCE: lexer.c:268-278: `if (out>=avail){ if (lx->strpos!=0 && out==0){ wrap } else return make_error("string literal too long") }`. The wrap to pool-start only triggers when no bytes are yet stored (out==0). If >=1 byte is stored and the tail is exhausted, the error is returned despite free space at pool start.

EXPECTED: Strings up to LEXER_STRBUF_CAP always succeed regardless of pool cursor, by wrapping before/while scanning.

ACTUAL: A string starting at strpos in (0,CAP) whose length exceeds the remaining tail is rejected even though it fits from position 0.

REPRO: Drive strpos to 1020 (avail=4), lex 'hello' (5 chars): 5th char hits out(4)>=avail(4) with out!=0 → false 'too long'.
close_reason: Fixed + mutation-proven in WL-0068; make clean && make test ALL GREEN (296 host + 61 emu) on command-com-default

title: PACK does not update or rebuild open NDX indexes — silently corrupts them after record renumbering
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R3 2026-06-28, wf_a2a0042d, adversarially verified] subsystem=SAMIR/mutate (os/samir/cmd/mutate.c).
EVIDENCE: m_pack (mutate.c:884-905) calls dbf_pack (renumbers survivors), dbf_flush, wa_refresh, wa_nav_reset — no NDX call. ndx.h:636 states the S5.5 contract 'After DBF DELETE/PACK, call ndx_delete_key for each deleted recno.' Open NDX B-trees keep stale physical recnos; wa_nav_reset only drops the in-memory order cache, not the on-disk tree.

EXPECTED: PACK rebuilds all open NDX files (REINDEX) after renumbering, or at minimum ndx_delete_key per deleted recno.

ACTUAL: NDX retains stale physical recnos; post-PACK SEEK/FIND return wrong records.

REPRO: 5-rec table, NDX on CODE; DELETE rec 2; PACK; SEEK of an old record's key returns wrong results.
close_reason: Fixed + mutation-proven in WL-0068; make clean && make test ALL GREEN (296 host + 61 emu) on command-com-default

title: LOCATE RECORD n FOR <cond> scans past record n when FOR is false, continuing to EOF

title: SKIP -1 from physical EOF lands at nrec-1 instead of nrec (off-by-one under-skip)
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R3 2026-06-28, wf_a2a0042d, adversarially verified] subsystem=SAMIR/nav (os/samir/cmd/nav.c, os/samir/cmd/workarea.c).
EVIDENCE: nav.c:373-385: SKIP past last sets wa->recno=nrec then eof=1. SKIP -1 reads cur via wa_recno (nav.c:359) = raw wa->recno = nrec (workarea.c:1044-1049 returns the raw field), so next=nrec-1. The external wac_recno (881-883) correctly returns nrec+1 at EOF, but the skip path uses wa_recno. Oracle gap: test_interp_nav.c:222-224 gates this path, never tests SKIP -1 from EOF.

EXPECTED: From virtual EOF (nrec+1), SKIP -1 lands at record nrec.

ACTUAL: Lands at nrec-1 because internal recno is nrec, not the virtual nrec+1.

REPRO: GO BOTTOM; SKIP (to EOF); SKIP -1; RECNO() returns nrec-1.
close_reason: Fixed + mutation-proven in WL-0068; make clean && make test ALL GREEN (296 host + 61 emu) on command-com-default

title: ndx_delete_key first-match descent returns -NDX_ERR_NOTFOUND for valid (key,recno) entries in any non-leftmost duplicate-key leaf
description:

EVIDENCE: ndx.c:2287-2293 descent breaks at the FIRST separator with key>=target (identical to insert). For a bulk-built non-unique index where >kpp records share key K, delete(K,recno-in-leaf_2) descends only into leaf_1, scans, fails NOTFOUND though the entry exists in leaf_2 (reachable by ndx_inorder but unreachable by delete/seek).

title: dbf_open_rw normalizes header_length to +1 form before reads use it — breaks every record read on +2-form files (BANK.DBF, TAX.DBF)
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R3 2026-06-28, wf_a2a0042d, adversarially verified] subsystem=SAMIR/.dbf codec (os/samir/fs/dbf.c).
EVIDENCE: dbf.c:459 sets tbl->header_length to on-disk value; records loaded from local header_length at 581; then dbf.c:602 overwrites tbl->header_length to (DBF_HDR_SIZE+descbytes+1), one byte short for a +2 file. dbf_read_rec (735) computes rec_off from the normalized (short) header_length, lands on the extra 0x00 of the 0x0D 0x00 terminator → not 0x20/0x2A → -DBF_ERR_BAD_REC (750-757). +2 fixtures: dbf_format.h:54.

EXPECTED: dbf_read_rec on a +2-form file reads record 1 at the original header_length offset, returning the live flag and decoded fields.

ACTUAL: Seeks one byte early, reads 0x00 as delete flag, returns -DBF_ERR_BAD_REC for every record. Read-only dbf_open skips line 602 and is unaffected.

REPRO: dbf_open_rw(BANK.DBF); dbf_read_rec(tbl,1,out,&del) → -DBF_ERR_BAD_REC(12).
close_reason: Fixed + mutation-proven in WL-0068; make clean && make test ALL GREEN (296 host + 61 emu) on command-com-default

description:

EVIDENCE: fn_builtins.c:845 `rounded=(double)(int64_t)(v*scale+0.5)/scale;` and 848 (negative-dec arm) `(int64_t)(v/scale+0.5)*scale`. (int64_t) truncates toward zero. For v=-2.7,dec=0: v+0.5=-2.2, (int64_t)(-2.2)=-2 → -2.0 (should be -3.0). dec_format (rt.c:247) correctly uses the static rt_floor64 (rt.c:207-213); fn_round skips it. The comment at fn_builtins.c:818-819 falsely claims it uses 'the same idiom as dec_format'.

EXPECTED: ROUND(-2.7,0)=-3.0; ROUND(-1234,-2)=-1200.0 — both arms should use rt_floor64.

ACTUAL: ROUND(-2.7,0)=-2.0; ROUND(-27,-1)=-20.0; ROUND(-1234,-2)=-1100.0 — every negative value rounds one unit toward zero.

REPRO: Evaluate ROUND(-2.7,0) → -2.0 (expected -3.0).
close_reason: Fixed + mutation-proven in WL-0068; make clean && make test ALL GREEN (296 host + 61 emu) on command-com-default

title: dos_read lacks a Carry-Flag check — read errors are returned as byte counts, emitting/writing garbage in TYPE, COPY and batch loading
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R2 2026-06-28, wf_2f47b15b, adversarially verified] subsystem=MILTON/COMMAND.COM (os/milton/command.c dos_read).
EVIDENCE: command.c:1439-1448 uses plain int $0x21 with no sbb %1,%1 to capture CF, unlike dos_open(:1427), dos_creat(:1469), dos_open_mode(:1511), dos_write_h(:1491). On AH=3Fh error (CF=1, AX=error code) dos_read returns the error code as a byte count. builtin_type(:2108-2113) then dos_write(chunk,err) emits err uninitialized bytes; builtin_copy(:2334-2344) writes them to the destination; batch_load_file(:2991-2995) advances total by err.

EXPECTED: Capture CF with sbb, return 0/sentinel on error; callers break on failure.

ACTUAL: A read error (e.g. ACCESS_DENIED=5) makes TYPE print 5 stack bytes, COPY corrupt the destination, batch mis-size the script.

REPRO: Trigger an AH=3Fh error mid-TYPE/COPY -> garbage bytes in output/destination.
close_reason: Fixed + mutation-proven in WL-0068; make clean && make test ALL GREEN (296 host + 61 emu) on command-com-default

title: App-switch erases the background NOTES window entirely from the compositor (chrome + content gone)
description:
[FLAIR GUI bug-hunt 2026-06-28, wf_4dfb6f55, adversarially verified] subsystem=FLAIR/desktop + process (compositor / app-switch).
EVIDENCE: flair_appswitch_pre.png shows HELLO (white) and NOTES (gray, bounds (260,120)-(560,340) per spec/flair_tenants_demo.h). flair_appswitch_post.png: after click-to-activate on HELLO, the entire NOTES window is absent — its non-HELLO-covered footprint shows bare teal desktop, no title bar, frame, or scrollbars. SelectWindow (window.c:357-371) raises HELLO without generating exposure damage for NOTES's newly-relevant area and no full desktop_paint_all follows the z-order change, so NOTES chrome is never repainted as a background window.

EXPECTED: After SelectWindow raises HELLO, NOTES stays in the z-order as a background window and is repainted (inactive chrome) in its non-occluded region.

ACTUAL: NOTES vanishes completely; only HELLO plus a stray fragment remain (see orphaned-fragment bug).

notes: ROOT CAUSE PINNED (re-test on mswo-fixed base, pixel-proven): a STALE wm->desktop_update, NOT a missing exposure/repaint and NOT region corruption. Init hides the two canon frame windows (kmain.c:1926-1927) -> distribute_exposure seeds desktop_update with their footprint (fd_win_bounds); the init recomposite goes through shell_render -> desktop_paint_all (shell.c:330) which NEVER reads/clears desktop_update (only desktop_paint_damage clears it, desktop.c:236). The stale region survives into the pump; the first app-switch desktop_paint_damage (kmain.c:2274) step-1 fills it TEAL, erasing NOTES's footprint (erasure boundary traces fd_win_bounds exactly). FIX (root-cause): desktop_paint_all must reset wm->desktop_update at its tail (a full paint satisfies all pending damage) -- this also fixes qi8v's drag path. NOTES then repaints inactive via v6t2(done)+a9iq. bz8f NOT implicated (no aliased region_op on the live path). ORACLE GAP: ppm_flair_appswitch_check never probes NOTES's non-overlap footprint, so it was GREEN while NOTES vanished -- the fix must add that probe (mutation-proven RED on today's build).
close_reason: Fixed: desktop_paint_all resets wm->desktop_update at its tail; the stale HideWindow footprint no longer leaks into the first desktop_paint_damage (app-switch=jmc5, drag=qi8v). title: FLAIR live compositor ERASES the modal dialog + menu bars when a window is dragged across them (non-WindowMgr layers not damage-tracked)
description:
SYMPTOM (operator, make run-flair): corrupted redraws when windows are moved past each other.

ROOT CAUSE: the live drag repaint desktop_paint_damage (os/flair/desktop.c:171) composites ONLY the WindowMgr document windows + the desktop background. The live scene ALSO contains the modal FILE COPY dialog (os/flair/dialog.h:420, rect x[140,500] y[200,280], drawn ON TOP) and TWO stacked menu bars (os/flair/shell.h:99-101, y[0,40]) -- both painted ONCE by shell_render and NOT participants in the WindowMgr damage/z-order model. When a document window is dragged across them, the vacated area falls through to wm->desktop_update and is filled with seafoam (desktop.c:197-200), ERASING the modal/bar; and a dragged window's visible region is not clipped against them (window.c fronts_union considers only WindowMgr windows), so it can OVERPAINT them.

EMPIRICAL (flair_live.img; drag W1 left 260px across W0 + modal): the modal right-half x[366,498] y[206,278] went from 85.5% white + 14.5% black (the dBoxProc dialog box + text) BEFORE to 100% teal AFTER -- the modal erased to desktop background. Window-over-window compositing is CLEAN and the cursor save-under is CLEAN; the defect is specifically the non-WindowMgr layers.

WHY IT ESCAPED: test-flair-drag's pixel oracle (tools/ppm_flair_drag_check.c) deliberately probes "right of window 0" and "above the modal", AVOIDING the modal/bar region; the region gate (test-interact) grades math, not composited pixels over these layers.

FIX OPTIONS: integrate the always-on-top layers (menu bars + modal) into the live compositor so they survive a damage repaint. Interim: after desktop_paint_damage, re-blit the bar + modal layers over the damaged region. Clean: make the bars + modal topmost participants in the z-order (windows clip against them via fronts_union; they repaint in the damage pass). Same incompleteness family as initech-z1f5 (live menu panel restore).

Oracle-first: depends on the independent modal/bar survival oracle.
design: RATIFIED (arch verify + red-team, 2026-07-07): a SINGLE ~15-LOC fold of a new wm->overlay_rgn into fronts_union (window.c:92-107) -- NOT the uniform-window model, NOT a re-composite wrapper. KEY INSIGHT: fronts_union feeds the WHOLE damage chain (visible_into->exposed->distribute_exposure->desktop_update), so once the overlay occludes, defect (b) overpaint AND defect (a) seafoam-erasure BOTH close for free -- overlay pixels are never written by desktop_paint_damage and survive from the initial shell_render. NO desktop.c change (sidesteps the jmc5 edit). The fix is inside the ONE shared occlusion primitive every paint path (drag/close/app-switch/full-render) routes through, so no path can bypass it (why the wrapper/per-site registration is rejected). ALIASING (Rule 3): use rgn_accumulate(out, overlay_rgn, UNION, sc2) with sc2 = (out==scratch_c)?scratch_b:scratch_c -- NEVER the naive region_op(out,out,overlay) self-alias (corrupts on overlap, the case under test). Modal-bbox is sufficient+exact (dBoxProc fills its whole bounds; bars are solid strips). Scene = flair_live (show_modal=1, kmain.c:965), the ONLY scene with the modal; NO init HideWindow there so desktop_update starts empty (pipa is pure occlusion, distinct from jmc5). LANES: 0 WindowMgr field+init-zero+WINDOW_MUTATE_IGNORE_OVERLAY (window.h/c); 1 the fold (window.c fronts_union); 2 scene wiring build overlay_rgn=union(bars{0,0,40,640}[+modal{140,200,500,280} iff show_modal]) in shell_build_scene + kmain alloc (REBASE on 4w15's shell.c/kmain.c edits); 3 dc4v EMU oracle tool + trace (RED-first); 4 mutation-proof via flair_live_mut_overlay.img (-DWINDOW_MUTATE_IGNORE_OVERLAY). Oracle blast radius ~zero: fold is a no-op when overlay_rgn==NULL (all host harnesses), so test-window/interact/drag/shell stay green; only WINDOW_MUTATE_IGNORE_OVERLAY needs EMU mutation-proof. dc4v probes (canon-graded, flair_live drag W1 left ~260px): modal (496,240)==idx0 + (450,240)==idx1 + area x[366,498]y[206,278] >=80pct white/black <=5pct teal; bar y=30 x[70,350] idx3-gray high; anchor (20,460)==idx2.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging any document window across the modal and the menu bars leaves them intact (no teal hole, no overpaint), verified by an independent pixel oracle the fix turns RED->GREEN; window-over-window compositing stays clean; reproducible build green.

title: FLAIR mouse: INDEPENDENT physical-direction oracle (PS/2 up -> cursor v DECREASES) + EVENT_MUTATE_FLIP_SIGN mutant
description:
The mouse-Y inversion (sibling bug) escaped every gate because all mouse-Y oracles grade the cursor by RECOMPUTING expected where.v from the SAME "cursor_v += dy" rule the artifact uses (harness/proptest/test_event.c manufactures dy=+5 and asserts v=240+5), and the only mouse mutant EVENT_MUTATE_STALE_WHERE drops the update (magnitude) but never tests SIGN. This is the HER-02 by-construction heresy on the sign axis (ADR-0010, Law 2).

Build an INDEPENDENT oracle that encodes the GROUND-TRUTH polarity from the hardware contract (a real PS/2 mouse-up packet: byte0 Y-sign bit + byte2 magnitude, +Y = physical up) and asserts that after the producer cooks it into the ring, the screen cursor v DECREASES (moves up). Mutation-prove with a new EVENT_MUTATE_FLIP_SIGN that inverts the producer sign and MUST drive this oracle RED. Optional EMU leg on the interactive image: inject a known physical-up motion, assert the cursor sprite rose.

This oracle is the RED half of the producer fix and must exist FIRST (Red->Green, CLAUDE.md Rule 1/6).
acceptance_criteria: A host oracle anchored to the PS/2 packet convention (NOT cook_raw's += rule) asserts physical-up -> screen v decreases; RED against the current inverted producer, GREEN after the negation fix; EVENT_MUTATE_FLIP_SIGN bites it.

title: FLAIR live cursor: vertical mouse axis INVERTED -- producer packs RAW PS/2 dy, violating the locked ring-payload Y contract
description:
SYMPTOM (operator, make run-flair): the mouse moves inverted in the VERTICAL axis -- physical-up moves the cursor/window DOWN; horizontal is correct.

ROOT CAUSE: a producer-side sign error that VIOLATES the locked ring-payload contract. spec/event_model.h:333-335 defines FLAIR_RAW_MOUSE payload bits 16..23 as "signed delta Y ... Y axis inverted from PS/2 convention to screen-down-positive" -- the PS/2->screen flip MUST happen BEFORE the value enters the ring. But the producer flair_live_mouse_post (os/milton/kmain.c:1024-1026) packs the RAW PS/2 dy (mouse.c:222 "+dy = up") with NO inversion. Downstream cook_raw (os/flair/event.c:441) correctly ADDS what the contract guarantees is an already-flipped screen-down delta (g_cursor_v += dy), so physical-up raises g_cursor_v and the cursor descends. cook_raw and test_event.c are CORRECT per spec; the bug is solely the producer. The misleading comment is mouse.c:225-227 ("the pump cooks the Y flip"), contradicting the locked spec.

EMPIRICAL (flair_live.img, QMP rel-mouse): rel-y +40 -> window top 120->80 (UP); rel-y -40 -> 120->160 (DOWN) => physical-up -> window-down. Reproduced.

WHY IT ESCAPED: the producer is __attribute__((unused)) on host (no host oracle) and runs only in the bare-metal live build; the EMU drag/mouse gate goldens BAKED IN the inverted behavior (Makefile:11199 "rel +y -> cursor up"; test-flair-mouse where.v calibrated to the inverted cook). No oracle establishes an INDEPENDENT physical-direction ground truth (HER-02 / ADR-0010 by-construction pattern, on the sign axis).

FIX: negate dy at the producer (kmain.c:1026) BEFORE narrowing into bits 16..23, in int width -- CRITICAL: -(int8)-128 = +128 is not int8-representable; negate in int, or saturate -128->+127. Update the stale ISR comment mouse.c:225-227. Leave cook_raw (event.c:441) and test_event.c UNCHANGED. Then RE-BASELINE the EMU gate goldens that encoded the inversion (test-flair-drag Makefile ~11193-11224 trace+expected window pos; test-flair-mouse Makefile:8396/8423 expected where.v) to the physical-correct direction -- do NOT revert the fix to keep them green.

Oracle-first: depends on the independent physical-direction oracle.
acceptance_criteria: make run-flair: physical-up moves the cursor/window UP. The independent direction oracle is RED before the producer fix and GREEN after. EMU drag/mouse gates re-baselined to physical-correct direction. test_event.c unchanged (correct per spec). Reproducible build green; ASCII-clean.
close_reason: Producer fixed (mouse_pack.h negate per the locked Sec-5 contract); every bug-calibrated trace/golden rebaselined to physical truth (mouse expectation, drag/dc4v/menu/crossdrag specs, locked appswitch trace w/ in-file Rule-8 note); all live-input emu gates + mutants re-verified green on main. Landed 5dd5525 together with the 8f5p oracle (now closed).

title: Rule-8: raise PROGRAM_BASE 0x30000->0x38000 for kernel BSS headroom (ADR-by-committee ruling)
description: The shell kernel outgrew the 128 KiB window [0x10000,0x30000) -- _kernel_end=0x30fc0 overruns PROGRAM_BASE by ~4.3 KiB after the p96i ANSI wiring. ADR-by-committee (memory-architect/period-purist/north-star lenses) RULED: raise PROGRAM_BASE 0x30000->0x38000 (the sanctioned mechanism, precedent 5pe; a growing resident kernel pushing the TPA up is the authentic DOS model). LOCKED-SPEC change (Rule 8). BLAST RADIUS (committee-found): (1) spec/memory_map.h PROGRAM_BASE 0x30000->0x38000 (PROGRAM_IMAGE etc. auto-compute); (2) 15 .asm fixtures hard-code org 0x00030100 -> 0x00038100 (incl. os/samir/boot/samir_crt0.asm + samir.ld); (3) SECONDARY data-page addresses 0x31000/0x32000 in datetime/vect/absdisk programs must shift +0x8000 -> 0x39000/0x3A000; (4) test_hardware_spec.c hard-coded CHECK(PROGRAM_BASE==0x30000) + spec/hardware.json literal must update; (5) re-verify the full EXEC gate-set + emu + Bochs (Rule 5). Verify program region [0x38000,0x70000) stays ample (PROGRAM_IMAGE_MAX ~155KiB > SAMIR ~107KiB -- committee-verified).
notes: WL-0042 Wave 4 blocker. Committee ruling 2026-06-20. Companion follow-up: merge g_fat/g_load_fat via fileio_fat_get_cache (B, the headroom bead).
close_reason: SUPERSEDED by option B (FAT-cache share). The ADR-by-committee ratified raising PROGRAM_BASE 0x30000->0x38000, but on implementation+grading the raise BROKE SAMIR: it shrank the disjoint AH=48h heap arena ([PROGRAM_IMAGE+image+BSS_RESERVE, ENV_BLOCK)) from ~48 KiB to ~16 KiB -> SAMIR's REPL failed to start (test-samir-boot RED). The committee's own endorsed option B is strictly better: the loader now SHARES the int21 file backend's whole-FAT buffer (fileio_fat_fat_buffer) instead of its own 6 KiB g_load_fat copy -> frees 6 KiB kernel .bss so the kernel fits at the ORIGINAL 0x30000 (_kernel_end 0x30fc0->0x2f7a0) WITH p96i, preserving SAMIR's full arena. The PROGRAM_BASE raise is no longer needed (kept available as a future option if the kernel outgrows even with B). Implemented in loader.c/loader.h/kmain.c + fileio_fat_fat_buffer reuse. Caught by Law-4 orchestrator grading (verify the report; the committee analysis missed the heap-arena consequence).

title: Kernel-window headroom: raise PROGRAM_BASE or share the two 6 KiB FAT buffers (g_fat/g_load_fat)
description: The shell kernel .bss is repeatedly bumping the program-load window guard (_kernel_end vs PROGRAM_BASE=0x30000, limit 0x2ff00) as the kernel grows. Across this session each wave (Wave 1 env/mz/batch, Wave 2 mvg crit_blockdev, Wave 3 device-chain) pushed it; mitigated tactically by trimming BATCH_FILE_MAX 4096->2048 (a .BAT size cut). The PRINCIPLED fix: either (a) raise PROGRAM_BASE (e.g. 0x30000->0x34000) -- a LOCKED-SPEC change (spec/memory_map.h, Rule 8) with wide blast radius (every .COM org 0x30100, the MCB arena window [0x30000,0x70000), PROGRAM_IMAGE, the absdisk seam -- needs an ADR amendment + every .asm fixture's org updated), OR (b) share ONE whole-FAT buffer between fat12.c (g_fat, 6144) and loader.c (g_load_fat, 6144) -- saves 6 KiB, but couples the loader's load_program_from_fat FAT cache to fat12's. Restore BATCH_FILE_MAX to 4096 once headroom exists.
notes: RATIFIED (committee 2026-06-20, gridlock=false) + ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT: PATH 2 -- whole-map shift UP by delta=0x8000. The chair OVERRULED a 3-lens PATH-1 majority on measured arithmetic: PATH-1A (reserve 0xC000) left only 736 B between arena_base and SAMIR .bss end (re-creates y206); PATH-1B (reserve 0x10000, arena shrinks to 31.2 KiB) PANICS SAMIR -- pal_milton.c PAL_MILTON_HEAP_PARAS=2048 requests EXACTLY 0x8000=32768 B via AH=48h with milton_panic on CF=1, and 31968<32768. PATH 2 keeps SAMIR's arena byte-identical (47.2 KiB), preserves disjointness, gains +32 KiB kernel window by reclaiming half the dead [0x90000,0xA0000) gap. FINAL CONSTANTS (spec/memory_map.h): PROGRAM_BASE 0x30000->0x38000, PROGRAM_IMAGE 0x30100->0x38100, ENV_BLOCK 0x5F000->0x67000, PROGRAM_STACK_BOT 0x60000->0x68000, PROGRAM_STACK_TOP 0x6FFFC->0x77FFC, PROGRAM_ALLOC_END 0x70000->0x78000, LOAD_STAGING_BASE 0x70000->0x78000; PROGRAM_BSS_RESERVE HELD at 0x10000 (covers measured 47.3 KiB .bss, 16.7 KiB slack). ORCHESTRATOR AMENDMENT (Law 4 -- the chair's 'kstart ESP unchanged' was a FLAW): staging at [0x78000,0x88000) would overlap the kernel stack [0x80000,0x90000); FIX = move kstart.asm ESP 0x8FFFC->0x97FFC so the kernel stack moves to [0x88000,0x98000), disjoint from staging, 32 KiB gap to VGA. boot_info@0x500 + FONT_STASH@0x1000 are low-mem (untouched); stage2 anchor 0x90000 dead after handoff. Plus 13 .asm orgs->0x38100 + ALL program scratch/result equs +0x8000 (vect BOGUS_24/R_CRITAL, datetime full R_* block, absdisk PATBUF/RDBUF/R_AX -- caught by self-audit), samir.ld+crt0, BATCH_FILE_MAX 2048->4096. GRADED GREEN: kernel-end guard re-bound to 0x38000 (_kernel_end=0x300e0 OK); SAMIR relinked @0x38100 .bss still 0xBD20 __bss_end 0x57040; test-loader 29/0, test-arena-disjoint 1321/0, test-samir-boot PASS (the y206 oracle). Full make test + Bochs in flight.
close_reason: DELIVERED (PATH 2, committee-ratified + orchestrator kstart amendment). PROGRAM_BASE 0x30000->0x38000 whole-map shift +0x8000; kernel window [0x10000,0x38000)=160 KiB (+32 KiB). PROGRAM_BSS_RESERVE held 0x10000 (the prescribed 32 KiB cut was disproven: SAMIR .bss measured 47.3 KiB not 26 KiB). SAMIR arena preserved 47.2 KiB (test-samir-boot PASS). Graded GREEN: 240 host + 39 emu + Bochs (triple_fault=0). Commit bae46d4, WL-0046.
