title: FAT16 volume mounts OK but all decode/encode is 12-bit-only: silent garbage on FAT16 mount
description: fat12_mount returns FAT12_OK for a volume it classifies FAT_TYPE_FAT16 (fat12.c:132), but next_cluster/set_entry/walk_chain and the EOC/bad predicates are hard-wired 12-bit + FAT12 thresholds (header even warns FAT16 OUT OF SCOPE). fat_type is set but never checked by any op. A FAT16 mount + read mis-decodes every entry (16-bit treated as straddled 12-bit) -> garbage chains / corrupt data, no fail-loud. Audit: fat12 fat12-fat16-decode-mismatch.
acceptance_criteria: Either reject FAT16 at mount (FAT12_ERR_UNSUPPORTED when total_clusters>=FAT12_MAX_CLUSTERS) so 12-bit code never runs on 16-bit FAT, or assert vol->fat_type==FAT_TYPE_FAT12 at every decode/encode entry and fail loud; test mounts a FAT16 image and asserts the loud rejection (mutation-proven); make test green.
close_reason: fat12_mount rejects FAT16 (FAT12_ERR_UNSUPPORTED) since all decode/encode is 12-bit-only. RED->GREEN (synthetic FAT16 boot sector via in-test memory blockdev, total_sectors bumped past 4085), mutation-proven. make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: FAT12 read path has no upper-cluster-bound: out-of-range cluster maps to in-image LBA, silent wrong data
description: fat12_next_cluster/walk_chain/read_file/read_partial only bounds-check the FAT BUFFER (off+1 < fat_len), never the cluster against the last valid data cluster. fat12_last_cluster() exists (fat12.c:973) but is write-path-only. An in-FAT link value above last-valid with (N*3/2+1)<fat_len is accepted and fed to BPB_CLUSTER_LBA. On 1.44MB geometry it happens to land >=2880 and is caught only by the file-backed blockdev EOF short-read -- a coincidence, not an invariant. With sectors_per_cluster>1 or FAT slack it maps to a VALID in-image LBA and silently returns the WRONG sector. Fuzzer (fat12_corrupt_fuzz.c:340-356) documents reliance on that coincidence. Audit: fat12 fat12-no-upper-cluster-bound + fat12-no-eoc-min-data-value-overlap-test.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit predicate cluster in [FAT12_FIRST_DATA_CLUSTER .. fat12_last_cluster(vol)] applied at every data-cluster consumer; returns FAT12_ERR_CLUSTER past last data cluster; fuzz/diff leg on a multi-sectors-per-cluster image pokes an in-FAT out-of-range link mapping to an in-image LBA and asserts fail-loud (RED today); make test green.
close_reason: Added fat12_cluster_in_range(vol,c) upper-bound predicate; hardened all 5 chain-walk sites (walk_chain + read_partial x2 + write_partial x3) so an out-of-range in-chain cluster is rejected (FAT12_ERR_CLUSTER) instead of mapped to a wrong/out-of-volume LBA. RED->GREEN (synthetic out-of-range link), write path hardened too (Rule 3). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: INT 21h AH=59h GET EXTENDED ERROR returns stale data after most failures
description: do_geterr (AH=59h) reports g_last_error, but int21_note_error() is called from only TWO sites (do_open :805, do_getcwd). Every other failing handler (do_write/read/close/lseek/dup/dup2/creat/unlink/exec/findfirst/findnext) sets CF+AX WITHOUT int21_note_error, so 59h returns the previous/zero error after the common 'call failed -> query 59h' idiom. Spec: DOS 3.3 PRM AH=59h keeps the most-recent INT 21h error. Test gap: test_int21_edge.c:542-579 hand-seeds the error via int21_note_error directly, never via a real failing dispatch -- which is why this is invisible. Audit: int21 geterr-not-populated-on-most-failures + geterr-test-gap.
acceptance_criteria: Centralize a set_error(f,code) helper (set_ax+cf_set+int21_note_error) used at every cf_set error return; dispatcher-driven oracle: fail OPEN/READ/WRITE through int21_dispatch then AH=59h asserts the just-returned code; mutation-proven; make test green.
close_reason: Single dispatch-choke capture in int21_dispatch: on CF=1, int21_note_error(AX). Covers every current+future failing handler; do_geterr (CF=0) never clobbers; success leaves last error intact. RED->GREEN, mutation-proven. make test 55 host + 19 emu GREEN.

title: INT 21h AH=40h WRITE rejects read/write-mode (AL=2) handles
description: do_write (os/milton/int21.c:653) gates FILE writes on e->open_mode != SFT_MODE_WRITE (==1). A handle opened AH=3Dh AL=2 (SFT_MODE_RDWR, sft.h:75) therefore returns ACCESS_DENIED on every WRITE, though read/write mode must permit writing. Breaks any program that opens a file mode-2 to update in place -- notably InitechBase .dbf record updates (the named consumer). do_read does NOT gate on mode (only kind), so read side is fine. Test gap: test_fileio.c only ever uses AL=0/AL=1 (never AL=2), so the bug is invisible to the oracle. VERIFIED against code 2026-06-13. Audit: fileio-sft rdwr-open-write-denied + rdwr-write-test-gap.

notes: Native-BIOS attempt (bochsbios + bochs-term installed): BIOS-bochs-latest does NOT fix it -- the guest faults EARLY (interrupt with IDT.limit=0x0 at t~363k), never reaching stage2 (no S1). So neither path boots clean on Bochs: SeaBIOS reaches stage2 but VBE-E00 (no VBE), native BIOS crashes pre-stage2 (likely the i440FX/ACPI/USB env or the tiny 2/2/32 geometry vs what the native BIOS expects). CONCLUSION: Bochs boot is a dedicated multi-step effort (try: standard disk geometry for the native BIOS; or term-headless to remove RFB timing; or a stage2 non-LFB fallback for the SeaBIOS path), NOT a quick win. Headless mechanism (RFB-unblock client) proven. Deferring per effort; QEMU remains the binding boot gate.
close_reason: Standard-VGA mode-0x13 fallback implemented + verified (3 commits: console 8bpp renderer, stage2 VBE->mode-0x13 fallback, kmain 8bpp boot_info + DAC palette). Bochs (legacy BIOS + pentium) now boots end-to-end with ZERO faults; QEMU VBE path unchanged. Locked by committed green oracles: test-console (host, 8bpp section mutation-proven) + test-tracer-boot (QEMU). Full suite 55 host + 19 emu GREEN. The committed Bochs differential GATE is tracked in initech-564 (de-risked, ready to build). Diagnosis: no VBE LFB on Bochs (legacy: ENOMODE, latest: E00 + won't POST due to CMOV/IDT.limit); standard VGA mode 0x13 is the portable answer.

title: Kernel has hit its 64 KiB window ceiling (_kernel_end 0x1fd20 vs PROGRAM_BASE 0x20000) -- blocks all further kernel growth
description: The kernel is linked at 0x10000 and PROGRAM_BASE=0x20000, giving a 64 KiB window. _kernel_end is now 0x1fd20 -- only ~480 bytes below the u0a guard limit (0x1ff00). The memory_map.h 'gap proof' comment still claims 32 KiB headroom but that is STALE: KERNEL_SECTORS grew to 96 and kernel .bss (cfg_fat_buf etc.) filled the window. ANY further kernel feature (509.8 INT 22/23/24 handlers next, but also 509.6/.7/.9 device chain/MCB/FCB) will trip the guard. Root cause: the kernel outgrew its window. Options: (A) raise PROGRAM_BASE (e.g. 0x20000 -> 0x30000) giving the kernel a larger window -- deliberate LOCKED-spec change (Rule 8), ripples into ~8 baked .asm 'org 0x00020100' constants + memory_map.h derived addrs + test_loader.c assertion; program image arena shrinks from ~252 KiB to still-ample ~190 KiB. (B) relocate large kernel scratch .bss buffers to free high conventional RAM (0x90000-0xA0000, below VGA) via fixed pointers, reclaiming .bss without touching PROGRAM_BASE or any program org. Either is a real fix; (A) is more mechanical, (B) avoids program-side ripple. Update the stale memory_map.h gap-proof comment as part of the fix. Re-run test-loader + the emu program gates (test-program/exec/type/dir/datetime/multiopen/exith/conin) which bake those org values.

title: FAT12 + file-I/O state-machine fuzzer (generative, shrinking, mtools differential)
description: We mandate mutation-proving (Rule 6) and FAT differential (Rule 5) and APPLY them universally, but we do NOT have generative/randomized fuzzing for the FAT12 + file-I/O layer that dBASE (M6) and Turbo Initech (M7/M8) now stand on. Current FAT oracles (test-fat, test-fat-partial, test-fat-write-partial, test-multiopen) are fixed enumerated matrices + mutants -- strong, but they don't explore the deep state space (Rule 3: all bugs are deep). The only property/fuzz mandates in CLAUDE.md are the region engine (initech-6dy, M3) and the xBase evaluator (initech-gmo, M6), both unbuilt; neither covers the file layer. BUILD a deterministic, seeded (Rule 11 -- no clock; seed is an input) generative fuzzer that drives randomized sequences of fat12_create / fat12_write_partial / fat12_read_partial / lseek / append / unlink / multi-open across many handles on a mounted image, and after each step DIFFERENTIALLY checks the volume against the python reference and/or mtools (re-mount + read-back), with SHRINKING of any failing sequence to a minimal reproducer. Run a bounded N-iteration sweep as a gate; on failure print the seed + shrunk op-sequence. Wire into the test vector (its own slower tier if needed). This is the standing hardening gate the file layer is missing. Mutation-prove the fuzzer itself bites (perturb a fat12 op, confirm the fuzzer finds it).
acceptance_criteria: A seeded generative fuzzer runs K randomized create/write/seek/read/append/unlink/multi-open sequences against a real FAT12 image, differentially verifying each state vs the python ref / mtools; a deliberately injected fat12 bug is CAUGHT and SHRUNK to a minimal reproducer (seed + op list printed); the gate is deterministic (same seed -> same run, Rule 11) and wired into the test infra; ASCII-clean.
close_reason: Generative FAT12+file-I/O fuzzer landed: deterministic seeded (no clock) sweep of randomized create/write_partial/read_partial/read_file/unlink across a multi-file pool, 3-way differential per op (in-process + remount + raw FAT-sync) and mtools/python at run-end, with greedy shrinking to a minimal seed+recipe. test-fat-fuzz green (200+40 seeds, ~9600 ops, deterministic across runs, in TEST_UNIT_GATES); test-fat-fuzz-mutant proves it finds+shrinks the no-RMW mutant (seed=1, 3 ops) + bites 4 others. No real bug in current fat12.c. make test green at 53 gates under load.

title: [epic] Multi-tenant file I/O: positioned read/write, seek, concurrent opens
description: Replace the single-static-buffer file model (one file open at a time, whole-file into a 64 KiB buffer at OPEN, EXEC staging reusing the same region per spec/memory_map.h) with a real multi-tenant model: per-handle positioned cluster-chain read AND write, real LSEEK, N concurrent opens via a small buffer pool, SFT teardown on EXIT, and EXEC staging decoupled from the file buffer. This is the load-bearing prerequisite for InitechBase (.dbf + .mdx open simultaneously, random seek, >64 KiB files), Turbo Initech (read source + write object, >64 KiB self-host source), and GUI app loading. Children: lq2, 0qh, snk, 6hk + the memory_map staging decouple.
acceptance_criteria: A single oracle proves: two files open concurrently with independent positioned read+write; LSEEK to arbitrary offset reads correct bytes; a >64 KiB file round-trips; EXEC of a program that itself opens a file does not corrupt either; SFT handles freed on EXIT. mtools differential stays green throughout.
close_reason: Multi-tenant file I/O epic COMPLETE. lq2 (fat12_read_partial), snk (fat12_write_partial), 0qh (positioned backend + single-buffer removal + EXEC staging decouple, proven by test-multiopen: 2 concurrent handles + 96 KiB file at offset 80000), 6hk (SFT teardown on EXIT). Single-buffer/one-file-at-a-time model eliminated; file layer ready for InitechBase (.dbf+.mdx, seek, >64 KiB) and Turbo Initech. make test green at 50 gates (35 host + 15 emu).

title: FAT12 write: seek-based partial write + multi-open write handles
description: AH=40h WRITE to a FILE uses whole-file-buffer-then-flush-at-CLOSE into a single 64KiB buffer (one open write file at a time), mirroring the read side. Implement positioned/seek-based partial write over the cluster chain + a multi-open write-handle pool. Surfaced building initech-509.11. Related: initech-lq2 (read partial), initech-0qh (multi-open pool).

The 'multi-open write handles' half is folded into the Step-3 pool (initech-0qh).

title: Remaining resident INT 21h query functions (0Eh/19h/2Ah-2Dh/36h/47h/59h/62h)

Currently each returns the controlled not-yet-impl diagnostic (CF=1 AX=0x0001) -- correct controlled-scope behavior but not the real function. Implement the cheap resident queries to round out the controlled register (the MCB 48h/49h/4Ah = 509.6, SETVECT/GETVECT 25h/35h = 509.8, FCB 0Fh-24h = 509.9, CREAT/write = 509.11 are separate). title: Harness: QMP keystroke injection (--keys) for interactive oracles
description: The QEMU harness (harness/emu/qemu.c + qemu_main.c) has QMP screendump but no way to inject keystrokes. The keyboard driver (initech-3rs), CON input (initech-n62), and the interactive shell (initech-7pc) all need an in-emulator oracle that types keys and asserts the OS response. Add a --keys option that, after the guest boots (a delay or a serial-marker trigger), sends QMP 'send-key' events (qcode sequence) over the existing QMP socket. Reuse qmp_send/qmp_drain. Mirror the existing --screendump plumbing. Oracle: a tiny boot test that echoes injected keys to serial proves a key sent via QMP reaches the guest.

Proven by the end-to-end test-kbd oracle (inject d,i,r -> guest echoes 'dir'); biting (no --keys -> no echo). QEMU-only (Bochs has no QMP send-key equivalent + is blocked at ERR-VBE, x0i).

title: Multi-file-open buffer pool (concurrent OPENs)
description: The 509.5 file backend (os/milton/fileio_fat.c) owns ONE static whole-file buffer, so a 2nd concurrent OPEN returns 0x0004 (too many open files / buffer busy). Real DOS FILES=20 allows many concurrent opens. Add a buffer pool (or the positioned partial-read above, which removes the need for whole-file buffers). Surfaced building initech-509.5.
notes: Absorbs snk's 'multi-open write handles': the pool must serve concurrent OPENs for BOTH read and write, each handle carrying its own position via fat12_read_partial/fat12_write_partial. Also owns: handle-parameterized backend vtable, int21+SFT rewire, and decoupling EXEC staging from FILE_BUFFER_BASE (memory_map.h).
close_reason: Multi-tenant positioned file I/O landed: backend vtable made positioned (read_at/write_at over the step-1/2 primitives), single 64 KiB whole-file buffer + file_data deleted, SFT slots are independent handles (root_slot added), EXEC staging decoupled. Proven by test-multiopen: 2 concurrent handles + independent positions + 96 KiB file read at offset 80000 (past the old cap); mutation-proven. make test green at 49 gates under load. Absorbed snk's multi-open write handles.

title: Positioned partial-read (fat12_read_partial) for large files
description: AH=3Fh READ currently relies on whole-file-read-at-OPEN into a single static 64KiB buffer (FILE_BUFFER_BASE). Files >64KiB cannot be opened, and only one file may be open at a time. Implement fat12_read_partial(vol,fat,entry,offset,count,buf) that navigates the cluster chain to offset/bytes_per_cluster and copies the requested slice, so READ is positioned over the chain without buffering the whole file. Brief Sec 4.2 'real read path (post-milestone)'. Surfaced building initech-509.5 file functions.
close_reason: fat12_read_partial landed: positioned cluster-chain read, host differential oracle vs independent python ref + mtools/dd (204 checks), mutation-proven (2 mutants bite). In TEST_UNIT_GATES; make test-unit green at 33 gates.

title: SFT teardown / re-init on process EXIT (multi-process)
description: sft_init() runs once at SYSINIT; the system SFT is not torn down or re-initialised when a process EXITs (4Ch). In the single-program cooperative model this is correct, but once a second program can load (or COMMAND.COM relaunches children), a prior program's open-file slots / redirected device slots would leak into the next process. On process EXIT the loader must release the process's JFT references (so file SFT slots free and the device slots' ref_counts reset) and/or sft_init must re-run. Surfaced building initech-509.3 (sft.c documents this as the SINGLE-PROCESS NOTE).
notes: Relevant when initech-509.5 (file OPEN) lands or when a multi-process/relaunch model arrives. See os/milton/sft.c SINGLE-PROCESS NOTE.
close_reason: sft_close_process walks the exiting process JFT and releases FILE-kind SFT slots (device slots 0-3 preserved by the kind gate), wired into do_terminate on g_cur_psp before g_exit. Proven by test-exit-handles (6 leaky EXEC runs x 4 opens = 24 > 16 slots, all succeed via reclaim) + mutation-proof (elide -> exhaust at run 5 -> RED). make test green at 50 gates under load.

title: INT 21h reentrancy hardening when IRQs are unmasked (DEC-04a C-5)
description: Per DEC-04a Consequence C-5: the int 0x21 trap gate (0x8F) leaves IF unchanged. Safe now ONLY because all IRQs are masked. When IRQ0(PIT)/IRQ1(keyboard) are unmasked (shell phase), an IRQ arriving inside the INT 21h dispatcher could re-enter it non-reentrantly (DOS INT 21h is not reentrant) and corrupt the frame. Harden: cli at int21_entry / sti before iretd, OR a reentrancy semaphore. Related: initech-n62 (keyboard/IRQ1), initech-3rs (PS/2 + PIT).
acceptance_criteria: INT 21h is reentrancy-safe with IRQs live (no frame corruption under an IRQ storm during a syscall).
notes: UPDATE (orch 2026-06-09): IRQs are now LIVE (initech-3rs unmasked IRQ0/IRQ1 + sti). INT 21h uses 0x8F TRAP gates (IF stays set), so a keyboard/PIT IRQ CAN now interrupt an in-flight INT 21h call. Currently SAFE purely because the kbd/pit ISRs share ZERO state with the dispatcher (verified: no refs to int21/g_dta/g_find/g_sft/g_cur_psp in kbd.c/pit.c). This bead's deeper audit is still owed: any future path where an ISR touches INT 21h state (or INT 21h calls kbd/pit while a search/DTA op is mid-flight) breaks the invariant -- then either mask IRQs around the critical section or make the state per-context. No locks now (cooperative model).
close_reason: Hardened: in-IRQ guard (g_irq_depth bracketed in the irq stubs) fails loud if INT 21h is entered from IRQ context; InDOS depth counter + dos_in_dos() hook (with do_exec snapshot/restore so EXEC chains don't drift it); kbd ring confirmed the sole ISR<->dispatcher shared structure (SPSC-safe). Proven by test-int21-irqstorm (5/5 enum + byte-exact multi-cluster read + 2nd handle under a 45-key + 100Hz-PIT storm) and 2 mutants (A: PIT scribble -> 4/5 enum -> RED; B: PIT int 0x21 -> guard panic -> RED). make test green at 51 gates under load. Verified by orchestrator (Rule 4); EXEC/conin/shell unaffected.

title: Ratify ADR amendment DEC-04a: 32-bit-flat INT 21h calling convention + IDT/PIC vector map
description: Research (docs/research/internals-int21h-ground-truth.md) surfaced load-bearing architectural choices for the INT 21h surface in 32-bit flat protected mode that are NOT derivable from ratified ADRs and warrant operator ratification (memory: ADRs are operator-ratified + authoritative): (1) literal int 0x21 via a TRAP gate (0x8F) at vector 0x21; (2) PIC remap master->0x28 / slave->0x30 (NOT the conventional 0x20/0x28) to keep vector 0x21 free for int 0x21 -- avoids the INT 21h<->IRQ1(keyboard) collision; (3) flat calling convention: AH=function (EAX[15:8]), flat ptr in EDX, count ECX, handle EBX, return EAX, error via CF in saved EFLAGS; (4) int21_frame_t layout matching the asm pushad order. These are being IMPLEMENTED now under a documented worklog decision (reversible); this issue tracks ratifying them as ADR-0003 amendment DEC-04a. ESCALATION: operator decision.
acceptance_criteria: DEC-04a drafted + ratified (or the convention revised per operator); spec/int21h_calling_convention.json locked to match.
close_reason: RATIFIED by ARB committee (3 reviewers Concur-with-comment: correctness/authenticity/governance) -> docs/adr/ADR-0003-AMENDMENT-DEC-04a-INT21h-Flat-Calling-Convention.md (full Initech house style + sign-off matrix). Committee found+fixed a real bug (do_getver BH mask) pre-ratification; oracle gap closed (test_int21 BH assertion). spec/int21h_calling_convention.json flipped provisional->ratified; test-spec green. Two forward obligations filed as beads.

title: Interrupt foundation: IDT + PIC remap/mask + CPU exception handlers + panic stub
description: No IDT exists; the kernel runs straight-line and halts. Prerequisite for the INT 21h trap (int 0x21 gate) AND hardware IRQs (keyboard/PIT, shell phase). Build: a 256-entry IDT (lidt), trap/interrupt gates, handlers for CPU exceptions 0-31 (-> fail-loud panic with vector + error code; the PC LOAD LETTER screen is initech-s25, a basic serial+console panic suffices here), remap the 8259 PIC away from CPU vectors 0x08-0x0F to 0x20-0x2F and MASK all IRQs (specific IRQs enabled later for keyboard/PIT). Foundational for InitechDOS internals (DEC-04/DEC-10). 32-bit flat protected mode (ADR-0001).
acceptance_criteria: IDT loaded; a software int reaches its handler; a deliberate CPU exception is caught and panics (not a silent triple-fault reboot); PIC remapped + masked, no spurious IRQ hits an exception vector; boot stays green.

title: FAT write + ECH byte-identity round-trip oracle (DEC-07 / section 7)

Delivered: ATA WRITE SECTORS 0x30 + CACHE FLUSH 0xE7 (ata.c, fail-loud); fat12_create/write_file/unlink (lowest-free cluster-chain alloc, both-FAT-copy sync, 12-bit packed-entry write = exact inverse of decode, deterministic mtime/mdate=0 per Rule 11); INT 21h AH=3Ch CREAT/40h WRITE-to-FILE (buffer-then-flush-at-close)/3Eh CLOSE-flush/41h UNLINK via the file-backend seam. Oracles: test-fat12-write (97,+? ) ; test-fat-write TRIPLE-agreement (our writer -> image -> mtools mdir/mcopy + python3 ref + our own reader, byte-for-byte content; normalizes date/time/serial) +2 mutants RED (one-FAT-copy, wrong-EOC); test-fatwrite in-emulator (CREAT+WRITE+CLOSE then OPEN+READ back through the OS on real ATA; post-run mcopy off the disk == 'hello'). Root-caused+fixed a kernel-size overflow (KERNEL_SECTORS 64->80 in Makefile+stage2.asm); all 22 gates re-verified green, triple_fault=0. Deferred: seek/partial write + multi-open (new bead), CHMOD/FILETIME (new bead), subdirs (ti8). QEMU-only (x0i Bochs).

After EXEC, 509.5's controlled register is functionally complete (CREAT 3Ch + FCB 0Fh-24h are separate beads 509.11/509.9).

title: PSP full 256-byte construction (DEC-05 / App B.2)
description: Construct full PSP on load per App B.2: INT 20h@00h, mem-ceiling@02h, saved INT 22/23/24 vectors@0Ah-15h, parent PSP@16h, JFT(20)@18h-2Bh, env seg@2Ch, INT21h/RETF@50h, default FCBs@5Ch/6Ch, cmd-tail+default DTA@80h. Majority vestigial, retained in full. Layout per spec/dos_structs.h psp_t.

title: Console-symbols fixture discrimination rests on unguarded symbol-table order
description: Post-landing review of bcf0ed57. The tier-0 fixture (factory/Makefile:100-103, tests/console-symbols-fixture/) distinguishes a size-qualified g_console_page reader from a last-match reader only because the 4-byte decoy comes AFTER the 4000-byte page in symbol-table order (readelf -sW on the built fixture: page idx 2, decoy idx 4; link order page.o then pointer.o). factory/tests/console-symbols.sh:13-14 refuses an ELF with no decoy, but never checks the order. Reproduced 2026-11-21: relinking the same two objects in reverse order (decoy idx 2, page idx 4) makes the gate mutant reader (factory/mutants/gates/console-symbols-last-match.patch) PASS console-symbols.sh with failures=0, while on the normal fixture it correctly FAILs (page=00011fc0 want 00011020). So a link-order or toolchain change silently turns the tier-0 check into a false pass; only the tier-2 gate-mutant sweep would notice. Fix: have console-symbols.sh assert the decoy follows the page in symtab order (e.g. readelf -sW ordering), so a non-discriminating ELF is refused. Red-first: the reversed-link fixture must be refused.

title: Tier-0 guard test-inputs.sh covers only Makefile recipe text: scripts and sub-makes in the test closure are unguarded

Reproduced: synthetic Makefiles whose test recipe is 'sh ./evil.sh' (evil.sh cats ../build/system/system.elf) or '$(MAKE) -f sub.mk check' (sub.mk recipe cats it) both pass with failures=0. Verified 2026-11-21 that every script currently in the closure is clean (only self-made scratch build/ paths), so this is latent: the next initech-qw018 is most likely introduced inside a test script, where build paths actually live, and the guard would stay green until a clean-checkout make test fails at the real check. Fix options: scan the scripts/sub-makefiles named by closure recipes for foreign build/ paths with a small allowlist for self-made scratch trees, or narrow the README/commit claim to recipe text only and accept the gap explicitly. Red-first: the two synthetic cases above.

title: test-inputs.sh misses foreign build paths already in make's database (variables, prerequisites, pattern rules, ../ traversal)
description: Post-landing review of bcf0ed57. factory/tests/test-inputs.sh claims to read 'the closure as make sees it' (line 5), but its awk (lines 14-41) scans only literal recipe text for $(TOP)/build/ or ../build/. Four shapes already present in the make -qp database escape it, each reproduced with synthetic Makefiles via the script's own [makefile-dir] argument (direct literal and double-colon controls correctly FAIL): (1) variable-indirect: ELF := $(TOP)/build/system/system.elf with recipe 'cat $(ELF)' passes failures=0 — the DB variables section is never scanned; (2) prerequisite + automatic variable: 'check: ../build/system/system.elf' with recipe 'cat $<' passes — deps strings are walked only for target membership (line 28), never scanned for build paths; (3) pattern rule: test depends on ../build/factory/toolx built by '../build/factory/%: %.c' whose recipe cats ../build/system/system.elf passes (INITECH_CHECKS 1) — implicit-rule entries are recorded under the pattern target and unreachable from the closure, and the concrete file is '# Not a target'; (4) traversal spellings: 'cat $(OUT)/../system/system.elf' and 'cat ../build/factory/../system/system.elf' both pass — the regex needs a literal prefix and the allowlist test q ~ /^factory\// (line 36) is not path-normalised. Why it matters: this guard is the only thing keeping tier 0 off other components' build output (initech-qw018, P0 clean-test failure); any of these ordinary Makefile idioms reintroduces it silently. Red-first check for a fix: these four synthetic cases must FAIL while the current factory Makefile stays green. Note the script also hard-codes the 'factory' allowlist while accepting a [makefile-dir] argument, so it cannot be reused for another component as written.

title: Turbo IDE PageLoad ignores work-file read errors after a successful page flush
description:
Location: turbo/ide/buffer.pas:179-233 (PageLoad reload loop and Reset at 190-191 have no IoNote/short-read check).

Scenario: navigation after a successful PageFlush; a work-file BlockRead fails or returns short during the reload half of PageLoad. The loop treats Got=0 as EOF, installs a truncated page with PgOrig=PgLen(short) and PgDirty=false, and BufErr stays 0, so DrawText shows no error. An edit on that page then flushes with the wrong PgOrig skip, duplicating/dropping suffix bytes in the work file; a later save can publish a corrupted document as success. The pending DOS error also leaks into the next IoNote elsewhere, misattributed.

Verified 2026-11-15 with the product's page-failure host binary: the shipped matrix (79 read/write positions) all lands in PageFlush; read fault at position 82+ (reload, 5000-line fixture) makes the harness print 'FAIL fault must be reported' (BufErr=0) and the retry RESULT.PAS is empty instead of the authored expected bytes. Re-review: reports/phase3/xreview-turbo-2.md finding 2. The 76j6x flush half itself is fixed; this is its unguarded reload half.

Red-first regression: extend page-failure read positions beyond the flush count into the reload reads (and the reload Reset); require BufErr reported, no truncated page installed as clean (keep the pre-navigation page or a retryable error state), and retry matching the independently authored bytes.
close_reason: Landed through2b6e642e: checked bounded reload candidate commits only after open/exact reads/close. Read/short-read/open/close fault matrix at both page ends, authored retry bytes, semantic premature-commit kill; both-emulator paged smoke green.

title: XCOPY refuses any file over 128 KiB, including its own 138 KiB XCOPY.COM, and aborts the whole copy
description:
Found in review xreview-dos-desktop (2026-11-15), commit ba678d18 (initech-gze1f fix).

dos/xcopy/xcopy_tree.c:38,254-256: transfer() buffers the whole source in a fixed 128 KiB static array and, for a larger file, prints Insufficient memory and sets error=4, which stops every remaining file (copy_dir loops on !error). Before ba678d18 XCOPY copied files of any size. The array is in .data, so XCOPY.COM and TREE.COM (same object) are now 138144 bytes each, and XCOPY cannot copy itself.

Reproduced with the shipped host tool build/dos/host/tool_test_xcopy_tree on an mtools image: SRC holds build/dos/XCOPY.COM (138144 B) and ZZZ.TXT; XCOPY 'SRC DST' prints Insufficient memory / 0 File(s) copied, exit 4; ZZZ.TXT is not copied. Destination bytes are preserved (no data loss). TURBO.COM (126612) and INITBASE.EXE (122768) are within 10 KiB of the limit.

README calls 128 KiB a local capacity, not a captured limit (constitution 5: no source for the number). Genuine DOS 3.30 XCOPY.EXE is now extracted (dos-owner-4 handoff, initech-0e5gu); capture its behaviour on a file larger than its buffer before keeping any cap. A retention design that streams large files can keep gze1f's property (no destination touched before the full source is read) only by staging to a temporary file or by verifying via a second pass; that choice needs a source.

Red-first test: in xcopy/tests/xcopy_tree.sh, XCOPY a directory holding the built XCOPY.COM and a second file; require both copied byte-exact (mtools).
close_reason: Landed 62a37bce on main. Red old cap at131073; genuine DOS3.30 XCOPY /V captured200000+followingfile success. Bounded2KiB staging through published INT21 CREATE_NEW/rename, source-read and /V failure retention, rollback and foreign-name guards graded by mtools.37XCOPY patches twice semantic killed; both emulators200000/V/fsck green; full two-emulator smoke and fresh rebased DOS/top plus DOS native allgreen. title: Certificate guard accepts GNU make := budget overrides in MAKEFLAGS
description:
Review-2026-11-15 at 5650a0e758cbda6cb0d25d1ebf14e494676381c3, factory/cert.sh:13-16 (f225fcf7). The guard rejects only literal space + setting + '=' in MAKEFLAGS, leaving GNU make's valid ':=' command-line assignment syntax untouched. A shell invocation env MAKEFLAGS=' -- TEST_BUDGET_S:=600' sh factory/cert.sh passes the guard; every nested make then receives TEST_BUDGET_S=600 with command-line origin, overriding component budgets. TEST_TIMEOUT_S:=600 works likewise. Unsetting the three environment variables does not remove MAKEFLAGS overrides.

Verified host-only without running a real certificate: /tmp/xreview-factory-word/cert-override.sh extracts the actual preflight through the unset (stops BEFORE id/work/stage code), then runs a tiny independent makefile that prints the effective settings and origins. The '=600' control is refused with exit 1. ':=600' is accepted with exit 0 and budget=600, origin=command line; the timeout variant prints timeout=600, origin=command line. Log: /tmp/xreview-factory-word/cert-override.log. The normal 'make cert TEST_BUDGET_S:=600' route can additionally be caught by the exported variable check; this finding concerns direct shell execution of cert.sh with inherited make flags.

Red-first acceptance: add these two MAKEFLAGS cases to factory/tests/cert.sh's controlled-stage fixtures; require refusal before clean-test starts. Normalize or discard inherited make overrides, or recognize all GNU make assignment forms and channels, before invoking sub-makes.

Report F4: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase3/xreview-factory-word.md. No product edit, smoke, emulator or real cert run.

description: aba737a4 (initech-q2w4b) reads the whole source once, discards it, rewinds with AH=42h and reads it AGAIN while writing (dos/xcopy/xcopy_tree.c:248-275). A read that succeeds on the probe pass but fails on the copy pass (soft/marginal sector, transient error) still truncates the old destination at CREATE and then deletes it at :275. Reproduced with the shipped harness: 5000-byte SRC\BIG.BIN over a 28-byte DST\BIG.BIN, XCOPY_FAIL_READ_AT=3 or 5 -> destination intact; =6 or 7 -> exit 5, 'Access denied', mtype: File ::DST/BIG.BIN not found. dos/README.md ('a source read failure at any offset leaves a pre-existing destination intact') and the comment at :270 ('An unreadable source never reaches here') overstate the guarantee. Genuine XCOPY buffers the file in memory, so for files that fit it cannot hit a read error after opening the destination. Red-first: add XCOPY_FAIL_READ_AT=6 to the q2w4b case in xcopy/tests/xcopy_tree.sh (red today). Fix candidates: copy from the buffered bytes, or write to a temporary name and rename only on success. title: InitechBase numeric GET keeps only the rightmost digits of an over-long entry (stores 0.12)
description:
Independent cross-provider review, 2026-11-15, origin/main c4722e74.

Unformatted numeric GET entry appends every key to g->raw, re-renders it, and copies only the rightmost `width` characters into the buffer (apps/initechbase/cmd/query.c, around the XB_N entry branch ~1594-1606: rt_memcpy(g->buf+(width-tn), text+(n-tn), tn)). Write-back parses that buffer. An entry longer than the field keeps only its tail.

Verified on the host (scratch harness against the built objects): N=12.50, @ 5,10 GET N, READ, Ctrl-Y then "123456789012345", Enter. N becomes 0.12 (READKEY 271). For a field N(10,2), "123456789" is accepted and stored as " 123456789", which is beyond the field's 7 integer places.

title: CALL with redirection fails Bad command or file name and never runs the batch
description: Reproduced 2026-11-14 on the booted product (probe in /tmp/call-probe.sh): in AUTOEXEC.BAT, call CHILD.BAT works, call with args works, CHILD.BAT > TRACE.TXT works, but call CHILD.BAT > TRACE.TXT (any args) prints Bad command or file name, creates no TRACE, and the child never runs. Root cause located: dos/command/command.c run_with_redirect (near 4077) pre-resolves external commands before opening output (compat33 REDIR BADNAME rule) and cmd_parse classifies CALL as CMD_EXTERNAL, so external_exists(CALL) fails. Batch control lines (batch_classify/dispatch_control kinds such as BL_CALL, and likely BL_IF/BL_FOR bodies with redirection) must be exempt from that pre-resolve. This is why every compat33 product case using call X.BAT > TRACE.TXT produces no TRACE today (see initech-inch5). Owner dos; fix red-first with a product session, keep the BADNAME capture behavior.

comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text:
## 02siz direct FAT inventory (all built product calls)

- finder_fs.c: mkdir; move_dirent; trash_suffix_name; unlink; rmdir; create;
  dir_identity; find_slot_in/read_partial; write_partial; format_83/read_dir;

- desktop_db.c: next_cluster free-space walk; find/read_partial bootstrap;
  find/read_file load; find/create/write_file/read_file verification,
  rename/rename rollback/unlink staging and commit; read_root_dir label;
  find/mkdir/hide_dir for Trash bootstrap/upgrade.
- finder_glue.c: find and find_slot_in for Apple-menu installed checks;
  find for Apple-menu launcher directory identity.
- volumes.c: fileio_fat_current_volume + fileio_fat_fat_buffer bootstrap;
  loader_bind_fat_volume and mounted record supply resident startup/loader.
- finder_storage.h: record-only FAT12 write policy and FAT16 cache selection;
  geometry checks/record types in actions/internal headers, not extra I/O.
No calls outside this list were found by rg fat12_|fileio_fat_ excluding
unbuilt kmain_legacy and test code. Its old two-bar/film arrangement stays unbuilt.

## Migration sequence and dependencies

1. Keep public signatures initially; move root Desktop DB byte reads to private
   DOS file sessions (3D/3F/3E), then staging/write/verification to 3C/40/3E and
   the existing published resident file_replace primitive. Use mtools readback
   and operation/sector failure sweeps. Preserve old destination under its own
   name after reported failure. Both-emulator gates before landing each step.
2. Replace binding operations mkdir/unlink/rmdir/read/write with DOS calls,
   resolving validated absolute paths from Finder directory identity. Preserve
   existing FAT16 refusal before writes and private PSP/CWD/DTA isolation.
3. Move enumeration/identity, Trash/Put Away/move, labels and Apple checks;
   remove the README temporary exception only when inventory is empty.

Concrete dependencies: kernel/int21.c do_rename explicitly rejects different
source/destination directories (AX=11h), directory targets (AX=5), per its
operator decision 2026-06-15. Finder Trash/Put Away and directory moves require
both. No Finder-only substitution preserves existing identity and move/safe
replacement behavior. Kernel owner must publish a permitted DOS/resident
binding or operator must amend that restriction. Also Finder DB and launcher
use physical directory clusters; public Find payload exposes attr/time/date/
size/name, not a child's cluster. The DTA reserved 21 bytes are explicitly
internal and cannot be used as a new Finder metadata interface. Need agreement
on path-based IDs/loader and persistence migration, or a published directory
binding. Do not launder FAT calls into a private platform entry or disk app.

## Owner requests read
## Operator instruction during this run

02siz remains deferred. The standing direct-FAT exception remains in force;
do not invent new move/identity services. Advisor/operator will decide scope.
Correction to migration analysis: REAL DOS 3.30 AH=56h DOES move a regular
closed file between directories on the SAME drive. It does not move/rename a
subdirectory or a hidden/system file; another drive is refused. Primary source:
Microsoft MS-DOS Version 3.3 Programmer's Reference, Function 56H Change
Directory Entry, Comments:
https://www.pcjs.org/documents/books/mspl13/msdos/dosref33/
(paragraph beginning 'The directory paths need not be the same').
Separate kernel fidelity issue filed: initech-50z67. No kernel edit authorized.

DOS 3.30 can supply path-based 39h mkdir, 3Ah rmdir (empty), 41h unlink (regular
file), 3Ch/5Bh create, 3Dh/3Eh open/close, 3Fh/40h read/write and 42h seek,
43h file attributes, 4Eh/4Fh enumeration/metadata (with private DTA), and 56h
same-drive regular-file rename/move. Free-space query 36h replaces the raw FAT
allocation walk; Trash suffix choice can use repeated Find on candidate paths.
Root Desktop DB staging/readback can use those calls plus the already published
resident file_replace commit primitive (a safe graphical save extension, NOT a
DOS 3.30 Rename claim). DOS enumeration can supply volume label, though its
formatted 8.3 result must preserve the raw 11-character volume-label spelling.
Still needing a decision/new binding or model migration: DIRECTORY moves and
renames for folder Trash/Put Away; stable physical directory identity and '..'
checks for persisted views/origins and the cluster-based loader; hiding the
service Trash DIRECTORY where DOS 43h refuses directory targets; and safe
cross-directory replacement with rollback for all the existing Finder routes.
No reinterpretation of reserved DTA bytes and no private FAT wrapper is planned.

create3Ch/5Bh, open/close3Dh/3Eh, read/write3Fh/40h, seek42h, attributes43h,

on the SAME drive. It does not move/rename a directory, hidden/system file or
another drive. Reference: Microsoft MS-DOS Version3.3 Programmer's Reference,
Function56H Change Directory Entry, Comments (directory paths need not match):
https://www.pcjs.org/documents/books/mspl13/msdos/dosref33/

Subdirectory bits: capture real3.30 before classifying other directory-attribute

title: Moving or resizing a hidden window distributes exposure for pixels it never owned
description:
Targeted Toolbox review of main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. No product changes.

flair/window.c:751 calls private visible_into directly even when w->visible is false; unlike ComputeVisible (:306), visible_into does not test visibility. MoveWindow treats the hidden old geometry as owned pixels and distributes false exposure at :774. set_document_frame repeats this at :810 for SizeWindow/CollapseWindow/ZoomWindow.

Concrete host sequence: create sole document frame (80,40,300,400), HideWindow, clear the correctly generated hide damage, MoveWindow(newLeft=100,newTop=120) while still hidden. No visible pixel owner changes, so desktop_update must stay empty. Actual desktop_update becomes nonempty. With underlying windows, false damage is instead delivered to their update regions. Hidden resize has the same problem. P2=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2.

Repair direction: compute no old footprint for an invisible actor; still update stored geometry. Check hidden move/resize/show against a literal owner-grid conservation property with underlying windows and an overlay. Preserve the intended caller-seeded actor repaint for normal visible moves.

title: Toolbox NEWWINDOW accepts inverted INT32 rectangles through signed overflow
description:
Targeted Toolbox review of main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. No product changes.

flair/tbxgate.c:451-452 subtracts r-l and b-t before fully bounding both endpoints. It checks l>=0 and r<=640 but omits l<=640 and r>=0; similarly it omits upper t/lower b. Inverted extreme rectangles can overflow the signed subtraction, pass the minimum size checks, then narrow to unrelated int16 geometry at :487-488.

Concrete INT81 sequence after valid REGISTER: NEWWINDOW(2147483547,60,-2147483548,280,2). Expected TBX_ERR_BADARG=-3 with no arena/list change (an inverted rectangle outside the desktop). Actual hosted unmodified gate built -O1 returns token 1, or token 2 when a normal window already exists. It constructs a window with x endpoints -101 and 100 and consumes the tenant's remaining window slot. UBSan stops at tbxgate.c:452:33: signed integer overflow: -2147483548 - 2147483547 cannot be represented in type int. This malformed call is used by privileged Toolbox arithmetic; no direct memory scribble is needed.

P2/toolbox-probes/gate.c; P2/toolbox-probes/run.sh <repo-root> runs both ordinary and UBSan builds. P2=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2. The prior interface report raised this question without establishing the bypass; do not fold it into fake-only issue initech-dcupi.

Repair direction: bound every endpoint before subtracting, or perform the dimension check in a wider type after proving the intended screen range. Add independent malformed-call tests requiring BADARG and unchanged heap/window state for both axes and INT32 endpoints. Source of truth: sdk/include/toolbox_gate.h section 3 bounded screen window geometry and the gate's explicit minimum dimensions.

title: Toolbox FILLRECT wraps wholly offscreen negative coordinates into visible content
description:
Targeted Toolbox review of main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c, 2026-11-14. No product changes.

flair/tbxgate.c:711-718 clips only against the content's upper endpoints, then narrows content-local int32 sums into int16. Far-negative coordinates wrap back into the visible window before the blitter clips. The additional visible/content clip still protects other windows; it cannot recover the requested geometry after narrowing.

Concrete INT81 sequence: REGISTER, NEWWINDOW(20,40,300,250,2), FILLRECT(1,-65536,-65536,-65526,-65526,TBX_COLOR_BLACK). The rectangle is wholly outside the window and must paint no pixels under toolbox_gate.h section 7's content-local clipped-drawing contract. Actual gate returns 0 and real blitter/surface change 100 pixels at the content origin (global x=26..35,y=62..71). This reproduces without undefined signed overflow. Extreme positive values additionally overflow the int32 additions in FILLRECT/TEXTDRAW (:612)/DRAWCELLS (:646-647); validate those through the same fix rather than only changing the fill cast.

P2/toolbox-probes/gate.c includes the existing real-gate routing fixture and links the real gate, region, blitter and surface implementations. The only renamed fixture stub is the blitter stub, allowing the real blitter to run. No SDK fake is involved. P2/toolbox-probes/run.sh <repo-root> prints DEFECT offscreen fill changed=100 pixels (expected 0), then returns nonzero. P2=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/phase2.

Repair direction: safely intersect in a wide coordinate domain before narrowing, or define and enforce explicit coordinate limits. Wholly clipped negative rectangles, partially clipped negative rectangles, int16 boundaries and INT32_MIN/MAX need independent pixel-set expectations. This is a new concrete product defect; the prior interface report only raised extreme-coordinate robustness as an unresolved question. It is separate from SDK-fake validation issue initech-dcupi.

title: Turbo Initech seed compiler reevaluates record assignment indices for each field
description:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: turbo/
Source report: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/review-turbo.md
Current file:line evidence and retained reproduction inputs/stdout/exit records were read and checked. No builds, make targets, emulators or tests were rerun during this filing. Earlier executions below are attributed to the reviewer.

Source finding: review-turbo.md #6

## Evidence
turbo/seed/codegen.c:1136-1140 invokes gen_field_addr for source and destination inside the per-field copy loop. gen_designator_base_addr at :1068-1069 calls gen_elem_addr; :978 invokes gen_index_byteoff for each field, reevaluating the index expression. The Pascal compiler instead copies through already-evaluated source/destination pointers at turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:4373-4396.

## Failing scenario
One record assignment invokes Index twice and combines the first field of src[1] with the second field of src[2]. Seed stdout is 2 11 22; FPC TP and Pascal Turbo Initech print 1 11 12. This probe demonstrates wrong values and repeated side effects; it does not demonstrate an out-of-bounds index.

## Failing program
```pascal
program probe;
type Pair = record a,b: integer; end;
var src,dst: array[1..4] of Pair; calls: integer;
function Index(dummy: integer): integer;
begin calls := calls + 1; Index := calls end;
begin
  src[1].a := 11; src[1].b := 12;
  src[2].a := 21; src[2].b := 22;
  calls := 0; dst[1] := src[Index(0)];
  writeln(calls, ' ', dst[1].a, ' ', dst[1].b)
end.
```

## Expected versus actual
| Execution | Output |
|---|---|
| FPC TP | `1 11 12` |
| Seed | `2 11 22` |
| Turbo | `1 11 12` |

Retained evidence: /tmp/turbo-defect-review/record-index/input.pas, reference.stdout (reference-longint.stdout for #4), seed.stdout/turbo.stdout and seed-exit/turbo-exit where generated. For #2 seed-build.log records rejection.

## Source of truth
Independent execution of the reproduction with Free Pascal in TP mode, as retained under /tmp/turbo-defect-review. CLAUDE.md constitution: The oracle is the truth; show the differential red before the fix. GOLDEN-MASTER item 7.

## Proposed fix
Evaluate and save each complete source and destination base address once, then copy fields from those pointers with the correct field direction.

## Red-first differential test and acceptance
Before fixing, execute direct seed output and compare exact stdout to fpc -Mtp: red is 2 11 22 versus 1 11 12. Preserve the Pascal path as a passing control. Extend gen_record_deep with separate source-only and destination-only side-effecting indices and self-copy; separating the sides avoids depending on their mutual evaluation order. Require index calls once per designator, intact record identity and correct field values. Existing constant/plain-variable indices and Pascal-only smoke do not exercise this seed defect.

Track shared execution coverage in existing task initech-h5uk7. Keep tier 0 emulator-free; use a suitable host runtime or the product-image tier-1/2 runner.

## Evidence limits
The reviewer used FPC 3.2.2, fpc -Mtp -B -O- -v0 references and a scratch-built C seed / FPC-hosted Pascal Turbo Initech compiler. Seed/Turbo results are executions of their emitted x86 assembly, linked with unchanged Multiboot startup and run under QEMU at 8 MiB. They do not verify resident loading/file runtime or native instruction encoding. Debug-exit status 1 denotes successful completion here; 124 denotes timeout. No product-image or self-host/DDC run is claimed. K2 == K3 alone cannot establish correctness of shared translation semantics.

title: Turbo Initech and seed compiler overwrite for counters before evaluating final bounds
description:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: turbo/
Source report: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/review-turbo.md
Current file:line evidence and retained reproduction inputs/stdout/exit records were read and checked. No builds, make targets, emulators or tests were rerun during this filing. Earlier executions below are attributed to the reviewer.

Source finding: review-turbo.md #5

## Evidence
turbo/seed/parser.c:1015-1016 constructs init_v and init_lim, then :1041-1042 emits the counter assignment first. turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:4701 stores the initial counter value before ParseExpression at :4710 evaluates the final bound. The final bound is saved once at :4719; this is an initialization-order defect, not repeated bound evaluation.

## Failing scenario

title: Turbo Initech and seed compiler for loops wrap past integer endpoints
description:

## Evidence
turbo/seed/parser.c:1018-1026 builds an inclusive guard and unconditional add/subtract step, appending that step after the body at :1033. turbo/seed/codegen.c:1345 emits wrapping 32-bit addition. turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:4726-4728 emits signed inclusive top testing, :4738-4739 unconditionally increments/decrements, and :4740-4741 jumps back. Neither path tests for the final value before the overflowing step.

## Failing scenario
A for loop from the maximum supported integer to itself executes twice and fails to finish within the recorded three-second timeout instead of executing once. Both outputs lack done. The descending minimum-endpoint analogue is inferred from the symmetric decrement path; add it to the regression tests. This termination bug is independent of the separate integer-width decision.

## Failing program
```pascal
program probe;
var i,count: integer;
begin
  count := 0;
  for i := 2147483647 to 2147483647 do
  begin
    count := count + 1;
    if count <= 2 then writeln('iteration ', count)
  end;
  writeln('done')
end.
```

## Expected versus actual
| Execution | Output / termination |
|---|---|
| FPC TP with `longint` declaration | `iteration 1` then `done`, exits |
| Seed with `integer` declaration | `iteration 1` then `iteration 2`, timeout 124; no `done` |
| Turbo with `integer` declaration | `iteration 1` then `iteration 2`, timeout 124; no `done` |

After the body, test whether the counter has reached its saved final value before stepping; retain the initial empty-range guard.

Require complete stdout iteration 1 followed by done and successful completion; current output iteration 1/iteration 2 and timeout 124 must fail. kernel/int21.c:293 stores one g_find; :3553-3556 emits zero resume fields; :3675-3682 resumes g_find without loading current DTA state. flair/tbxgate.c:1016 restores only DTA pointer.

## Failing scenario
Interleave FINDFIRST into DTA A and DTA B, restore A then FINDNEXT: B's exhausted cursor replaces A's enumeration. Child/Toolbox searches can destroy caller enumeration.

## Source of truth
MS-DOS Encyclopedia AH=4Eh/4Fh: first 21 DTA bytes carry search continuation.

## Proposed fix
Encode/decode and validate continuation from the selected DTA rather than a single global search.

## Red-first test and acceptance
Two independent expected file sequences interleaved across DTAs, plus EXEC child and Toolbox FILE_FIND; no skips/repeats and full caller continuation restored.

## Ground truth or decision needed
Implementation is substantial; choose a bounded validated DTA representation consistent with the flat ABI.

title: I123 B07: Accept the documented leading dollar sign in numeric entry
description: Root cause: os/i123/app/face_a.c:905-908 classifies $ as VALUE, but os/i123/core/fmt.c:653-668 accepts only an optional sign followed by digits/decimal point; commit at face_a.c:934-947 then attempts formula parsing and refuses $12.34. Ground truth: Lotus Reference p. 1-19 (PDF 35), audit evidence/references/manual-pdf-035.txt: a leading dollar sign enters the number and currency display is a separate format choice. Pickup: Recognize the documented typed-number currency prefix at the entry boundary without treating absolute formula references such as +$A$1 as numeric literals. title: SAMIR RUN verb: the PAL EXEC seam (nested EXEC from a running SAMIR.COM; loader.c rejects with LOADER_ERR_BUSY) -- test-samir-dml-run is pending by name
description: dBASE III PLUS RUN/! executes a DOS command from inside the interpreter. The real-III+ golden (xbase_prog_diff mint, case run) exists and the host/emu legs are written (test-samir-dml-run), but InitechDOS's loader refuses a nested EXEC while a program is resident (loader.c:1193 LOADER_ERR_BUSY) and the PAL has no EXEC seam. Design: a DOS-3.3-true nested EXEC (AH=4Bh from a resident .COM: save the caller's state, load the child above it, return the exit code) -- which SideKick (initech-6fdt) and COMMAND /C already need; then RUN returns to SAMIR_DML_CASES with its mutant. PM moved 'run' to SAMIR_DML_PENDING on 2026-10-17 (Makefile).
notes: 2026-10-20 part 2 landed on lane/samirrun (5562d6fe): PAL exec slot, RUN/! verb, run case back in SAMIR_DML_CASES, VERSION.TXT graded vs the same command processor's VER > VERREF.TXT (PM decision). PM-RATIFIED PENDING OPERATOR: shell kernels route EXEC COMMAND.COM to command_exec_secondary (the in-kernel COMMAND /C builtin) since the transient COMMAND.COM is not a loadable .COM; flagship follow-up bead filed. Two CRLF pairs around RUN are AUTHORED (golden cannot show which side).
close_reason: nested EXEC kernel half (a582c909) + SAMIR RUN/! via the PAL exec slot and COMMAND /C, run back in SAMIR_DML_CASES vs the real III+ golden (host + emu + mutants), VERSION.TXT graded vs the same command processor's VER; merged on main. Flagship EXEC COMMAND.COM guard -> initech-13ig

title: FLAIR as a command: boot to InitechDOS, type FLAIR (or let AUTOEXEC.BAT do it) to start the desktop, and Special > Exit to InitechDOS RETURNS to the prompt without a reboot -- the Windows 3.x / GEM-over-DOS flow the PRD names (operator question 2026-10-17: 'we can boot to dos, then start flair right?')
description: Today the flagship kernel enters the FLAIR pump before COMMAND.COM runs (BOOT_FLAIR_LIVE) and Exit to InitechDOS hands off one-way to the transient. Period-correct (PRD Sec 1.4, ADR-0012): the system boots to the banner and A:\>; FLAIR.COM (a small flat external in \DOS, or a shell internal) enters the resident Toolbox through a documented INT 21h/INT 81h gate; the desktop pump runs cooperatively over the shell's PSP chain; Exit to InitechDOS tears the desktop down (the existing exit path: alert, put away, DESKTOP.DB commit) and returns to COMMAND.COM with the console rebuilt -- no reboot; AUTOEXEC.BAT on the flagship volume ends with FLAIR so the shipped boot still lands on the desktop (the gates' boot markers and goldens stay byte-identical: the splash/desktop appear after the banner + AUTOEXEC, so every locked trace that starts at FLAIR-LIVE-OK is unchanged; the test-boot DOS legs see the banner first); the DOS-only images simply lack the FLAIR external. Oracles: emu gate test-flair-from-dos (boot the flagship with a data volume whose AUTOEXEC.BAT has no FLAIR line -> prompt; type FLAIR -> FLAIR-LIVE-OK; Exit -> SHELL-READY again; type FLAIR again -> desktop again: the round trip, twice), mutants (FLAIR returns to a reset console; second FLAIR fails), the TPS journey still green, test-boot/test-shell unchanged, Bochs leg; clip flair_from_dos (Rule 14). ADR-0003 amendment DEC-19 for the resident-Toolbox entry contract.
notes: 2026-11-02 PM: lane/flaircmd (d104e007, 6 commits, 33 files: FLAIR.COM arms the resident Toolbox via INT 81h TBX_DESKSTART, Exit returns to the prompt; test-flair-cmd-host +4 mutants were green on 2026-10-17; emu gate not done) archived as ../initech-lane-archive/branches-2026-11-02/lane_flaircmd.bundle + .vs-base.patch. 36 files conflict with main (kmain.c, transient.h/hdr, bochs_legs.mk, fixture_volumes.mk). NUMBERING COLLISION: the lane wrote ADR-0003 Amendment DEC-19 'Resident Toolbox Entry', but DEC-19 is now the operator-ratified INT 21h AH=4Bh AL=03h Load Overlay amendment (lane/phaseA-dec19, bead initech-dewv); renumber this one DEC-20 on revival. Kernel-size impact unknown; cap margin is 92 B.

title: Kernel .bin recipes: add Makefile prerequisite so size/placement guards cannot be silently skipped on constant changes

Padding proved byte-equivalent either way (sha256-identical images), so no corruption -- but the guard must be unskippable. Fix = add Makefile (or a dedicated geometry-stamp file to avoid full-rebuild-on-any-Makefile-edit) as an order-correct prerequisite across the kernel .bin recipes; Rule 7 Core tier (cross-cut, 48 recipes).

title: [bug] test_keep is address-dependent: g_arena_seg_base truncates the MAP_32BIT mmap address to 16 bits -- rare ASLR-draw RED (B1/B3/B4)
description: Observed 2026-08-24: test-keep went RED inside a full make test (4 failures: B1 resident-owner, B3 ALLOC-above + still-resident, B4 survives-reclaim) then GREEN standalone and 0/90 repeated runs (incl. big-env). Root-cause hypothesis (test_keep.c:319): g_arena_seg_base = (uint16_t)((mmap_addr >> 4) & 0xFFFF) -- a MAP_32BIT address >>4 is up to ~26 bits, truncated to 16, so the arena segment is effectively a random 16-bit value per run; placements near the 0xFFFF wrap (~0.02% of draws) break the B3 'got > seg_base+16' compare and the seg_owner lookups. Fix: derive test segments from an arena-relative base (e.g. force seg_base = a fixed constant by passing paragraphs relative to the arena, or assert/skip when (addr>>4) > 0xFFF0 window), never from truncated host addresses. NOT caused by the GUI lanes (none touch mcb/int21/test_keep; failure reproduced-in-principle from address math alone). Until fixed this gate is a rare coin -- a lone test-keep RED in a vector should be re-run standalone before blaming the diff (Rule 4), and this bead is the citation.

title: updateRgn-within-visible is an unstated load-bearing invariant: tenant updateEvt paint clips to contRgn+updateRgn only, so any stale seed surviving a z-order change lets a BACKGROUND tenant stomp the FOREGROUND's pixels
description: Found 2026-07-31 during the Wave A gofc/rqz5 landing (first-person, no delegation). MECHANISM: ref_tenant.c's updateEvt handler (and the ADR-0013 tenant contract generally) paints clipped to contRgn INTERSECT updateRgn, NEVER to the window's CURRENT visible region -- it trusts updateRgn subset-of visible(w) as an invariant. That invariant is maintained only OPERATIONALLY: WindowMgr_invalidate SECTs seeds with visible-at-seed-time, and the DQ2 pump order guarantees no z-order change intervenes between seed and route within one dispatch. But NOTHING re-clips PENDING damage when occlusion changes: any sequence of WM ops without a route/validate boundary (two NewWindows in a row at the tenants launch site was the live instance -- NOTES's brief-front full-struct activation seed survived HELLO launching on top of it) leaves stale damage that the route then delivers, and the tenant paints pixels it no longer owns (background stomps foreground). Caught live: test-flair-appswitch TIER-A went RED (overlap #C0C0C0 NOTES_FILL where #FFFFFF HELLO_FILL belongs) the moment desktop_paint_damage stopped blanket-validating. FIXED NARROWLY at the launch site (desktop_validate_all after the from-scratch shell_render, kmain.c step 4b) -- but the CLASS remains: any future multi-WM-op sequence without a cycle boundary re-opens it. PROPER FIX (BeginUpdate fidelity, IM I): flair_route_updates should clip the damage to the window's CURRENT visible region at delivery time (updateRgn INTERSECT ComputeVisible(w)) before synthesizing the updateEvt -- the exact semantics of BeginUpdate's visRgn INTERSECT updateRgn port setup. Needs a scratch-region discipline decision in process.c (ComputeVisible requires a caller scratch distinct from the manager's internals; route has no scratch param today). Alternative: a window.c verb that re-clips pending damage on every covering op (NewWindow/SelectWindow/ShowWindow) -- more invasive, keeps the invariant globally true. Oracle for whichever lands: a host test that seeds a background window with damage overlapping the front window (simulating the stale case), routes, and asserts the front window's pixels survive; mutant = drop the clip.
notes: R1.4 lane: RED-first three-window stale-seed case failed old route at test_process_update.c overlap; delivery now clips updateRgn INTERSECT current visRgn with Rule-2 subset assertion. Host 18 checks green; UPDATE_NO_VISCLIP red via BACK stomp. Emu intentionally not run per lane brief.

title: region_from_rects does O(n^2) self-union identity-copy; wide accumulations approach the per-row cap and fail-loud

For a wide multi-span accumulation each intermediate union approaches the per-row inversion cap (RGN_ROW_X_MAX); combined with the mswo fail-loud bound this makes moderately complex from_rects inputs fail-loud where a direct union-accumulate would not. Distinct from the cap-value question (initech-44ab): this is an allocation/algorithm-shape concern. title: Heap REUSE walks the entire class free-list instead of head-only — violates documented LIFO spec, strands undersized head blocks permanently
description:
[FLAIR bug-hunt R2 2026-06-28, wf_2f47b15b, adversarially verified] subsystem=FLAIR/heap (os/flair/heap.c).
EVIDENCE: heap.h:166-168 documents head-only ('if the free-list HEAD has cap>=request, pop it'), but heap.c:95-111 is a while(blk!=0) walk with a prev pointer that unlinks the first fitting node anywhere; a too-small head is skipped and a deeper block reused, and small head blocks never return to the bump allocator. The oracle (test_flair_heap.c:168-189, Property 2) tests only a single-element free-list, so head-vs-walk divergence is never exercised.

EXPECTED: If freelist[klass]->cap>=need pop head, else fall through to BUMP; a too-small head must not trigger a deeper search.

ACTUAL: Walks all nodes and reuses any fit regardless of position.

title: ADR-0013 tension: app-death survival vs WindowRecords-in-child-arena (Sec 3.4 vs 3.6)
description: ADR-0013 Sec 3.4 claims application DEATH (crash, not clean quit) survives a corrupt child arena because 'WindowRecords are caller-owned records the WindowMgr threads, so removing them from the z-order does not read the dead heap.' But Sec 3.2/3.6 has the tenant allocate its WindowRecords + region pools FROM its child arena -- so the z-order links (w->nextWindow) live in the arena that death corrupts, and DisposeWindow/z-order removal WOULD read the dead heap. Internal tension. Options: (a) WindowMgr keeps a separate window index not reliant on traversing arena-resident nextWindow; (b) tenant WindowRecords live in a shell-owned pool separate from the app DATA arena (split the arena: a shell-owned 'records' region + an app 'data' arena); (c) accept death-survival is best-effort and scope it to data-only corruption. NEEDS a committee ruling + ADR-0013 amendment. Clean teardown (close/DisposeWindow/one-shot-free/promote) + the O-3 leak invariant are UNAFFECTED and land in the first cut (initech-vi5k/xp5t); only the corrupt-arena-DEATH sub-test of O-3 is deferred pending this. Raised during App Contract Wave 3 orchestration.
close_reason: RESOLVED via ADR-0013 Amendment AC-2 (split-arena), committee-ratified + adversarial-verified (wf_00931e9e), commit 3eb39e4. Tenant WindowRecords + region pools now carve from a master-backed records_arena (FLAIR_CLASS_HANDLE) separate from the DATA arena; new FlairProcess_kill death path reads ONLY records-resident structural state, so app death provably survives a corrupt DATA arena. BC-6 now satisfied (was FALSE). O-3 gained the previously-deferred corrupt-arena death sub-test (scribble app->block -> kill -> list/z-order empty, no panic, avail stable); mutants UBD0_MUT_RECORDS_IN_DATA_ARENA (kill reads scribbled arena -> SIGSEGV/RED) + TEARDOWN_MUT_LEAK_RECORDS bite. 287 host + 57 emu + Bochs boot leg GREEN.

title: Harness: deterministic, regenerable GUI-interaction VIDEO capture (frame-stitch record mode + ffmpeg GIF/MP4 + make record-flair + auto-on-failure clip)
description:
GOAL: capture SHORT, REPRODUCIBLE videos of FLAIR GUI interactions for diagnosis -- temporal artifacts (the frozen-then-teleport drag of initech-34gp; the modal erased mid-drag of initech-pipa) are structurally invisible to single screendumps. Scripted/deterministic capture is the priority; output BOTH a lightweight GIF/APNG (embed in beads/worklogs) AND a high-fidelity MP4/WebM; integrate as BOTH an on-demand make target AND opt-in auto-capture on a red emu gate.

DESIGN (deep-research verified core, adversarially fact-checked against QEMU primary docs + the record/replay author's KVM-Forum talk; full report in docs/ or the session transcript):
- QEMU has NO native movie command; `screendump` (one frame; supports format=ppm|png since 7.1) is the only screen primitive -> VIDEO = stitch frames + ONE external encoder (ffmpeg). Keep the dependency footprint to exactly ffmpeg + the existing C QMP harness (Law 3).
- DETERMINISM (Rule 11): run QEMU single-CPU TCG (NO kvm) with a FIXED `-icount shift=N` (NEVER shift=auto -- auto resyncs to wall-clock and breaks reproducibility). Under fixed icount the guest virtual clock is a function of executed instructions, not host time. CLOCK the screendumps to the GUEST time base (a PIT-tick / serial FLAIR-FRAME marker the live build emits), NOT host wall-clock, so frame cadence is reproducible. Full bit-for-bit hardening = layer record/replay (rr=record once WITH the injected --mouse/--keys, then rr=replay to capture frames -- NOTE on replay live QMP input is IGNORED, events come from the log); but since the harness input is ALREADY scripted/deterministic, START with plain fixed-icount + guest-tick-clocked dumps and only add rr if frame nondeterminism appears (record/replay is historically fragile + version-pinned).
- ENCODE (ffmpeg only, both formats): GIF = palettegen/paletteuse single-pass split with stats_mode=diff (static desktop) + scale=flags=neighbor (crisp 8bpp pixel art, NOT lanczos); the indexed-8 palette reproduces exactly. MP4/WebM = libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p (or libvpx-vp9) with scale=flags=neighbor. For byte-reproducible outputs strip ffmpeg metadata: -fflags +bitexact -flags:v +bitexact -map_metadata -1 (no creation_time/encoder tag).

DELIVERABLES:
1. Extend harness/emu/qemu.c with a RECORD mode: dump screendump frame_%05d.ppm on each guest FLAIR-FRAME marker (or every K PIT ticks) while replaying a scripted interaction; add the -icount shift=N flag.

title: FLAIR live drop-shadow integration: widen window clip to include the shadow band (decouple drawer frame-rect from strucRgn clip)
description: Follow-up from initech-54nw. The documentProc 1px drop shadow at offset (1,1) is correctly EMITTED by flair_draw_document_window (graded GREEN by test-chrome-fidelity, host/unclipped) but is INVISIBLE on the booted desktop. Root cause (verified via screendump probe + desktop.c read): the live compositor clips each window's chrome to w->strucRgn (desktop.c:223 paint_window_chrome(dst,w,w->strucRgn,w->strucRgn)), and strucRgn == the window bounds rect (window.c region_set_rect(strucRgn,bounds)). The shadow draws at x=right / y=bottom, OUTSIDE [left,right)x[top,bottom), so clip_in() drops it. DESIGN HAZARD: the drawer's frame rect is itself region_get_bbox(w->strucRgn) (desktop.c:117), so naively widening strucRgn by the shadow band shifts bbox.right->561 and the FRAME would move to 560, shadow to 561 (wrong); it also changes occlusion semantics (fronts_union/visible_into) + drag-expose + FindWindow. Real System 7 CalcDoc: struct region = content + frame + SHADOW BAND (window-frame.md Sec 1, StandardWDEF_a.txt L1230-1235 InsetRect MinusOne + DBox shadow). FIX (region-layer): decouple the drawer's window-frame rect from the clip region -- e.g. pass the window-bounds rect to flair_draw_document_window explicitly while making the clip = strucRgn-with-shadow-band; OR composite the shadow in desktop.c into the exposed desktop region with z-order (a front window's shadow over a back window). Then amend ppm_flair_check (c) to assert x=W1_R is FRAME ink (shadow) + x=W1_R+1 teal. Sequences with the window-region / 5l5z event-loop work (shares strucRgn + expose math). Cite window-frame.md Sec 1/Sec 4.
notes: 2026-07-21 solidity forensics — ROOT FOUND: the drop shadow IS drawn (chrome.c:854-865, column at x=right, row at y=bottom) but both write 1px OUTSIDE the window frame == strucRgn bbox (desktop.c:133,139), and clip_in (chrome.c:66-80) rejects everything outside visRgn ⊆ strucRgn — every shadow pixel is discarded. Fix = the already-planned strucRgn widening (CalcDoc-style shadow band, ../system7-decomp/specs/chrome/window-frame.md L36: struct = content grown 1px + shadow band) so visible(W) includes the shadow band; exposure/damage math then handles shadow erasure for free. In epic initech-av7s scope.

title: Kernel-growth runway exhausted at PROGRAM_BASE=0x40000 -- next growth needs high-half / extended-memory relocation
description: re30.2 (Step A) performed the SECOND +0x8000 whole-map shift (0x38000->0x40000), spending the LAST of the conventional free gap. The kernel stack region is now [0x90000,0xA0000), ESP=0x9FFFC, butting the 0xA0000 VGA / mode-0x13 LFB fallback aperture with ZERO gap (disjoint: 0x9FFFC < 0xA0000, but no slack). This is the MAXIMUM PROGRAM_BASE raise possible under the conventional-memory (<640 KiB) scheme: a third +0x8000 shift would push the kernel stack top into/over 0xA0000. The kernel.ld B0 ASSERT and memory_map.h now say so. CONSEQUENCE: any future kernel-resident growth past the current ~17 KiB shell-kernel headroom (FLAIR call sites in re30.3+, the verb layer, more Managers, MILTON redirection) cannot be absorbed by another raise. The mitigation when this binds: relocate the kernel and/or its stack to a high-half / extended-memory layout (the FLAIR heap already lives at 0x100000+; ADR-0001 makes >1 MiB directly addressable in flat 32-bit). This needs an ADR/committee decision (kernel link base, stack placement, stage2 load path, the self-host fixpoint determinism implications). NOT urgent now (re30.2 fits with ~17 KiB to spare) -- file-and-watch. title: Loader: child PSP inherits the parent JFT (enables external EXEC output redirect)
description: psp_build (os/milton/psp.c) HARD-RESETS the child JFT standard handles to CON (jft[0]=0 stdin, jft[1]=1 stdout, jft[2]=1 stderr, jft[3]=2 aux, jft[4]=3 prn) on every EXEC, ignoring the parent's open/redirected handles. Authentic DOS has the child INHERIT the parent's JFT (the AH=4Bh child gets a copy of the parent's handle table). RESULT: COMMAND.COM's > / >> redirect (hsct OUTPUT increment) works for BUILTINS (they run in the shell's own PSP with the DUP2'd handle 1 -> file) but NOT for external .COM EXEC children (their handle 1 is reset to CON). Empirically confirmed: GREET.COM> GOUT.TXT prints GREETINGS to SCREEN and leaves GOUT.TXT empty. FIX: thread the parent JFT (handles 0..4, or all 20) into psp_build via a params field and copy them into the child PSP when a parent PSP exists (g_cur_psp at EXEC time). Oracle: a child-inherits-parent-JFT property test + an emu gate mirroring test-hsct-redir but EXEC'ing GREET.COM> file and asserting GREETINGS appears via TYPE (from the file), not on screen during the EXEC. Touch: psp.c/psp.h/loader.c (the loader/PSP layer hsct deliberately did NOT touch). Ref: ADR-0003 DEC-06; MS-DOS 3.3 Tech Ref (handle inheritance on EXEC); the hsct OUTPUT increment driver already brackets EXEC correctly -- zero command.c change needed once this lands.

title: IOCTL AH=44h fidelity (4nbn): AL=08 takes BL=drive not a handle; AL=01 asserts an invented DX output
description:

Current working rules: component make test/smoke/mutants and orchestrator local make cert, under CLAUDE.md named sections. Prior evidence (names/ownership normalized; line numbers and observations remain historical, not fresh reproductions):
Adversarial review of initech-4nbn (both P3, benign): (1) real DOS AX=4408h (Is-Block-Device-Changeable) takes BL=drive-number on a BLOCK device, not an EBX/JFT handle; our model resolves EBX as a JFT handle and always returns AX=0x0001/CF=1 (not-applicable, since the SFT exposes no block-device handle). (2) AL=01h Set-Device-Info is modeled as a no-op success that echoes DX=0x80D3, but real DOS 4401h does not define DX as an output -- the oracle over-asserts an invented return (WL-0025 'oracle asserts a value the contract doesn't produce', benign). comments.text:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: kernel/
Source findings: review-interfaces.md #14 (known SET/4408 portion)
Reports: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports
Evidence checked by reading the current tree. No make, emulator, mutation or test run was performed during this triage. Reported earlier experiments are attributed, not repeated.

## Evidence
kernel/int21.c:1828-1845 accepts SET raw-mode request without changing behavior and echoes locked DX; :1898-1906 resolves 4408's BL drive operand as a JFT handle.

## Failing scenario
Raw-mode SET succeeds but following input remains cooked; 4408 with a valid drive can fail as invalid handle. This existing issue is deferred; evidence comment does not reopen or reprioritize it.

## Source of truth
MS-DOS Encyclopedia 4401h/4408h; SET has no specified DX result. Needs ground truth captured first for supported local raw-mode transitions.

## Proposed fix
Implement or visibly refuse unsupported SET changes, relax invented DX assertions and resolve 4408's drive contract within operator-approved scope.

## Red-first test and acceptance
Captured raw Ctrl-Z/no-Enter transition and 4408 drive operands independent of JFT; do not assert undefined DX output.

## Ground truth or decision needed
Should raw mode and 4408 be implemented now or explicitly refused/documented while deferred?

Evidence comment only: existing title, priority, type and status are unchanged.

title: FAT12 allocator: free-cluster search hints from prev+1, can falsely report NO_SPACE under fragmentation
description: Lens-2 finding during zs24 L1 verification (pre-existing, NOT introduced by zs24). fat12_grow_dir (fat12.c ~1120) and the file-extend/write paths (fat12.c ~1796, ~2056) call fat12_find_free(vol,fat,fat_len, prev+1), i.e. search for the lowest free cluster AT OR ABOVE the current tail. If all free clusters sit below the tail, allocation returns FAT12_ERR_NO_SPACE even though space exists. Mirrors the established extend convention so it is self-consistent, but a fragmented volume can spuriously fail. Fix uniformly across all three call sites (wrap-around search from cluster 2) with a fuzz case that places free clusters only below the tail. Low priority (floppy/low-fragmentation today).

comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text:
Additional confirmed Phase-2 evidence for initech-9wx9, main 09d52a32173911debc13035096135143fefb4b2c. kernel/fat12.c:2925-2928 (and whole-file allocation :2610).

A healthy mtools FAT12 image has TARGET.BIN, 512 bytes, at last data cluster 2848. Fill the preceding 2846 clusters with FILL.BIN then delete FILL.BIN. 1,457,152 bytes are free, all below TARGET's tail. Appending ONE byte with the real fat12_write_partial returns rc=-11/wrote=0; the DOS backend converts this to a zero-byte short write. mcopy can immediately create CONTROL.BIN on that image, and fsck.fat -n is clean. This is still present in the file paths even though initech-fov8 fixed directory growth's fallback.

Reproducer, exact mtools recipe, images and red assertion: reports/phase2/kernel-repro/{fat_probe.c,run-fat.sh,fragment.img,check.sh}; sh check.sh fragment exits 1, expecting the requested 513-byte result but finding 512. No issue duplicated. Attach component:kernel and review-2026-11-14 to route this to the actual owner.

Nested MD/RD does NOT fall out trivially: fat12_mkdir writes the new dir's own 8.3 entry into the PARENT via the root-only fat12_write_dirent(free_slot) and scans the parent via fat12_scan_root; both must move to the new parent-aware fat12_scan_dir + fat12_write_dirent_in_dir, and the parent-full case must GROW the parent subdir (fat12_grow_dir, already available). fat12_rmdir's empty-check is already subdir-capable (uses fat12_read_dir on the target). ORACLE: a nested '\SUB\NEWDIR' differential vs 'mmd ::SUB/NEWDIR' (mirror test-fat12-mkdir) + the do_mkdir/do_rmdir int21 path, plus a per-primitive mutant. Pointers: os/milton/fat12.c fat12_mkdir/fat12_rmdir parent_dir_start guards; os/milton/fileio_fat.c fat_mkdir/fat_rmdir dir_start!=0 guards; os/milton/int21.c do_mkdir/do_rmdir.
