title: INT 21h subdir EXEC + subdir WRITE (CREAT/UNLINK/WRITE inside a subdir)
description:
Follow-up split out of initech-mzxa (ti8 Layer 2). mzxa wired the READ-side subdir resolution into the INT 21h file backend: OPEN/READ + FINDFIRST/NEXT now resolve and enumerate \SUB\FILE paths via fat12_resolve_path/fat12_read_dir (real-backend integration green). TWO deferred pieces, both because the underlying fat12 write/load primitives are ROOT-only:

(1) do_exec (AH=4Bh) stays ROOT-ONLY (mzxa decision 3): the EXEC source feeds the loader program-load path (load_program_from_fat -> load_program), which locates the .COM by a ROOT-dir 8.3 name. Threading a resolved containing-directory cluster into the loader is a riskier loader-internal change; mzxa kept do_exec rejecting subdir paths (path_has_subdir_or_drive at int21.c do_exec). This bead: let EXEC load a program from a subdirectory by resolving the source path to its dir_entry and feeding the located entry's own start_cluster to the loader.

(2) CREATE/UNLINK/WRITE inside a subdirectory: fileio_fat.c fat_create/fat_unlink return 0x0003 for a non-root dir_start_cluster (fat12_create/fat12_unlink/fat12_write_partial work over the ROOT dir + a root-dir slot for write-back). The mzxa file backend threads dir_start through create/unlink additively (param present, root==0 byte-identical), but the WRITE primitives must become subdir-aware (allocate a dir slot in a subdir cluster chain, write-back into it). This is the FAT WRITE-side subdir work (sibling of initech-509.11).

GROUNDED POINTERS (mzxa session): fileio_fat.c fat_create/fat_unlink non-root guards; int21.c do_exec path_has_subdir_or_drive; the resolve seam (int21_file_backend_t.resolve + resolve_dir_path). ORACLE: extend test_fileio_subdir.c (real backend) with subdir CREAT/WRITE/UNLINK round-trips + a subdir EXEC over a nested data disk.

title: ti8 Layer 2: thread resolved subdir through the INT 21h file backend (vtable cross-cut + g_cwd)
description:
Core-tier cross-cut (Rule 7) split out of initech-ti8 after grounding (workflow wf_fc0ea9c9-a7a, this session). ti8 Layer 1 (fat12.c: fat12_dir_t + fat12_read_dir + fat12_resolve_path, READ-side) is additive and self-contained, oracle-gated at the fat12 layer. THIS bead is Layer 2: actually wire subdir-path resolution into the INT 21h DOS API so OPEN/FINDFIRST/etc. resolve \SUB\FILE paths.

WHY SEPARATE: the int21_file_backend_t vtable (int21.h:149-220, VERIFIED) is purely root-relative today (open()/create()/dir_entry()/unlink() take only name83 / a flat index). Threading a resolved directory (a uint16 start_cluster, 0=root, is the lowest-coupling thread) is a multi-file change: int21.h + fileio_fat.c (real backend, fat_open@81/fat_dir_entry@147) + THREE host mocks in lockstep (test_fileio.c@319, test_int21.c@103, test_int21_edge.c) or nothing compiles.

GROUNDED SCOPE (all line numbers VERIFIED this session, the brief's were stale):
- 5 path_has_subdir_or_drive() rejection sites to replace with resolve_path: do_open@858, do_creat@931, do_unlink@995, do_findfirst@1405, do_exec@1476. Preserve AX=0x0003 PATH_NOT_FOUND on a bad/non-dir component (keeps do_geterr AH=59h class/action/locus green) and preserve the INT21_PATH_SCAN_MAX overlength fail-loud + the INT21_MUTATE_PATHSCAN_NOBOUND mutation oracle.

title: Shell: environment store + SET built-in + EXEC env inheritance
description: No environment exists: the env block is a fixed 2-byte empty stub (loader.c:256, ENV_BLOCK 0x5F000) and EXEC passes env_block=0 (command.c:433). Build a real master environment (PATH/COMSPEC/PROMPT vars), a SET built-in (set/list/clear), and per-process env copy passed through exec_param_block_t.env_block to the child PSP. Underpins PROMPT, PATH, and batch %VAR%.
design:
TRANCHE-E design (grounded WL-0037+ audit). Three increments, each RED->GREEN->mutation-proven->make test, SERIAL on shared files (Rule 3):
INC-1 (no shared-file risk): NEW pure-logic module os/milton/env.c + env.h -- a freestanding master environment store (fixed-capacity arena, NO libc): env_set(name,val) (upsert, upcases name per DOS), env_get, env_unset (NAME= clears), env_count/iter, and env_serialize(buf,cap)-> DOS-format block = sequence of ASCIIZ 'NAME=VALUE\0' strings + a final extra '\0' (empty env = lone '\0\0'). Host oracle test_env.c (HOSTED, like cmd_* TU). Seed PATH/COMSPEC/PROMPT.
INC-2 (command.c): NEW CMD_SET in command.h enum + cmd_classify table row; cmd_set handler: 'SET' lists 'NAME=VALUE' lines, 'SET NAME=VALUE' upserts, 'SET NAME=' clears. Wire the global master env into kmain shell loop. test via test_command + an emu DIR-style leg later.
INC-3 (loader.c): on EXEC, env_serialize the master env into ENV_BLOCK (0x5F000) and pass env_linear=ENV_BLOCK (not 0) so child PSP env_seg points at the real block (psp_build already does flat_to_fake_paragraph). Per-process: child inherits a COPY (already physically separate region). Mutation: drop the serialize -> child sees empty env -> oracle RED.
Ground truth: DOS env block format = ASCIIZ NAME=VALUE strings, double-NUL terminated (Ralf Brown INT 21h/AH=4Bh EPB + PSP:2Ch). DOS 3.0+ trailing word-count=1 + progpath is OPTIONAL nicety, deferred. Unblocks dibc(PROMPT)/atf(PATH)/xw1(batch %VAR%).
close_reason: Tranche E complete: env store (inc-1) + SET built-in (inc-2) + EXEC env inheritance (inc-3), all RED->GREEN, mutation-proven, 220 host gates + test-program emu EXEC green.

title: Loader control-transfer asm reads jump target via memory operand after switching ESP
description: Entry asm (loader.c:323-336) does mov stack_top,%esp THEN jmp *entry_eip where entry_eip is a memory operand. Correct only because KERNEL_CFLAGS is -O0 with a frame pointer (EBP-relative locals resolve into the kernel frame). If the build moves to -O2 or -fomit-frame-pointer, entry_eip/psp_ptr/stack_top become ESP-relative and jmp *%4 dereferences the just-switched PROGRAM stack -> garbage/triple-fault. No compile-time guard pins this. Audit: loader-psp loader-asm-jmp-reads-operand-after-esp-switch.
acceptance_criteria: Load entry_eip into a dedicated register BEFORE the ESP switch (or pin the fn with an optimize/no-omit-frame-pointer attribute + a guard); behavior unchanged at -O0 and -O2; make test green.
close_reason: Entry asm loads the jump target (entry_eip) into EAX BEFORE the ESP switch and jmps via register, eliminating the only post-switch memory read. By construction optimization-safe. Demonstrated RED->GREEN at -O2 -fomit-frame-pointer (pre-fix: GREET.COM never runs; fixed: passes); no -O0 regression. The permanent -O2 coverage arrives free when the toolchain moves to -O2/i686-elf (initech-6pm/CDR-0001) -- test-exec then becomes the -O2 gate and now stays green. make test 55h+21e GREEN.

title: CONFIG.SYS larger than 1024-byte scratch is silently discarded (comment claims truncation)
description: sysinit_apply_config reads CONFIG.SYS into static char cfg_buf[1024] via fat12_read_file, which returns FAT12_ERR_BUFFER (does NOT truncate) when file>buf. So a >1024B CONFIG.SYS makes from_disk stay 0 and the user's whole file is silently ignored for SYSINIT_CONFIG_BASELINE; summary prints source=baseline masking the discard. Comment at sysinit.c:134-135 wrongly claims truncation. A 1024B CONFIG.SYS is period-realistic. Audit: sysinit-boot configsys-oversize-silent-baseline-fallback (+ sysinit-phases-no-host-test).
acceptance_criteria: Either honor truncation via incremental read, or fail loud (distinct 'SYSINIT: CONFIG.SYS too large' marker before fallback) and fix the comment; factor the file-read so sysinit_apply_config is host-drivable with an injected fake; host tests for from_disk success, oversize, FILES-absent baseline=20, FILES clamp; make test green.
close_reason: sysinit honors first 1KB of an oversize CONFIG.SYS via fat12_read_partial (trim to last line) + flags it 'source=CONFIG.SYS(truncated@1024)' instead of silently discarding to baseline (operator choice). Fixed misleading comment. New test-sysinit-oversize gate (oversize fixture, FILES=8 in first lines): RED (baseline FILES=20) -> GREEN (truncated@1024 FILES=8), mutation-proven. make test 55h+21e GREEN.

title: dos_reentry_panic serial output spins unbounded on a dead UART
description: panic.c bounds its serial spin (PSERIAL_SPIN_MAX) precisely so the fail-loud path cannot wedge. The sibling path irq.c rserial_putc (irq.c:60-66) spins while !(LSR&THRE) with NO bound; on an absent/stuck UART (common 86Box config) dos_reentry_panic hangs before it can int3 into the real panic -- defeating the loud-and-bounded guarantee. Audit: interrupts dos-reentry-panic-unbounded-serial-spin.
acceptance_criteria: irq.c rserial_putc uses the same bounded spin (PSERIAL_SPIN_MAX, drop byte on timeout) as pserial_putc; make test green.
close_reason: bcg.5: do_puts NULL-guard + INT21_PUTS_SCAN_MAX bound; RED (NULL deref segfault)->GREEN, mutation-proven. bcg.8: rserial_putc bounded by RSERIAL_SPIN_MAX mirroring panic.c (target-only port I/O; emu irq-storm serial path confirms no regression). make test 55h+19e GREEN.

title: 8259A spurious IRQ7 (0x2F) / IRQ15 (0x37) wedge the machine; no spurious-IRQ EOI discipline
description: Vectors 0x2F/0x37 are never installed with real handlers, so an 8259A spurious interrupt (INTR deasserted before ack -- electrical noise/timing) lands on isr_spurious -> permanent cli;hlt. Real-hw contract: master spurious (IRQ7) -> send NO EOI; slave spurious (IRQ15) -> EOI to master only. On period PCs (Rule 5) one line-noise glitch on IRQ7 halts the system. title: CONFIG.SYS decimal-overflow guard off-by-one (config_sys.c:76)
description: cfg_parse_uint guard 'if (v > 429496729u)' is checked before v=v*10+digit; at v==429496729 with next digit 6-9 the multiply-add overflows uint32 and WRAPS instead of saturating at 0xFFFFFFFF (the documented contract). 2^32-family values (e.g. FILES=4294967296) wrap to ~0 and clamp UP to FILES_MIN instead of DOWN to FILES_MAX. Benign (still in-range) but violates the saturation contract. Found by the wave-B CONFIG.SYS fuzzer (initech-hjv). Fix: guard 'v > (0xFFFFFFFFu - digit)/10u'. Must update the fuzzer's ref_parse_uint to the corrected saturating logic + add an explicit 2^32-family clamp-to-MAX assertion + a mutant restoring the off-by-one.
close_reason: Fixed in this commit: precise overflow guard (v > (UINT32_MAX-digit)/10), fuzzer ref updated in lockstep, off-by-one mutant added + caught. 55 host + 19 emu green.

title: Build-time guard: kernel _kernel_end must stay below PROGRAM_BASE (0x20000)
description: The kernel size guards in the Makefile check only the LOADED .bin size vs KERNEL_SECTORS*512 -- they do NOT check that _kernel_end (the end of .bss, which is NOT in the .bin) stays below PROGRAM_BASE (0x20000). During 509.2 the shell kernel's .bss (cfg_fat_buf[4608]) pushed _kernel_end to 0x1FF60 -- only 160 bytes below PROGRAM_BASE -- a SILENT near-collision the existing guards could not see (the .bin still fit). A future kernel .bss growth would silently corrupt the program-load region (0x20000). Add a build-time check (extract _kernel_end via nm from each kernel ELF, assert < PROGRAM_BASE with a margin) so this fails LOUD (Rule 2) like the .bin-size guard does. Apply to all kernel variants (or the largest as a canary). Cite spec/memory_map.h PROGRAM_BASE.
acceptance_criteria: Building any kernel whose _kernel_end >= PROGRAM_BASE (or within a small margin) fails the build with a clear message naming _kernel_end and PROGRAM_BASE; deliberately bloating a kernel's .bss past 0x20000 is caught at build, not at runtime.
close_reason: Build-time _kernel_end < PROGRAM_BASE guard added to all 15 kernel .bin recipes: nm extracts _kernel_end, asserts < PROGRAM_BASE-256 (parsed from spec/memory_map.h), fails loud with actionable message. Mutation-proven (orchestrator independently: 0x1000 .bss bloat -> _kernel_end=0x20d60 -> build RED; .bin guard stayed green proving the gap closed). Current headroom: 480 bytes.

title: FINDFIRST DTA layout deviates from real-DOS byte offsets

Our DIR.COM reads our offsets so it is self-consistent, but the DTA is NOT byte-compatible with real DOS -- a real-DOS program (or a differential test vs real DOS FINDFIRST) would read garbage. title: Selected DOS tests pass TESTS into kernel catalogue generation
description:
In a clean checkout, make -C dos test TESTS=fdisk-session stops before the selected test if build/kernel/dos_messages.h has yet to be generated. dos/Makefile calls the kernel make for the catalogue and make forwards the DOS-only TESTS override. Kernel registration rejects it with "unknown TESTS: fdisk-session".

Reproduced without changing files from the root using: make -n -C dos -W "$PWD/kernel/include/dos_messages.json" "$PWD/build/kernel/dos_messages.h" TESTS=fdisk-session. The command exited 2 at mk/host-test.mk:14. Log: /tmp/initech-5o7p3/selected-catalog.log. Run make catalog first as a workaround. Default top-level tests and the DOS mutation runner work.

Keep the selected DOS test in the outer make and scope TESTS out of the kernel catalogue prerequisite. A clean selected run should generate the header and execute fdisk-session, with a summary for that single test.

title: InitechBase flush adds 0x1A EOF to no-EOF DBF inputs (conformance C03/C04)

Genuine III+ captures C03 (partial-record) and C04 (missing-record): real III+ REPLACE fills the row in place and leaves the file without a 0x1A EOF byte; InitechBase whole-file flush always emits 0x1A (fs/dbf.c dbf_serialize, documented S1.4 decision). Reader diff: tail REF '' HOST '1a' for BASE.DBF and SAVED.DBF, all other meaningful bytes equal. C03/C04 removed from tests/conformance/accepted.cases as known failures until the operator decides whether flush should preserve a missing EOF on damaged inputs or the S1.4 always-emit decision stands.

Decision owner: operator + committee.

Implement AL=01 (set device-info word back), AL=06 (get input status: AL=0xFF ready / 0x00 not-ready), AL=07 (get output status), AL=08 (changeable media, block-device only) as thin SFT-derived answers; ground the bits from the DOS 3.3 PRM.
notes: Adversarial review of ro6c (2026-06-15) found int21.h:63-68 mislabels the device-info bit NAMES for bits 1-4 vs the real MS-DOS char-device contract. Correct layout to ground from the PRM/RBIL: bit0=stdin, bit1=stdout, bit2=NUL, bit3=CLOCK, bit4=special, bit5=raw/binary, bit6=not-EOF-on-input, bit14=IOCTL-strings, bit15=ISDEV. The header currently has ISCIN=bit1/ISCOT=bit2/ISNUL=bit3/ISCLK=bit4 (shifted one position). These macros are DEAD today (CON=0x80D3 literal + ISDEV/STDIN are the only ones referenced) and the shipped VALUE 0x80D3 is correct, so NO behavioral impact -- but this bead MUST correct the bit-name labels (PRM-grounded) before implementing the AL=01/06/07/08 minors against them.

comments.author: tobiasosborne
comments.text:
Review triage: 2026-11-13, main at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918. Component: kernel/
Source findings: review-interfaces.md #5 and #7
Reports: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports
Evidence checked by reading the current tree. No make, emulator, mutation or test run was performed during this triage. Reported earlier experiments are attributed, not repeated.

## Evidence
kernel/int21.c:3240-3244 makes CLOSE(0..4) a no-op even after redirection; :2368,2470 accepts/stores unvalidated OPEN mode; :1113-1115 compares whole mode byte for WRITE. kernel/psp.c:219-223 inherits every handle; sft_inherit does not filter bit 7.

## Failing scenario
Redirect a file to handle1 then CLOSE(1): it remains usable. AL=03h OPEN succeeds; AL=81h opens but WRITE is denied and child inherits it. Existing umbrella explicitly covers close-predefined-handle leak and open-mode-not-validated; no duplicate filed.

## Source of truth
DOS 3.3 PRM AH=3Dh/3Eh and IBM p.4-15. Access, sharing and inheritance are distinct fields. Needs ground truth captured first for exact local SHARE-absent sharing matrix; no network scope expansion.

## Proposed fix
After resident-lifetime repair, close all valid handles uniformly; mask access bits, reject invalid/reserved modes and omit noninheritable entries in child construction.

## Red-first test and acceptance
Redirect/close each 0..4, then READ/WRITE/CLOSE must error6 and next OPEN reuse handle; AL=03h rejects with error12, AL=81h writes but child entry is closed; test sharing against captures.

## Ground truth or decision needed
What sharing modes must local DOS 3.3 honor or refuse with SHARE absent?

## Coordination
Depends on new SFT-lifetime issue; append evidence only, preserve this umbrella's title/priority/status.

Evidence comment only: existing title, priority, type and status are unchanged.

Additional Pascal code-generation review evidence, 2026-11-13. Main checked at 2ca3ee2dbd881479554249b0cfb1c35cbc725918.
Source: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-tobias-Projects-InitechOS/1260bfe2-7290-4153-8f2a-6958c19d092a/scratchpad/reports/review-turbo.md
Current source lines and retained scratch reproduction inputs/stdout/exit records were read; no builds, make targets, emulators or tests were rerun during this filing. Earlier executions remain attributed to the reviewer. Existing issue fields, priority and status are unchanged.

## Confirmed existing compatibility gap
The review's integer narrowing reproduction belongs here, not in a new bug. Both current compilers retain 32-bit arithmetic/storage: turbo/seed/codegen.c:1345 (add), :1361 (multiply), :1779-1785 (dword stores); turbo/compiler/turbo.pas:3008-3010 (32-bit arithmetic), :4404 (dword store).

## Failing program
```pascal
program probe;
var a,b: integer;
begin
  a := 32767; b := 200;
  a := a + 1; b := b * b;
  writeln(a, ' ', b)
end.
```

## Expected versus actual
| Execution | Output |
|---|---|
| FPC TP | `-32768 -25536` |
| Seed | `32768 40000` |
| Turbo | `32768 40000` |

Retained evidence: /tmp/turbo-defect-review/overflow/input.pas, reference.stdout, seed.stdout, turbo.stdout and the generated-execution logs/exit records. Inputs use FPC 3.2.2 -Mtp -B -O- -v0 for the independent reference. Seed/Turbo actuals execute x86 emitted by the C seed / FPC-hosted Pascal compiler through unchanged Multiboot startup in scratch QEMU; this is not a resident native-emitter/product-image validation.

## Red-first differential and acceptance
First show the exact generated-execution stdout comparisons red: -32768 -25536 from independent FPC TP assignment narrowing versus 32768 40000 from both product compiler paths. Add this narrowing case to semantic execution coverage in initech-h5uk7; before implementing TP-width changes, also use captured real-TP intermediate-expression expectations, because FPC TP mode widens some expressions. The independent local capture register /home/tobias/Projects/turbopascal-decomp/re/fpc-vs-tp55.md:42-47 shows real TP wrapping where FPC widens (200*200 and 300*300, i+1, shifts and abs). Do not use Delphi-mode Integer corpus headers as the TP16 reference.

## Scope qualification
The archived programmer guide currently promises 32-bit Integer and wrap at attic/pubs/manuals/turbo-initech-programmers-guide/ch03-types.tex:40-49, while this issue retains an earlier operator ruling for TP16 semantics. This filing records that conflict without deciding it, changing scope, or modifying the issue's deferred status or P4 priority. Width affects arithmetic, assignment, parameters, layouts and bootstrap capacity; a local masking patch is not a complete fix. The separately filed endpoint-loop bug is independent of the ultimate integer width.

value: AUDIT TRAP (2026-07-09): a compound Bash command that cd'd into .claude/worktrees/agent-* persisted the cwd across later tool calls -- subsequent Makefile/gate inspections silently read the STALE worktree (176+27 gates, 10758-line Makefile) instead of the repo root (296+61, 17298 lines). Always verify pwd (or use absolute paths) before trusting repo-state reads; stale worktrees shadow repo state convincingly.

Basilisk II Mac OS 8.1 mint traps (initech-kd60, 2026-08-16): (1) Mac OS Setup Assistant in Startup Items HANGS BasiliskII on first boot (100% CPU, input dead) -- trash the alias from the CD boot first; baked out of boot81.img. (2) NEVER SIGKILL BasiliskII with the HFS volume mounted: the MDB still looks perfect (sig BD, blessed dirID) but the volume no longer boots -- Special->Shut Down only; keep a pristine backup. (3) Mac surface is the CHILD window named 'Basilisk II' at root +80,+97 (metacity frame lies). (4) The screenshot Mac cursor is a stale ghost -- not evidence input is dead; test with press-and-hold. (5) Initialize dialog default button is Cancel; Cmd-A does not select-all in its Name field. (6) Boot wait 45s (desktop at ~27s). (7) OS 8.1 install is ~100s in Basilisk, not wall-clock-slow.

Bochs RFB display does NOT render VGA mode 0x13 (initech-6pj/564): even a pristine REAL-MODE fill of mode 0x13 (index 1 everywhere + DAC[1] programmed), halted before the kernel, comes back ALL BLACK over the RFB display plugin (raw framebuffer bytes 0/345600 nonzero; RFB serves the guest as 720x530 true-color 3-3-2). The OS writes the mode-0x13 framebuffer CORRECTLY -- proven 4 independent ways: (1) stage2 real-mode write/readback at 0xA0000 returns the written byte; (2) Bochs debugger write-watchpoint on 0xAF9FF fires (kernel fill reaches the high framebuffer byte); (3) host oracle test-console 8bpp 57 checks; (4) serial shows BANNER-BEGIN/text/BANNER-END through console_putc. So Bochs's RFB plugin (the only headless display in this build) cannot display chained 256-color mode 0x13 -- a Bochs RFB limitation, NOT an InitechOS bug. CONSEQUENCE: the Bochs tri-emulator gate must assert on SERIAL markers + no-triple-fault (resolution/display-independent, the rigorous Rule-5 signal), not a screendump. A visual Bochs screendump of mode 0x13 is not achievable via RFB here; mode 0x12 (640x480x16 planar) MIGHT render on RFB (untested) but needs a planar renderer. /tmp/rfb_capture.py is the (working) RFB framebuffer-capture client.

Clock-skew gotcha (env): build/ artifacts can acquire mtimes ~tens of minutes in the FUTURE relative to the system clock, which makes GNU make skip ALL rebuilds (every target looks newer than freshly-edited sources) -> false-green/false-red oracles. Symptom: 'Clock skew detected. Your build may be incomplete.' + a mutation-proof gate (e.g. test-dosmsg-mutant [B]) fails to bite because the intermediate 'make kernel_shell.bin' is a silent no-op. FIX: 'make clean' wipes the future-dated artifacts; rebuild from clean gives clock-consistent mtimes and the gates behave. Always 'make clean' before trusting an incremental oracle run if the skew warning appears.

DOSBox-X mint harness (2026-09-26, lotus123-decomp/re/harness-setup.md): never pass -silent (forces SDL dummy video -> black), never end [autoexec] with exit (segfault; use -exit), set [sdl] videodriver=x11 + [dosbox] quit warning=false, drive with xdotool XTEST (not --window/XSendEvent) after windowfocus, never windowactivate --sync without a WM. Real 1-2-3 R2.2 needs INIT (unresolved under emulation; initialized ref tree runs). WP 5.1 installs from one staged dir via Custom install.

FLAIR compositor oracle gap (jmc5/qi8v, 2026-07-07): tools/ppm_flair_appswitch_check.c graded an app-switch GREEN while the background NOTES window was fully erased to teal -- because it only probes the FOREGROUND (HELLO overlap + accent + menu band), never the BACKGROUND window's non-overlap footprint. This is the WL-0066 'grade math/foreground, not the whole composite' lesson recurring. RULE: any live-desktop pixel oracle MUST probe the region that the bug ERASES (the peer/background window's own footprint), not just the actor's. Also: desktop_paint_all did not clear wm->desktop_update, so init-seeded damage leaked into the pump and the first desktop_paint_damage painted it teal -- a full-repaint entry point must invalidate pending damage.

FLAIR/InitechOS host-build gotchas (proven WL-0064): (1) the dev host is 64-bit with NO -m32 multilib -- host test binaries are 64-bit, so (int32_t)(uintptr_t)ptr TRUNCATES; recover owners by MATCHING (int32_t)(uintptr_t)app == w->refCon (truncated-both-sides works on host-64 AND flat-32) + a magic tag, never cast refCon back to a pointer; use a full-width void* for per-instance state. (2) the FLAIR heap (heap.c) is BUMP + per-class LIFO free-list: flair_free does NOT roll back the bump cursor and flair_heap_avail returns size-used (bump tail only) -- so a teardown/leak oracle must assert 'avail STABLE across launch/exit cycles >=2 (free-list reuse), a leak drifts it monotonically DOWN', NOT 'avail returns to pre-launch' (which reds a correct impl). (3) Law-4 eyeball as an agent: build the image -> build/qemu_harness --disk IMG --screendump --screendump-after MARKER -> pnmtopng the .ppm -> Read the .png. (4) parallel coding lanes must verify via direct gcc to /tmp, never concurrent make (build/ race).

FLAIR live-GUI testing gap + the method (2026-06-28): the Phase 4.5 waves shipped on GREEN host oracles + a single boot-frame screendump, but NEVER drove the live desktop -- so 138 real bugs (2 P0, ~20 P1) escaped (operator found ~5 in 10s). The oracles 'grade math, not composited pixels or live behaviour' (initech-pipa's words). THE METHOD (was researched in initech-l9cd but unused): drive the live desktop with build/qemu_harness --disk build/flair_live.img (or flair_tenants.img) --mouse 'm<dx>:<dy>,l1,l0' --keys SPEC --keys-after FLAIR-LIVE-READY --screendump --screendump-after <MARKER> ; markers: FLAIR-LIVE-READY/FLAIR-DRAG/FLAIR-MENU/FLAIR-CLOSE (os/milton/kmain.c). Convert PPM->PNG (pnmtopng | convert -filter point -resize 200%) and Read it; sample exact RGB from build/*.ppm with python. NOTE mouse Y is INVERTED in the harness spec (rel +y -> cursor up). Bugs filed under label gui-bughunt; full report docs/FLAIR-GUI-bug-hunt-2026-06-28.md. LESSON: a structural/host oracle is necessary but NOT sufficient for a GUI -- Law 4 requires driving the live desktop + comparing composited pixels to the ../system7-decomp goldens.

FLAIR mouse IRQ12 (FO-6, commit 3835b02): the dual-PIC EOI ORDER is load-bearing -- mouse_irq_handler MUST outb(0xA0,0x20) [SLAVE] THEN outb(0x20,0x20) [MASTER]; a master-only EOI leaves the slave ISR bit set and SILENTLY WEDGES all further IRQ12 (proven by the MASTER_ONLY_EOI mutant: 0 distinct FLAIR-MOUSE). A slave IRQ also needs BOTH the master cascade (IRQ2) AND the slave IRQ12 (bit4) unmasked (pic_unmask_irq12). isr.asm uses  so irq12_entry is an inert stub in the 26 non-flair kernels (mouse.o links only into flair_live) -- keeps them byte-stable. The no-wedge property is asserted by injecting >=2 mouse events and requiring >=2 DISTINCT FLAIR-MOUSE on QEMU; flair_live can't exercise IRQ12 on Bochs (640x480 ENOMODE halts before the loop) -> Bochs strict-PIC coverage is follow-up initech-<probe-bead>.

Ground truth for Turbo Initech (M8): ../turbopascal-decomp (created 2026-10-24, bead initech-v872) holds the real Turbo Pascal 5.5 golden master (Embarcadero museum tp55.zip, sha256 a04ff655...), a dosbox-x mint harness on Xvfb :88 (tools/remint.sh), and goldens MINT00-05: IDE shots + specs/ide-geometry.md, 70 verified compiler error numbers (specs/compiler-errors.md), runtime error formats (specs/runtime-errors.md), Write/Str/Val formatting vs fpc (specs/write-formatting.md), and the initech-os corpus under real TPC (re/fpc-vs-tp55.md: TP Integer is 16-bit, round() is half-away-from-zero, Real default format differs). TP 6.0 not obtainable (GAPS G-1). Like the other decomp siblings it has NO git remote yet.

march-i386-pin-2026-08 (GUI remediation R3.1): the freestanding artifact was compiling with the HOST gcc default arch -- cmov (P6+) throughout every kernel -- violating ADR-0001's 386+ target silently; the Bochs legs run cpu model=pentium (no cmov) and only caught it when a new Bochs-exercised path (the R3.1 DESKTOP.DB bootstrap) contained one: PANIC vec=06 after FLAIR-FAT-MOUNT-OK, QEMU green. Fix: -march=i386 pinned in KERNEL_CFLAGS + SAMIR_COM_PROFILE. TWO lessons: (1) any tri-emulator disagreement = investigate the CPU-model delta FIRST (objdump | grep -E 'cmov|bswap|xadd|cmpxchg'); (2) a CFLAGS change does NOT invalidate built objects (objects prereq sources, not the Makefile) -- ALWAYS rm build/*.o or make clean after global flag edits; the stale kernel still contained cmov after the pin until the clean rebuild.

SESSION-CLOSE TRAP 2026-11-02: 'git pull --rebase' on a main that carries LOCAL MERGE COMMITS (lane merges not yet pushed) replays every merged lane commit linearly even when origin has not moved (rebase drops merge commits), and conflicts in the lane's files.
